1.165.m: The sacred utterances must be made there with their syllables in reverse order; / and the [Gāyatrī-]head must be made with syllables reversed, O lord of men.

1.165.s:
ādau śiraḥ prayoktavyaṃ praṇavānte ca yādava ..
svāhāsthāne ca phaṭkāraṃ sādhyanāmasamanvitam .. 57 ..
1.165.d:
आदौ शिरः प्रयोक्तव्यं प्रणवान्ते च यादव ॥
स्वाहास्थाने च फट्कारं साध्यनामसमन्वितम् ॥ 57 ॥
1.165.m: The head must be employed at the beginning and at the end of the praṇava, O Yādava, / and in place of 'svāhā', the syllable 'phaṭ', joined with the name of the target.

1.165.s:
gāyatrīṃ cintayettatra dīptānalasamaprabhām ..
ghātayantī ca śūlena keśeṣvākṛṣya vairiṇam .. 58 ..
1.165.d:
गायत्रीं चिन्तयेत्तत्र दीप्तानलसमप्रभाम् ॥
घातयन्ती च शूलेन केशेष्वाकृष्य वैरिणम् ॥ 58 ॥
1.165.m: There one should contemplate Gāyatrī having a radiance equal to blazing fire, / striking the enemy with a trident, having dragged him by the hair,

1.165.s:
nirdahantīṃ ca taṃ krodhādbhrukuṭībhīṣaṇānanām ..
uccāṭane ca tāṃ devīṃ vāyubhūtāṃ vicintayet .. 59 ..
1.165.d:
निर्दहन्तीं च तं क्रोधाद्भ्रुकुटीभीषणाननाम् ॥
उच्चाटने च तां देवीं वायुभूतां विचिन्तयेत् ॥ 59 ॥
1.165.m: and burning him up in rage, her face terrible with knitted brows. / And in acts of expulsion, one should contemplate that goddess as wind.

1.165.s:
vahamānāṃ tathā sādhyaṃ tasmāddeśātsudūrataḥ ..
abhicāre ca hotavyā rājikā viṣamiśritāḥ ..1.165.60 ..
1.165.d:
वहमानां तथा साध्यं तस्माद्देशात्सुदूरतः ॥
अभिचारे च होतव्या राजिका विषमिश्रिताः ॥1.165.60 ॥
1.165.m: carrying away the target far from that region. / And in destructive sorcery, mustard seeds mixed with poison should be offered into the fire,

1.165.s:
svaraktamiśraṃ hotavyaṃ kaṭutailamathāpi vā ..
tatrāpi ca viṣaṃ deyaṃ homakāle ca yatnataḥ..61 ..
1.165.d:
स्वरक्तमिश्रं होतव्यं कटुतैलमथापि वा ॥
तत्रापि च विषं देयं होमकाले च यत्नतः॥61 ॥
1.165.m: or pungent oil mixed with one's own blood should be offered into the fire; / there too poison should be carefully added at the time of oblation.

1.165.s:
madhye jahyādyadi krodhaṃ dhruvaṃ naśyetsa eva tu ..
anāgasi na kartavyamabhicāramato budhaiḥ ..
alpāgasi na kartavyamabhicāraṃ tathaiva tu .. 62 ..
1.165.d:
मध्ये जह्याद्यदि क्रोधं ध्रुवं नश्येत्स एव तु ॥
अनागसि न कर्तव्यमभिचारमतो बुधैः ॥
अल्पागसि न कर्तव्यमभिचारं तथैव तु ॥ 62 ॥
1.165.m: If he should abandon his anger midway, he himself will surely be destroyed. / Therefore, the wise should not perform destructive sorcery against one who is guiltless; / likewise, destructive sorcery should not be performed against one whose fault is small.

1.165.s:
mahāparādhaṃ balinaṃ devabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakam ..
abhicāreṇa yo hanyānna sa doṣeṇa lipyate .. 63 ..
1.165.d:
महापराधं बलिनं देवब्राह्मणकण्टकम् ॥
अभिचारेण यो हन्यान्न स दोषेण लिप्यते ॥ 63 ॥
1.165.m: One who slays by destructive sorcery a powerful man of great transgression, / a thorn to gods and brahmins, is not stained by guilt.

1.165.s:
dharmapradhāne tu nare alpāgasi tathaiva ca ..
abhicāraṃ na kurvīta bahūpāyaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 64 ..
1.165.d:
धर्मप्रधाने तु नरे अल्पागसि तथैव च ॥
अभिचारं न कुर्वीत बहूपायं विचक्षणः ॥ 64 ॥
1.165.m: Against a man who is devoted to dharma, and likewise one of small fault, / the discerning man of many expedients should not perform destructive sorcery.

1.165.s:
bahūnāṃ kaṇṭakaṃ yaṃ tu pāpātmānaṃ sudurmatim ..
hanyātprāptāparādhaṃ tu tasya puṇyaphalaṃ labhet .. 65 ..
1.165.d:
बहूनां कण्टकं यं तु पापात्मानं सुदुर्मतिम् ॥
हन्यात्प्राप्तापराधं तु तस्य पुण्यफलं लभेत् ॥ 65 ॥
1.165.m: One who slays that wicked, extremely ill-minded man / who is a thorn to many and has incurred guilt, gains the fruit of merit.

1.165.s:
ye bhaktāḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ devadevaṃ janārdanam ..
na tānabhicarejjātu tatra tadviphalaṃ bhavet .. 66 ..
1.165.d:
ये भक्ताः पुण्डरीकाक्षं देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥
न तानभिचरेज्जातु तत्र तद्विफलं भवेत् ॥ 66 ॥
1.165.m: Against those who are devoted to the lotus-eyed Janārdana, the god of gods, / one should never practice sorcery; there it would become futile.

1.165.s:
na hi keśavabhaktānāmabhicāreṇa karhicit ..
vināśamabhipadyeta tasmāttatra samācaret .. 67 ..
1.165.d:
न हि केशवभक्तानामभिचारेण कर्हिचित् ॥
विनाशमभिपद्येत तस्मात्तत्र समाचरेत् ॥ 67 ॥
1.165.m: For devotees of Keśava never suffer / destruction through sorcery; therefore, one should act properly in that regard.

1.165.s:
seyaṃ dhātrī vidhātrī ca sāvitryaghavināśinī ..
prāṇāyāmena japyeta tathaivāntarjalena ca .. 68 ..
1.165.d:
सेयं धात्री विधात्री च सावित्र्यघविनाशिनी ॥
प्राणायामेन जप्येत तथैवान्तर्जलेन च ॥ 68 ॥
1.165.m: She is the supporter and the ordainer, the Sāvitrī who destroys sins; / she should be recited with breath control, and likewise while submerged in water.

1.165.s:
savyāhṛtīkapraṇavā japtavyā śirasā saha ..
praṇavena tathā'bhyastā vācyā vyāhṛtayaḥ pṛthak .. 69 ..
1.165.d:
सव्याहृतीकप्रणवा जप्तव्या शिरसा सह ॥
प्रणवेन तथाऽभ्यस्ता वाच्या व्याहृतयः पृथक् ॥ 69 ॥
1.165.m: She should be recited with the vyāhṛtis and the praṇava, together with the head mantra; / and the vyāhṛtis, preceded by the praṇava, should be pronounced separately.

1.165.s:
daivataṃ savitā tvasyā gāyatraṃ chanda eva ca ..
viśvāmitra ṛṣiścaiva procyate vasudhādhipa .. 1.165.70 ..
1.165.d:
दैवतं सविता त्वस्या गायत्रं छन्द एव च ॥
विश्वामित्र ऋषिश्चैव प्रोच्यते वसुधाधिप ॥ 1.165.70 ॥
1.165.m: Her deity is Savitṛ, her metre is the gāyatrī, / and Viśvāmitra is proclaimed her seer, O lord of the earth.

1.165.s:
karmendriyāṇi pañcaiva pañca buddhīndriyāṇi ca ..
pañcendriyārthānmahatāṃ bhūtānāṃ caiva pañcakam .. 71 ..
1.165.d:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चैव पञ्च बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि च ॥
पञ्चेन्द्रियार्थान्महतां भूतानां चैव पञ्चकम् ॥ 71 ॥
1.165.m: The five organs of action and the five cognitive senses, / the five objects of the senses and the group of five great elements,

1.165.s:
mano buddhistathaivātmā avyaktaṃ ca yadūttama ..
caturviṃśatyathaitāni gāyatryā akṣarāṇi tu .. 72 ..
1.165.d:
मनो बुद्धिस्तथैवात्मा अव्यक्तं च यदूत्तम ॥
चतुर्विंशत्यथैतानि गायत्र्या अक्षराणि तु ॥ 72 ॥
1.165.m: mind, intellect, and the self, as well as the unmanifest, O best of Yadus— / these are the twenty-four syllables of the Gāyatrī.

1.165.s:
praṇavaṃ puruṣaṃ viddhi sarvagaṃ pañcaviṃśakam ..
saptalokāni yānīha mahāvyāhṛtayastathā .. 73 ..
1.165.d:
प्रणवं पुरुषं विद्धि सर्वगं पञ्चविंशकम् ॥
सप्तलोकानि यानीह महाव्याहृतयस्तथा ॥ 73 ॥
1.165.m: Know the praṇava to be the Cosmic Person, all-pervading, the twenty-fifth principle; / and the great vyāhṛtis are the seven worlds in this cosmos.

1.165.s:
śirasaśca tathā vācyaḥ puruṣaḥ parameśvaraḥ ..
evaṃvidhā sā sāvitrī japtavyā satataṃ budhaiḥ .. 74 ..
1.165.d:
शिरसश्च तथा वाच्यः पुरुषः परमेश्वरः ॥
एवंविधा सा सावित्री जप्तव्या सततं बुधैः ॥ 74 ॥
1.165.m: And the Cosmic Person, the supreme Lord, is to be declared the head mantra. / Such is the Sāvitrī that should be constantly recited by the wise;

1.165.s:
hotavyā ca tathā śaktyā sarvakāmasamṛddhidā ..
gāyatrīmātraśaraṇo varaṃ vipraḥ suyantritaḥ .. 75 ..
1.165.d:
होतव्या च तथा शक्त्या सर्वकामसमृद्धिदा ॥
गायत्रीमात्रशरणो वरं विप्रः सुयन्त्रितः ॥ 75 ॥
1.165.m: and she should be offered into the fire according to one's capacity, bestowing the fulfillment of all desires. / A restrained brahmin whose only refuge is the Gāyatrī is preferable

1.165.s:
nāyantritaścaturvedī sarvāśī sarvavikrayī ..
gāyatrīṃ japate yastu kalyamutthāya vai dvijaḥ .. 76 ..
1.165.d:
नायन्त्रितश्चतुर्वेदी सर्वाशी सर्वविक्रयी ॥
गायत्रीं जपते यस्तु कल्यमुत्थाय वै द्विजः ॥ 76 ॥
1.165.m: to an unrestrained master of the four Vedas who eats everything and sells everything. / A twice-born man who, having arisen at dawn, recites the Gāyatrī,

1.165.s:
lipyate na sa pāpebhyaḥ padmapatramivāmbhasā ..
kāmakāmo labhetkāmaṃ gatikāmastu sadgatim ..
akāmastadavāpnoti yadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam .. 77 ..
1.165.d:
लिप्यते न स पापेभ्यः पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
कामकामो लभेत्कामं गतिकामस्तु सद्गतिम् ॥
अकामस्तदवाप्नोति यद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ 77 ॥
1.165.m: is not stained by sins, like a lotus leaf by water. / One desiring desires obtains his desire, one desiring a state of being obtains a good state; / one devoid of desire attains that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.165.s:
evaṃ prabhāvā varadā pavitrā gāyatryathoktā tava rājasiṃha ..
japanti ye tāṃ paramaṃ prayānti sthānaṃ parasyā'pratimasya puṃsaḥ .. 78 ..
1.165.d:
एवं प्रभावा वरदा पवित्रा गायत्र्यथोक्ता तव राजसिंह ॥
जपन्ति ये तां परमं प्रयान्ति स्थानं परस्याऽप्रतिमस्य पुंसः ॥ 78 ॥
1.165.m: Thus the boon-granting, purifying Gāyatrī of such power has been described to you, O lion among kings; / those who recite her go to the supreme abode of the highest, incomparable Cosmic Person.

1.166.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
mahāvartipradānasya yatphalaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
tanmamācakṣva tattvena vidhiṃ kālaṃ tathaiva ca .. 1 ..
1.166.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
महावर्तिप्रदानस्य यत्फलं भृगुनन्दन ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन विधिं कालं तथैव च ॥ 1 ॥
1.166.m: Vajra said: / The fruit of offering a great lamp-wick, O son of Bhṛgu— / tell me that accurately, as well as the procedure and the proper time.

1.166.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
mahāvartiḥ sadā deyā bhūmipāla mahāphalā ..
kṛṣṇapakṣe viśeṣeṇa tatrāpi ca viśeṣataḥ .. 2 ..
1.166.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
महावर्तिः सदा देया भूमिपाल महाफला ॥
कृष्णपक्षे विशेषेण तत्रापि च विशेषतः ॥ 2 ॥
1.166.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A great lamp-wick bringing great fruit should always be offered, O protector of the earth, / especially during the dark fortnight, and even there most especially

1.166.s:
amāvāsyā ca nirdiṣṭā dvādaśī ca mahāphalā ..
āśvayujyāmatītāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣasya yā bhavet .. 3 ..
1.166.d:
अमावास्या च निर्दिष्टा द्वादशी च महाफला ॥
आश्वयुज्यामतीतायां कृष्णपक्षस्य या भवेत् ॥ 3 ॥
1.166.m: the new moon day is designated, and the twelfth day brings great fruit. / When the month of Āśvina has passed, the new moon day

1.166.s:
amāvasyā tadā puṇyā dvādaśī vā viśeṣataḥ ..
devasya dakṣiṇe pārśve deyā tailatulā nṛpa .. 4 ..
1.166.d:
अमावस्या तदा पुण्या द्वादशी वा विशेषतः ॥
देवस्य दक्षिणे पार्श्वे देया तैलतुला नृप ॥ 4 ॥
1.166.m: or the twelfth day of the dark fortnight that occurs then is particularly auspicious. / On the right side of the deity, O king, a balance-weight of oil should be given;

1.166.s:
palāṣṭakayutāṃ rājanvartiṃ tatra tu dāpayet ..
mahārajanaraktena samagreṇa tu vāsasā .. 5 ..
1.166.d:
पलाष्टकयुतां राजन्वर्तिं तत्र तु दापयेत् ॥
महारजनरक्तेन समग्रेण तु वाससा ॥ 5 ॥
1.166.m: a wick measuring eight palas should be placed there, O king, / made of an entire cloth dyed red with safflower.

1.166.s:
vāmapārśve ca devasya deyā ghṛtatulā nṛpa ..
palāṣṭakayutāṃ śuklāṃ vartiṃ tatra tu dāpayet .. 6 ..
1.166.d:
वामपार्श्वे च देवस्य देया घृततुला नृप ॥
पलाष्टकयुतां शुक्लां वर्तिं तत्र तु दापयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.166.m: And on the left side of the deity, O king, a balance-weight of ghee should be given; / a white wick measuring eight palas should be placed there,

1.166.s:
vāsasā tu samagreṇa sopavāso jitendriyaḥ ..
mahāvartidvayamidaṃ sakṛddattvā mahīpate .. 7 ..
1.166.d:
वाससा तु समग्रेण सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
महावर्तिद्वयमिदं सकृद्दत्त्वा महीपते ॥ 7 ॥
1.166.m: made of an entire cloth, while fasting and with senses conquered. / Having given this pair of great lamp-wicks even once, O lord of the earth,

1.166.s:
svarlokaṃ suciraṃ bhuktvā jāyate bhūtale yadā ..
tadā bhavati lakṣmīvānrūpasaubhāgyamāśritaḥ .. 8 ..
1.166.d:
स्वर्लोकं सुचिरं भुक्त्वा जायते भूतले यदा ॥
तदा भवति लक्ष्मीवान्रूपसौभाग्यमाश्रितः ॥ 8 ॥
1.166.m: having enjoyed heaven for a very long time, when he is born on the surface of the earth, / he then becomes prosperous, endowed with beauty and good fortune;

1.166.s:
rāṣṭre ca jāyate yasmindeśe ca nagare'thavā ..
kule ca rājaśārdūla tatra syāddīpavatprabhā .. 9 ..
1.166.d:
राष्ट्रे च जायते यस्मिन्देशे च नगरेऽथवा ॥
कुले च राजशार्दूल तत्र स्याद्दीपवत्प्रभा ॥ 9 ॥
1.166.m: and in whatever realm, country, city, / or family he is born, O tiger among kings, his radiance there is like a lamp.

1.166.s:
atyujjvalaśca bhavati yuddheṣu kalaheṣu ca ..
khyātiṃ yāti tathā loke sajjanānāṃ ca sadguṇaiḥ .. 1.166.10 ..
1.166.d:
अत्युज्ज्वलश्च भवति युद्धेषु कलहेषु च ॥
ख्यातिं याति तथा लोके सज्जनानां च सद्गुणैः ॥ 1.166.10 ॥
1.166.m: He becomes intensely brilliant in battles and in disputes; / he also attains renown in the world and among good people through his noble virtues.

1.166.s:
ekāmapyatha yo dadyādabhīṣṭamanayordvayoḥ ..
mānuṣye sarvamāpnoti taduktaṃ te mayā'nagha .. 11 ..
1.166.d:
एकामप्यथ यो दद्यादभीष्टमनयोर्द्वयोः ॥
मानुष्ये सर्वमाप्नोति तदुक्तं ते मयाऽनघ ॥ 11 ॥
1.166.m: Moreover, whoever should give even one of these two that is desired / obtains everything in human life; that has been told to you by me, O sinless one.

1.166.s:
svarge tathārdhamāpnoti bhāgaṃ kālaṃ ca yādava ..
sāmānyasya tu dīpasya rājandāne mahatphalam .. 12 ..
1.166.d:
स्वर्गे तथार्धमाप्नोति भागं कालं च यादव ॥
सामान्यस्य तु दीपस्य राजन्दाने महत्फलम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.166.m: Likewise in heaven he obtains half the share and the time, O Yādava. / From the gift of an ordinary lamp, O king, there is great fruit;

1.166.s:
kiṃ punarmahato yasya phalasyānto na vidyate ..
dīpadānaṃ paraṃ puṇyamanyadeveṣvapi dhruvam .. 13 ..
1.166.d:
किं पुनर्महतो यस्य फलस्यान्तो न विद्यते ॥
दीपदानं परं पुण्यमन्यदेवेष्वपि ध्रुवम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.166.m: how much more from a great one, whose fruit knows no end! / The gift of a lamp to other deities is surely supreme merit;

1.166.s:
kiṃ punardeva devasya tvanantasya mahātmanaḥ ..
giriśṛṅgeṣu dātavyā nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca .. 14 ..
1.166.d:
किं पुनर्देव देवस्य त्वनन्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
गिरिशृङ्गेषु दातव्या नदीनां पुलिनेषु च ॥ 14 ॥
1.166.m: how much more to the god of gods, the infinite, the great-souled! / Lamps should be given on mountain peaks and on sandbanks of rivers,

1.166.s:
catuṣpatheṣu rathyāsu brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛheṣu ca ..
vṛkṣamūleṣu goṣṭheṣu kāntāragahaneṣu ca .. 15 ..
1.166.d:
चतुष्पथेषु रथ्यासु ब्राह्मणानां गृहेषु च ॥
वृक्षमूलेषु गोष्ठेषु कान्तारगहनेषु च ॥ 15 ॥
1.166.m: at crossroads, on highways, and in the houses of brahmins, / at the roots of trees, in cowpens, and in thick forests.

1.166.s:
dīpadānena sarvatra mahatphalamupāśnute ..
yāvantyakṣinimeṣāṇi dīpaḥ prajvālito nṛpa .. 16 ..
1.166.d:
दीपदानेन सर्वत्र महत्फलमुपाश्नुते ॥
यावन्त्यक्षिनिमेषाणि दीपः प्रज्वालितो नृप ॥ 16 ॥
1.166.m: Through the gift of a lamp everywhere, one obtains great fruit. / For as many blinks of the eye as a lamp burns brightly, O king,

1.166.s:
tāvantyeva sa rājendra varṣāṇi divi modate ..
dīpadānena rājendra cakṣuṣmāniha jāyate .. 17 ..
1.166.d:
तावन्त्येव स राजेन्द्र वर्षाणि दिवि मोदते ॥
दीपदानेन राजेन्द्र चक्षुष्मानिह जायते ॥ 17 ॥
1.166.m: for just so many years does he rejoice in heaven, O best of kings. / Through the gift of a lamp, O best of kings, one is born here with keen sight,

1.166.s:
rūpasaubhāgyayuktāśca dhanadhānyasamanvitāḥ ..
dīpamālāṃ prayacchanti ye narāḥ śārṅgiṇo gṛhe .. 18 ..
1.166.d:
रूपसौभाग्ययुक्ताश्च धनधान्यसमन्विताः ॥
दीपमालां प्रयच्छन्ति ये नराः शार्ङ्गिणो गृहे ॥ 18 ॥
1.166.m: endowed with beauty and good fortune, and possessed of wealth and grain. / Those men who offer a row of lamps in the house of the bow-wielder,

1.166.s:
bhavanti te candrasamāḥ svargamāsādya mānavāḥ ..
dīpāgāraṃ naraḥ kṛtvā kūṭāgāranibhaṃ śubham .. 19 ..
1.166.d:
भवन्ति ते चन्द्रसमाः स्वर्गमासाद्य मानवाः ॥
दीपागारं नरः कृत्वा कूटागारनिभं शुभम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.166.m: those mortals, having reached heaven, become like the moon. / A man having made an auspicious house of lamps resembling a gabled pavilion

1.166.s:
keśavālayamāsādya nāke bhāti sa śakravat ..
yathojjvalaḥ sadā dīpo dīpadātāpi yādava .. 1.166.20 ..
1.166.d:
केशवालयमासाद्य नाके भाति स शक्रवत् ॥
यथोज्ज्वलः सदा दीपो दीपदातापि यादव ॥ 1.166.20 ॥
1.166.m: in the abode of Keśava, shines in heaven like Śakra. / Just as a lamp is always radiant, so too the giver of a lamp, O Yādava,

1.166.s:
tathā nityojjvalo loke nākabhraṣṭo'bhi jāyate ..
samīpe tu yathā loke cakṣūṃṣi phalavanti hi .. 21 ..
1.166.d:
तथा नित्योज्ज्वलो लोके नाकभ्रष्टोऽभि जायते ॥
समीपे तु यथा लोके चक्षूंषि फलवन्ति हि ॥ 21 ॥
1.166.m: falls from heaven and is born into the world always radiant. / For just as eyes are indeed fruitful when near [a lamp] in the world,

1.166.s:
tathā dīpasya dātāro bhavanti saphalekṣaṇāḥ ..
yathaivordhvagatirnityaṃ rājandīpaśikhā śubhā .. 22 ..
1.166.d:
तथा दीपस्य दातारो भवन्ति सफलेक्षणाः ॥
यथैवोर्ध्वगतिर्नित्यं राजन्दीपशिखा शुभा ॥ 22 ॥
1.166.m: so the givers of a lamp become ones whose vision is fruitful. / Just as the auspicious flame of a lamp always moves upward, O king,

1.166.s:
dīpadātustathaivordhvagatirbhavati śobhanā ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena dīpā deyā nareśvara.. 23 ..
1.166.d:
दीपदातुस्तथैवोर्ध्वगतिर्भवति शोभना ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन दीपा देया नरेश्वर॥ 23 ॥
1.166.m: so the upward journey of the giver of a lamp becomes splendid. / Therefore, with every effort, lamps should be given, O lord of men.

1.166.s:
āśvayujyāmatītāyāṃ yāvadrājendra kārtikī ..
tāvaddīpapradasyoktaṃ phalaṃ rājanviśeṣataḥ ..24..
1.166.d:
आश्वयुज्यामतीतायां यावद्राजेन्द्र कार्तिकी ॥
तावद्दीपप्रदस्योक्तं फलं राजन्विशेषतः ॥24॥
1.166.m: From the passing of the full moon of Āśvina until the full moon of Kārttika, O king of kings, / the reward for the giver of a lamp is described as especially great, O king.

1.166.s:
tāvatkālaṃ prayacchanti ye tu dīpaṃ sadā niśi ..
tuṃge deśe mahatteṣāṃ bahiḥ puṇyaphalaṃ bhavet .. ..25..
1.166.d:
तावत्कालं प्रयच्छन्ति ये तु दीपं सदा निशि ॥
तुंगे देशे महत्तेषां बहिः पुण्यफलं भवेत् ॥ ॥25॥
1.166.m: Those who constantly offer a lamp at night for that duration of time / on an elevated place outside, great shall be the fruit of their merit.

1.166.s:
yasyāndhakāre gahane prākāśyaṃ tena jāyate.
prākāśye yaduśārdūla tena yānti hi tatsukham ..26..
1.166.d:
यस्यान्धकारे गहने प्राकाश्यं तेन जायते।
प्राकाश्ये यदुशार्दूल तेन यान्ति हि तत्सुखम् ॥26॥
1.166.m: By him who causes brightness in deep darkness, / because of that brightness, O tiger among the Yadus, they attain that very joy.

1.166.s:
śravaṇe dīpakaṃ dattvā nadīdvitayasaṃgame ..
tejasvī ca yaśasvī ca rūpavānabhijāyate .. 27 ..
1.166.d:
श्रवणे दीपकं दत्त्वा नदीद्वितयसंगमे ॥
तेजस्वी च यशस्वी च रूपवानभिजायते ॥ 27 ॥
1.166.m: By giving a lamp under the constellation Śravaṇa at the confluence of two rivers, / one is born radiant, renowned, and handsome.

1.166.s:
dīpā nadīṣu dātavyāḥ kārtikyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ..
āśvayukkṛṣṇapakṣasya yā tu pañcadaśī bhavet .. 28 ..
1.166.d:
दीपा नदीषु दातव्याः कार्तिक्यां च विशेषतः ॥
आश्वयुक्कृष्णपक्षस्य या तु पञ्चदशी भवेत् ॥ 28 ॥
1.166.m: Lamps should be offered on rivers, and especially on the full moon of Kārttika; / and on what is the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight of Āśvina,

1.166.s:
bilvadvāreṣu dātavyāstathā dīpā yathāvidhi ..
anyatrāpi tadā dīpairmahatpuṇyaphalaṃ labhet .. 29 ..
1.166.d:
बिल्वद्वारेषु दातव्यास्तथा दीपा यथाविधि ॥
अन्यत्रापि तदा दीपैर्महत्पुण्यफलं लभेत् ॥ 29 ॥
1.166.m: lamps should also be offered according to rule at the entrances of bilva trees. / Elsewhere too, by means of lamps at that time, one obtains a great reward of merit.

1.166.s:
śravaṇadvādaśīyoge kṛṣṇapakṣe tathaiva ca ..
ghṛtena dīpā dātavyāstilairvā yadunandana .. 1.166.30 ..
1.166.d:
श्रवणद्वादशीयोगे कृष्णपक्षे तथैव च ॥
घृतेन दीपा दातव्यास्तिलैर्वा यदुनन्दन ॥ 1.166.30 ॥
1.166.m: Likewise, upon the conjunction of the twelfth lunar day with Śravaṇa in the dark fortnight, / lamps should be offered with ghee or with sesame [oil], O delight of the Yadus.

1.166.s:
vasāmajjādibhirdeyā na tu dīpāḥ kathañcana ..
dattvā dīpaṃ na kartavyaṃ tena karma vijānatā .. 31 ..
1.166.d:
वसामज्जादिभिर्देया न तु दीपाः कथञ्चन ॥
दत्त्वा दीपं न कर्तव्यं तेन कर्म विजानता ॥ 31 ॥
1.166.m: Lamps must never be given with fat, marrow, and the like. / Having offered a lamp, a knowing person should not use it for secular tasks.

1.166.s:
nirvāpaṇaṃ ca dīpasya hiṃsanaṃ ca vigarhitam ..
yaḥ kuryāttena karmāṇi syādasau puṣpitekṣaṇaḥ .. 32 ..
1.166.d:
निर्वापणं च दीपस्य हिंसनं च विगर्हितम् ॥
यः कुर्यात्तेन कर्माणि स्यादसौ पुष्पितेक्षणः ॥ 32 ॥
1.166.m: Extinguishing a lamp and harming it is censured; / whoever performs [other] tasks with it will have clouded vision.

1.166.s:
dīpahartā bhavedandhaḥ kāṇo nirvāpako bhavet ..
dīpadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .. 33 ..
1.166.d:
दीपहर्ता भवेदन्धः काणो निर्वापको भवेत् ॥
दीपदानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥ 33 ॥
1.166.m: A thief of a lamp will become blind; one who extinguishes it will become one-eyed. / There has been no gift higher than the gift of a lamp, nor will there ever be.

1.166.s:
dīpadānaṃ tu kartavyaṃ vipraveśmasu paṇḍitaiḥ..
dvijaveśmani yo dadyātkārtike māsi dīpakam .. 34 ..
1.166.d:
दीपदानं तु कर्तव्यं विप्रवेश्मसु पण्डितैः॥
द्विजवेश्मनि यो दद्यात्कार्तिके मासि दीपकम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.166.m: The gift of a lamp should be made by wise men in the houses of brahmins. / Whoever offers a lamp in the dwelling of a twice-born in the month of Kārttika,

1.166.s:
agniṣṭomaphalaṃ tasya pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ ..
prāṇijāṃ nīlaraktāṃ ca dīpe vartiṃ vivarjayet.. 35 ..
1.166.d:
अग्निष्टोमफलं तस्य प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥
प्राणिजां नीलरक्तां च दीपे वर्तिं विवर्जयेत्॥ 35 ॥
1.166.m: the wise declare for him the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. / One should avoid in a lamp a wick derived from animals or one that is blue or red.

1.166.s:
viśeṣeṇa pradātavyā padmasūtrabhavā nṛpa ..
padmasūtrodbhavāṃ vartiṃ gandhatailena dīpake .. 36 ..
1.166.d:
विशेषेण प्रदातव्या पद्मसूत्रभवा नृप ॥
पद्मसूत्रोद्भवां वर्तिं गन्धतैलेन दीपके ॥ 36 ॥
1.166.m: Especially, O king, a wick made from lotus fibres should be offered. / Offering in a lamp a wick made from lotus fibres with scented oil,

1.166.s:
virogaḥ subhagaścaiva dattvā bhavati mānavaḥ ..
dātavyaṃ devadevasya karpūreṇa ca dīpakam..
aśvamedhamavāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet..37..
1.166.d:
विरोगः सुभगश्चैव दत्त्वा भवति मानवः ॥
दातव्यं देवदेवस्य कर्पूरेण च दीपकम्॥
अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्॥37॥
1.166.m: a man becomes free from illness and fortunate. / A lamp made with camphor should be offered to the God of gods; / one attains [the merit of] a horse sacrifice and uplifts his family.

1.166.s:
etanmayoktaṃ tava dīpadāne phalaṃ samagraṃ yaduvaṃśacandra ..
śrutvā yathāvatsatataṃ tu deyā dīpāstvayā viprasurālayeṣu .. 38 ..
1.166.d:
एतन्मयोक्तं तव दीपदाने फलं समग्रं यदुवंशचन्द्र ॥
श्रुत्वा यथावत्सततं तु देया दीपास्त्वया विप्रसुरालयेषु ॥ 38 ॥
1.166.m: This complete fruit regarding the gift of a lamp has been spoken by me to you, O moon of the Yadu lineage; / having heard it properly, lamps should constantly be offered by you in the dwellings of brahmins and gods.

1.167.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam ..
dīpadānāllalitikā yadavāpa purā nṛpa .. 1 ..
1.167.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥
दीपदानाल्ललितिका यदवाप पुरा नृप ॥ 1 ॥
1.167.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Here they also cite this ancient story / of what Lalitikā obtained in former times through the gift of a lamp, O king.

1.167.s:
āsīccitraratho nāma vidarbheṣu mahīpatiḥ ..
tasya putraśataṃ rājño jajñe pañcadaśottaram .. 2 ..
1.167.d:
आसीच्चित्ररथो नाम विदर्भेषु महीपतिः ॥
तस्य पुत्रशतं राज्ञो जज्ञे पञ्चदशोत्तरम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.167.m: There was an earth-ruler named Citraratha among the Vidarbhas; / to that king were born one hundred and fifteen sons.

1.167.s:
ekaiva kanyā tasyāsīllalitā nāma nāmataḥ ..
sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi .. 3 ..
1.167.d:
एकैव कन्या तस्यासील्ललिता नाम नामतः ॥
सर्वलक्षणसम्पूर्णा रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि ॥ 3 ॥
1.167.m: He had only one daughter, Lalitā by name, / endowed with all auspicious marks, peerless in beauty on earth.

1.167.s:
tāṃ dadau kāśirājāya sa pitā cārudharmiṇe ..
śatāni tasya bhāryāṇāṃ trīṇyāsaṃścātra dharmiṇaḥ .. 4 ..
1.167.d:
तां ददौ काशिराजाय स पिता चारुधर्मिणे ॥
शतानि तस्य भार्याणां त्रीण्यासंश्चात्र धर्मिणः ॥ 4 ॥
1.167.m: Her father gave her to the king of Kāśi, Cārudharmin; / three hundred wives belonged to that righteous one.

1.167.s:
tāsāṃ madhye'gramahiṣī lalitāsya tadā'bhavat ..
viṣṇorāyatane tasyāḥ sahasaṃ rājasattama .. 5 ..
1.167.d:
तासां मध्येऽग्रमहिषी ललितास्य तदाऽभवत् ॥
विष्णोरायतने तस्याः सहसं राजसत्तम ॥ 5 ॥
1.167.m: Among them, Lalitā then became his chief queen. / In the temple of Viṣṇu, O best of kings,

1.167.s:
pradīpānāṃ prajvalati divārātramarindama ..
tāmisramāśvayukpakṣaṃ śuklapakṣaṃ ca kārtikāt .. 6 ..
1.167.d:
प्रदीपानां प्रज्वलति दिवारात्रमरिन्दम ॥
तामिस्रमाश्वयुक्पक्षं शुक्लपक्षं च कार्तिकात् ॥ 6 ॥
1.167.m: a thousand lamps of hers burned day and night, O subduer of foes, / from the dark fortnight of Āśvina and the bright fortnight of Kārttika.

1.167.s:
tasyāḥ prajvalitaṃ dīpamuccasthānakṛtaṃ tathā ..
tasminkāle tathā nityaṃ brāhmaṇāvasatheṣu sā ..7..
1.167.d:
तस्याः प्रज्वलितं दीपमुच्चस्थानकृतं तथा ॥
तस्मिन्काले तथा नित्यं ब्राह्मणावसथेषु सा ॥7॥
1.167.m: Her lamp blazed, set in a high place; / at that time, she was thus constantly [active] in the dwellings of brahmins;

1.167.s:
nityaṃ bhavati sāyāhne dīpapreṣaṇatatparā ..
catuṣpatheṣu rathyāsu devatāyataneṣu ca .. 8 ..
1.167.d:
नित्यं भवति सायाह्ने दीपप्रेषणतत्परा ॥
चतुष्पथेषु रथ्यासु देवतायतनेषु च ॥ 8 ॥
1.167.m: every day at twilight she was intent upon sending lamps / to crossroads, streets, and temples of the gods,

1.167.s:
caityavṛkṣeṣu goṣṭheṣu parvatānāṃ ca mūrdhasu ..
pulineṣu nadīnāṃ ca kūpamūleṣu yādava .. 9 ..
1.167.d:
चैत्यवृक्षेषु गोष्ठेषु पर्वतानां च मूर्धसु ॥
पुलिनेषु नदीनां च कूपमूलेषु यादव ॥ 9 ॥
1.167.m: to sacred trees, cowpens, and upon the peaks of mountains, / on the sandbanks of rivers, and at the foot of wells, O descendant of Yadu.

1.167.s:
tasminbhavati sākāle dīpadānaparāyaṇā ..
tāṃ sapatnyo'tha saṅgamya papracchuridamādṛtāḥ ..1.167.10..
1.167.d:
तस्मिन्भवति साकाले दीपदानपरायणा ॥
तां सपत्न्योऽथ सङ्गम्य पप्रच्छुरिदमादृताः ॥1.167.10॥
1.167.m: At that time she was devoted to the giving of lamps. / Then her co-wives gathered together and respectfully asked her this:

1.167.s:
sapatnya ūcuḥ ..
sarvāndharmānparityajya lalite tvaṃ sadaiva tu ..
viṣṇorāyatane subhrūrdīpadānaparāyaṇā.. 11 ..
1.167.d:
सपत्न्य ऊचुः ॥
सर्वान्धर्मान्परित्यज्य ललिते त्वं सदैव तु ॥
विष्णोरायतने सुभ्रूर्दीपदानपरायणा॥ 11 ॥
1.167.m: The co-wives said: / Abandoning all religious practices, O Lalitā, you are always, / O lovely-browed one, devoted to the gift of lamps in the temple of Viṣṇu.

1.167.s:
tadetatkathayāsmākaṃ lalite kautukaṃ param ..
manyāmahe tvayāvaśyaṃ dīpadānaphalaṃ śrutam .. 12 ..
1.167.d:
तदेतत्कथयास्माकं ललिते कौतुकं परम् ॥
मन्यामहे त्वयावश्यं दीपदानफलं श्रुतम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.167.m: Therefore tell us this, O Lalitā, our supreme wonder: / we think that you have surely heard the fruit of the gift of lamps.

1.167.s:
lalitikovāca ..
nāhaṃ matsariṇī bhadrā na ca rāgādidūṣitā ..
ekapatyāśrayā yātā bhavatyo mama mānadāḥ .. 13 ..
1.167.d:
ललितिकोवाच ॥
नाहं मत्सरिणी भद्रा न च रागादिदूषिता ॥
एकपत्याश्रया याता भवत्यो मम मानदाः ॥ 13 ॥
1.167.m: Lalitikā said: / I am not envious, good ladies, nor corrupted by passion and the like; / you, my respecters, have come under the protection of a single husband.

1.167.s:
apṛthagdharmacaraṇāḥ śṛṇvantu gaditaṃ mama ..
mayaitaddīpadānasya yathā vai bhujyate phalam .. 14 ..
1.167.d:
अपृथग्धर्मचरणाः शृण्वन्तु गदितं मम ॥
मयैतद्दीपदानस्य यथा वै भुज्यते फलम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.167.m: You who observe undivided dharma, listen to what is spoken by me, / how this fruit of the gift of a lamp is indeed enjoyed by me.

1.167.s:
harasya dayitā bhāryā śailarājasutā varā ..
umādevīti madreṣu devikā yā saridvarā .. ..15..
1.167.d:
हरस्य दयिता भार्या शैलराजसुता वरा ॥
उमादेवीति मद्रेषु देविका या सरिद्वरा ॥ ॥15॥
1.167.m: The beloved wife of Hara, the excellent daughter of the mountain king, / is the goddess Umā, [manifest as] the Devikā, that excellent river among the Madras,

1.167.s:
narāṇāmanukampārthaṃ brāhmaṇairavatāritā ..
tīrayorubhayostasyāḥ kṣetraṃ krośacatuṣṭayam .. 16 ..
1.167.d:
नराणामनुकम्पार्थं ब्राह्मणैरवतारिता ॥
तीरयोरुभयोस्तस्याः क्षेत्रं क्रोशचतुष्टयम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.167.m: brought down by brahmins for the sake of compassion toward men. / On both of its banks, its sacred field extends for four krośas.

1.167.s:
tasmim̐stīrthe tu pānīyaṃ sarvatīrthaprakalpitam ..
tasmiṃstīrthe mṛtā martyāḥ prāpnuvanti śubhāṃ gatim ..17..
1.167.d:
तस्मिम्̐स्तीर्थे तु पानीयं सर्वतीर्थप्रकल्पितम् ॥
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे मृता मर्त्याः प्राप्नुवन्ति शुभां गतिम् ॥17॥
1.167.m: In that sacred ford, the water has the efficacy of all holy fords; / mortals who die in that holy ford attain an auspicious destination.

1.167.s:
śrutābhilāṣitā dṛṣṭā devikā pāpanāśinī ..
tasyāṃ snātvā sakṛnmartyo gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt..18..
1.167.d:
श्रुताभिलाषिता दृष्टा देविका पापनाशिनी ॥
तस्यां स्नात्वा सकृन्मर्त्यो गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात्॥18॥
1.167.m: Heard of, longed for, or seen, the Devikā destroys sins; / having bathed in it once, a mortal attains the status of Gaṇeśa's attendant.

1.167.s:
tasyāstīrthaṃ nṛsiṃhākhyaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam..
nṛsiṃhavapuṣā snānaṃ kṛtaṃ yatra purā śubhā..19..
1.167.d:
तस्यास्तीर्थं नृसिंहाख्यं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम्॥
नृसिंहवपुषा स्नानं कृतं यत्र पुरा शुभा॥19॥
1.167.m: There is a holy ford on it named Nṛsiṃha, which destroys all impurities, / where of old, O auspicious ladies, bathing was performed in the form of Nṛsiṃha.

1.167.s:
sauvīrarājasya purā maitreyo'bhūtpurohitaḥ..
tasmim̐stīrthe tadā tena viṣṇorāyatanaṃ kṛtam .. 1.167.20 ..
1.167.d:
सौवीरराजस्य पुरा मैत्रेयोऽभूत्पुरोहितः॥
तस्मिम्̐स्तीर्थे तदा तेन विष्णोरायतनं कृतम् ॥ 1.167.20 ॥
1.167.m: In former times, Maitreya was the royal priest of the king of Sauvīra; / at that holy ford, he then made a temple of Viṣṇu.

1.167.s:
ahanyahani śuśrūṣāṃ puṣpadhūpādilepanaiḥ ..
dīpadānādibhiścaiva cakre tatra sa vai dvijaḥ ..21..
1.167.d:
अहन्यहनि शुश्रूषां पुष्पधूपादिलेपनैः ॥
दीपदानादिभिश्चैव चक्रे तत्र स वै द्विजः ॥21॥
1.167.m: Day after day, with flowers, incense, ointments, and the like, / and with the offering of lamps, that twice-born indeed performed service there.

1.167.s:
kārtike dīpakāstatra pradattāstena caikadā ..
āsīnnirvāṇabhūyiṣṭho devārcāpurato niśi .. 22 ..
1.167.d:
कार्तिके दीपकास्तत्र प्रदत्तास्तेन चैकदा ॥
आसीन्निर्वाणभूयिष्ठो देवार्चापुरतो निशि ॥ 22 ॥
1.167.m: Once in Kārttika, lamps were offered there by him; / at night, before the image of the god, [one lamp] was almost extinguished.

1.167.s:
devatāyatane cāsaṃ tathāhamapi mūṣikā..
pradīpa vartiharaṇe kṛtabuddhirvarānanā ..23..
1.167.d:
देवतायतने चासं तथाहमपि मूषिका॥
प्रदीप वर्तिहरणे कृतबुद्धिर्वरानना ॥23॥
1.167.m: And I, O fair-faced ladies, was a mouse in that temple of the deity, / my mind resolved on stealing the wick of the lamp.

1.167.s:
gṛhītā ca mayā vartirvṛṣadaṃśo rurāva ca ..
naṣṭā cāhaṃ tadā tasya mārjārasya bhayāttadā .. 24 ..
1.167.d:
गृहीता च मया वर्तिर्वृषदंशो रुराव च ॥
नष्टा चाहं तदा तस्य मार्जारस्य भयात्तदा ॥ 24 ॥
1.167.m: The wick was seized by me, and a cat cried out; / and then I fled out of fear of that cat.

1.167.s:
vartiprāntena naśyantyā dīpakaḥ prerito mayā ..
jajvāla pūrvavaddīptyā tasminnāyatane punaḥ .. 25 ..
1.167.d:
वर्तिप्रान्तेन नश्यन्त्या दीपकः प्रेरितो मया ॥
जज्वाल पूर्ववद्दीप्त्या तस्मिन्नायतने पुनः ॥ 25 ॥
1.167.m: As I fled with the end of the wick, the lamp was nudged by me; / in that temple it blazed again with brightness as before.

1.167.s:
mṛtā cāhaṃ tadā jātā vidarbharājakanyakā ..
jātismarā mahīpasya mahiṣī cārudharmiṇaḥ .. 26 ..
1.167.d:
मृता चाहं तदा जाता विदर्भराजकन्यका ॥
जातिस्मरा महीपस्य महिषी चारुधर्मिणः ॥ 26 ॥
1.167.m: And dying then, I was born as the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, / remembering past lives, the chief queen of King Cārudharmin.

1.167.s:
eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya kārtike māsi śobhanāḥ ..
dattasyāyatane viṣṇoryasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭiruttamā .. 27 ..
1.167.d:
एष प्रभावो दीपस्य कार्तिके मासि शोभनाः ॥
दत्तस्यायतने विष्णोर्यस्येयं व्युष्टिरुत्तमा ॥ 27 ॥
1.167.m: Such is the power of a lamp in the month of Kārttika, O auspicious ladies, / offered in the temple of Viṣṇu, of which this is the supreme reward.

1.167.s:
yadi vo nāsti mātsaryaṃ dīpo deyaḥ sadā śubhāḥ ..
asaṅkalpitamapyetatpreraṇaṃ yatkṛtaṃ mayā .. 28 ..
1.167.d:
यदि वो नास्ति मात्सर्यं दीपो देयः सदा शुभाः ॥
असङ्कल्पितमप्येतत्प्रेरणं यत्कृतं मया ॥ 28 ॥
1.167.m: If you have no envy, a lamp should always be given, O auspicious ladies; / even this nudging [of the wick] was done by me without intention.

1.167.s:
keśavālayadīpasya tasyedaṃ bhujyate phalam ..
etasmātkāraṇāddīpānahametānaharniśam .. 29 ..
1.167.d:
केशवालयदीपस्य तस्येदं भुज्यते फलम् ॥
एतस्मात्कारणाद्दीपानहमेतानहर्निशम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.167.m: This fruit is now enjoyed from that lamp in the abode of Keśava. / For this reason, day and night, I offer these lamps

1.167.s:
prayacchāmi harerdhāmni jñātasya ca hi yatphalam ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktāḥ sapatnyastā dīpadānaparāyaṇāḥ .. 1.167.30 ..
1.167.d:
प्रयच्छामि हरेर्धाम्नि ज्ञातस्य च हि यत्फलम् ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्ताः सपत्न्यस्ता दीपदानपरायणाः ॥ 1.167.30 ॥
1.167.m: in the dwelling of Hari; for what fruit is there when it is known? / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus addressed, those co-wives became devoted to the gift of lamps,

1.167.s:
babhūvurdevadevasya keśavasya sadā gṛhe ..
tataḥ kālena mahatā tena rājñā mahātmanā ..
viṣṇulokamanuprāptāḥ pañcatvaṃ prāpya mānada .. 31 ..
1.167.d:
बभूवुर्देवदेवस्य केशवस्य सदा गृहे ॥
ततः कालेन महता तेन राज्ञा महात्मना ॥
विष्णुलोकमनुप्राप्ताः पञ्चत्वं प्राप्य मानद ॥ 31 ॥
1.167.m: always in the house of Keśava, the god of gods. / Then after a great time, together with that high-souled king, / having met their death, O giver of honor, they reached the world of Viṣṇu.

1.167.s:
taṃ lokamāsādya nṛpeṇa sārdhaṃ sā rājaputrī kamalābharūpā ..
reme mahīpāla mudā sametā dīpapradānāccyavanādvimuktā .. 32 ..
1.167.d:
तं लोकमासाद्य नृपेण सार्धं सा राजपुत्री कमलाभरूपा ॥
रेमे महीपाल मुदा समेता दीपप्रदानाच्च्यवनाद्विमुक्ता ॥ 32 ॥
1.167.m: Having reached that world together with the king, that princess, whose beauty was like Lakṣmī's, / rejoiced with delight, O protector of the earth, freed from falling [from heaven] through the gift of lamps.

1.168.s:
vajra uvāca ..
upavāsāsamarthānāṃ hīnānāṃ draviṇena ca ..
karmaṇā kena dharmajña toṣamāyāti śaṅkaraḥ .. 1 ..
1.168.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
उपवासासमर्थानां हीनानां द्रविणेन च ॥
कर्मणा केन धर्मज्ञ तोषमायाति शङ्करः ॥ 1 ॥
1.168.m: Vajra said: / For those incapable of fasting and devoid of wealth, / by what act, O knower of dharma, does Śaṅkara attain satisfaction?

1.168.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
santi puṣpāṇyaraṇyeṣu mūlāni ca phalāni ca ..
svayaṃ grāhyāṇi rājendra yaistuṣyati janārdanaḥ .. 2 ..
1.168.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
सन्ति पुष्पाण्यरण्येषु मूलानि च फलानि च ॥
स्वयं ग्राह्याणि राजेन्द्र यैस्तुष्यति जनार्दनः ॥ 2 ॥
1.168.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There are flowers in the forests, and roots and fruits, / to be gathered by oneself, O king of kings, with which Janārdana is pleased.

1.168.s:
candraḥ sāmānyadīpo'yaṃ vibhavaiḥ kimprayojanam ..
yathālabhyena rājendra yaistuṣyati janārdanaḥ ..3..
1.168.d:
चन्द्रः सामान्यदीपोऽयं विभवैः किम्प्रयोजनम् ॥
यथालभ्येन राजेन्द्र यैस्तुष्यति जनार्दनः ॥3॥
1.168.m: The moon is a universal lamp; what need is there for riches? / With whatever is available, O king of kings, Janārdana is pleased.

1.168.s:
phalamūlāśano'raṇye kusumairmadhusūdanam ..
sampūjya satataṃ kāmānabhīṣṭānpratipadyate .. 4 ..
1.168.d:
फलमूलाशनोऽरण्ये कुसुमैर्मधुसूदनम् ॥
सम्पूज्य सततं कामानभीष्टान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 4 ॥
1.168.m: Subsisting on fruits and roots in the forest, constantly worshipping / Madhusūdana with blossoms, one obtains one's desired wishes.

1.168.s:
akāmastadavāpnoti yadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ..
araṇyeṣu naraḥ kṛtvā devadevasya cārcanam ..5..
1.168.d:
अकामस्तदवाप्नोति यद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
अरण्येषु नरः कृत्वा देवदेवस्य चार्चनम् ॥5॥
1.168.m: Free of desire, he attains that highest step of Viṣṇu. / A man having performed the worship of the god of gods in forests,

1.168.s:
atītamuddharedrājanphalena sa śataṃ nṛṇām ..
bhaviṣyāṇāṃ śataṃ caiva narāṇāṃ yadunandana .. 6 ..
1.168.d:
अतीतमुद्धरेद्राजन्फलेन स शतं नृणाम् ॥
भविष्याणां शतं चैव नराणां यदुनन्दन ॥ 6 ॥
1.168.m: O king, would rescue a hundred past men through [that] fruit, / and indeed a hundred future men, O delight of the Yadus.

1.168.s:
nagare'pi vasanyastu bhaikṣyāśī saṃśitavrataḥ ..
araṇyādāhṛtaiḥ puṣpairmūlapatraphalāṅkuraiḥ..7..
1.168.d:
नगरेऽपि वसन्यस्तु भैक्ष्याशी संशितव्रतः ॥
अरण्यादाहृतैः पुष्पैर्मूलपत्रफलाङ्कुरैः॥7॥
1.168.m: Even living in a city, one who eats begged food, steadfast in his vows, / with flowers, roots, leaves, fruits, and shoots brought from the forest,

1.168.s:
yathopapannaiḥ satatamabhyarcayati keśavam ..
sarvakāmaprado devastasya syānmadhusūdanaḥ .. 8 ..
1.168.d:
यथोपपन्नैः सततमभ्यर्चयति केशवम् ॥
सर्वकामप्रदो देवस्तस्य स्यान्मधुसूदनः ॥ 8 ॥
1.168.m: constantly worships Keśava with whatever is available, / to him the god Madhusūdana will be the granter of all desires.

1.168.s:
tasyāpyakāmakāmasya paraṃ sthānaṃ prakīrtitam ..
yatra gatvā na śocanti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padama......
svayamāhṛtya puṣpādyaibhaikṣyāśī keśavārcanam ..
kṛtaṃ yena sa rājendra vaṃśānuddharate śatam .. 1.168.10 ..
1.168.d:
तस्याप्यकामकामस्य परं स्थानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
यत्र गत्वा न शोचन्ति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम॥॥॥
स्वयमाहृत्य पुष्पाद्यैभैक्ष्याशी केशवार्चनम् ॥
कृतं येन स राजेन्द्र वंशानुद्धरते शतम् ॥ 1.168.10 ॥
1.168.m: For him too, free from desires, the supreme abode is proclaimed, / having gone where they do not grieve, that highest step of Viṣṇu. / By whom the worship of Keśava is performed with flowers and the like gathered by oneself, living on begged food, / he, O king of kings, rescues a hundred lineages:

1.168.s:
vaṃśānatītānpañcāśattāvataścāpyanāgatān ..
uddharedātmano rājannātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 11 ..
1.168.d:
वंशानतीतान्पञ्चाशत्तावतश्चाप्यनागतान् ॥
उद्धरेदात्मनो राजन्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 11 ॥
1.168.m: he would rescue fifty past lineages and as many future lineages / of his own, O king; there should be no doubt about this.

1.168.s:
(gṛhastho'pi naro rājandharmāgatadhanāgamaḥ ..
araṇyādāhṛtaiḥ puṣpairyaḥ kuryātkeśavārcanam .. 12..
1.168.d:
(गृहस्थोऽपि नरो राजन्धर्मागतधनागमः ॥
अरण्यादाहृतैः पुष्पैर्यः कुर्यात्केशवार्चनम् ॥ 12॥
1.168.m: (Even a householder, O king, whose acquisition of wealth has come through dharma, / who would perform worship of Keśava with flowers brought from the forest,

1.168.s:
etadeva samāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
dharmārjitadhanaḥ krītvā yaḥ kurvankeśavārcanam .. 13 .. )
1.168.d:
एतदेव समाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
धर्मार्जितधनः क्रीत्वा यः कुर्वन्केशवार्चनम् ॥ 13 ॥ )
1.168.m: attains this very [fruit]; there should be no doubt about this. / One whose wealth is acquired through dharma, who buys [them] while performing worship of Keśava,

1.168.s:
svayamuptaiśca kusumairyaḥ kuryātkeśavārcanam ..
uddhariṣyatyasandehaṃ saptapūrvāparānnarān .. 14 ..
1.168.d:
स्वयमुप्तैश्च कुसुमैर्यः कुर्यात्केशवार्चनम् ॥
उद्धरिष्यत्यसन्देहं सप्तपूर्वापरान्नरान् ॥ 14 ॥
1.168.m: or one who would perform worship of Keśava with blossoms sown by oneself, / will without doubt rescue seven preceding and succeeding men.

1.168.s:
yathākathañcidāhṛtya kathañcitpūjayeddharim ..
nākapṛṣṭhamavāpnoti na me'trāsti vicāraṇā .. 15 ..
1.168.d:
यथाकथञ्चिदाहृत्य कथञ्चित्पूजयेद्धरिम् ॥
नाकपृष्ठमवाप्नोति न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा ॥ 15 ॥
1.168.m: Having procured [them] in whatever way, if one somehow worships Hari, / he attains the vault of heaven; I have no doubt about this.

1.168.s:
mānuṣye ca parāṃ rājañchriyamāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
vanādāhatya kusumaiḥ kartavyaṃ devatārcanam .. 16 ..
1.168.d:
मानुष्ये च परां राजञ्छ्रियमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
वनादाहत्य कुसुमैः कर्तव्यं देवतार्चनम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.168.m: And in human birth, O king, he undoubtedly attains supreme prosperity. / Gathering blossoms from the forest, one should perform worship of the deity.

1.168.s:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ dūrvāṅkuramathāpi vā ..
nivedayitvā kṛṣṇāya bhoktā nākamavāpnuyāta ..
akṣamaistūpavāsānāṃ tathā dhanavivarjitaiḥ .. 17 ..
1.168.d:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं दूर्वाङ्कुरमथापि वा ॥
निवेदयित्वा कृष्णाय भोक्ता नाकमवाप्नुयात ॥
अक्षमैस्तूपवासानां तथा धनविवर्जितैः ॥ 17 ॥
1.168.m: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, or even a blade of dūrvā grass— / having offered it to Kṛṣṇa, the enjoyer would attain heaven. / But by those incapable of fasts, and likewise destitute of wealth,

1.168.s:
vanādāhṛtya kusumaiḥ kartavyaṃ devatārcanam ..
araṇyādāhṛtaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sampūjya madhusūdanam ..18..
1.168.d:
वनादाहृत्य कुसुमैः कर्तव्यं देवतार्चनम् ॥
अरण्यादाहृतैः पुष्पैः सम्पूज्य मधुसूदनम् ॥18॥
1.168.m: having brought blossoms from the forest, worship of the deity should be performed. / Having worshipped Madhusūdana with flowers brought from the forest,

1.168.s:
pūrvajanmani samprāptaṃ rājyaṃ śṛṇu narādhipa ..
nṛgo yayātirnahuṣo viṣvagaśvaḥ karandhamaḥ .. 19 ..
1.168.d:
पूर्वजन्मनि सम्प्राप्तं राज्यं शृणु नराधिप ॥
नृगो ययातिर्नहुषो विष्वगश्वः करन्धमः ॥ 19 ॥
1.168.m: kingdom was obtained in a previous birth; hear [of them], O ruler of men: / Nṛga, Yayāti, Nahuṣa, Viṣvagaśva, Karandhama,

1.168.s:
dilīpo yavanāśvaśca ṛtuparṇo bhagīrathaḥ ..
somakaḥ sahadevaśca mahāmālo mahāhanuḥ ..1.168.20..
1.168.d:
दिलीपो यवनाश्वश्च ऋतुपर्णो भगीरथः ॥
सोमकः सहदेवश्च महामालो महाहनुः ॥1.168.20॥
1.168.m: Dilīpa, Yavanāśva, Ṛtuparṇa, Bhagīratha, / Somaka, Sahadeva, Mahāmāla, Mahāhanu,

1.168.s:
revakaḥ kālakākhyaśca kṛtavīryo guṇākaraḥ ..
devarātaḥ kakutsthaśca vinīto vikrame raghuḥ .. 21 ..
1.168.d:
रेवकः कालकाख्यश्च कृतवीर्यो गुणाकरः ॥
देवरातः ककुत्स्थश्च विनीतो विक्रमे रघुः ॥ 21 ॥
1.168.m: Revaka, Kālakākhya, Kṛtavīrya, Guṇākara, / Devarāta, Kakutstha, and Raghu, modest in valor,

1.168.s:
mahotsāho vītabhayo niramitraḥ prabhākaraḥ ..
kapotaromā parjanyaścandrasenaḥ parāntakaḥ .. 22 ..
1.168.d:
महोत्साहो वीतभयो निरमित्रः प्रभाकरः ॥
कपोतरोमा पर्जन्यश्चन्द्रसेनः परान्तकः ॥ 22 ॥
1.168.m: Mahotsāha, Vītabhaya, Niramitra, Prabhākara, / Kapotaromā, Parjanya, Candrasena, Parāntaka,

1.168.s:
bhīmaseno dṛḍharathaḥ kuśanābhaḥ prabhadrakaḥ ..
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ pūrvajanmani keśavam .. 23 ..
1.168.d:
भीमसेनो दृढरथः कुशनाभः प्रभद्रकः ॥
एते चान्ये च बहवः पूर्वजन्मनि केशवम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.168.m: Bhīmasena, Dṛḍharatha, Kuśanābha, and Prabhadraka— / these and many others, having worshipped Keśava in a previous birth,

1.168.s:
pūjayitvā kṣitāvasyāṃ prāpū rājyamakaṇṭakam ..
yakṣatvamatha devatvaṃ gandharvatvaṃ tathaiva ca .. 24 ..
1.168.d:
पूजयित्वा क्षितावस्यां प्रापू राज्यमकण्टकम् ॥
यक्षत्वमथ देवत्वं गन्धर्वत्वं तथैव च ॥ 24 ॥
1.168.m: obtained on this earth an unobstructed kingdom. / The state of a yakṣa, or the state of a god, and likewise the state of a gandharva,

1.168.s:
vidyādharatvaṃ nāgatvaṃ ye gatā manujottama ..
bahutvātte kathaṃ śakyā mayā vaktuṃ tavānagha .. 25 ..
1.168.d:
विद्याधरत्वं नागत्वं ये गता मनुजोत्तम ॥
बहुत्वात्ते कथं शक्या मया वक्तुं तवानघ ॥ 25 ॥
1.168.m: the state of a vidyādhara, the state of a nāga—those who reached them, O best of men, / because of their multitude, how can they be told by me to you, O sinless one?

1.168.s: tasmādyatnaḥ sadā kāryaḥ puruṣaiḥ kusumārcane ..26..
1.168.d: तस्माद्यत्नः सदा कार्यः पुरुषैः कुसुमार्चने ॥26॥
1.168.m: Therefore, effort should always be made by men in worshipping with blossoms.

1.168.s:
araṇyajātaiḥ kusumaiḥ sadaiva saṃpūjayitvā svayamāhṛtaistu ..
sarveśvaratvaṃ phalamāpnuvanti rājendra tadvarṇayituṃ na śakyam .. 27 ..
1.168.d:
अरण्यजातैः कुसुमैः सदैव संपूजयित्वा स्वयमाहृतैस्तु ॥
सर्वेश्वरत्वं फलमाप्नुवन्ति राजेन्द्र तद्वर्णयितुं न शक्यम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.168.m: Having constantly worshipped with blossoms born in the forest and gathered by oneself, / they obtain the fruit of sovereign lordship over all, O king of kings; it cannot be described.

1.169.s:
vajra uvāca ..
aṭavyo dāruṇā brahmansiṃhavyāghraniṣevitāḥ ..
taskarācaritā ghorāḥ sarīsṛpavimiśritāḥ .. 1 ..
1.169.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
अटव्यो दारुणा ब्रह्मन्सिंहव्याघ्रनिषेविताः ॥
तस्कराचरिता घोराः सरीसृपविमिश्रिताः ॥ 1 ॥
1.169.m: Vajra said: / The forests are terrible, O brahmin, frequented by lions and tigers, / traversed by thieves, frightful, and filled with crawling beasts;

1.169.s:
nityotthitasya cādhvānaṃ dāhakṣayakaraṃ param ..
ataḥ svalpataraṃ karma brūhi me keśavārcane .. 2 ..
1.169.d:
नित्योत्थितस्य चाध्वानं दाहक्षयकरं परम् ॥
अतः स्वल्पतरं कर्म ब्रूहि मे केशवार्चने ॥ 2 ॥
1.169.m: and for one constantly set out, travel brings extreme exhaustion and decay. / Therefore, tell me of an even lesser work in the worship of Keśava.

1.169.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ svalpataraṃ rājandevaveśmānulepanam ..
mahāphalaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ .. 3 ..
1.169.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः स्वल्पतरं राजन्देववेश्मानुलेपनम् ॥
महाफलं विनिर्दिष्टं ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः ॥ 3 ॥
1.169.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / An even lesser [work] than this, O king, is the smearing of the deity's temple; / it is declared as having great fruit by brahmins who have mastered the Vedas.

1.169.s:
sammārjanaṃ tu yaḥ kuryātpuruṣaḥ keśavālaye ..
rajastamobhyāṃ nirmuktaḥ sa bhavennātra saṃśayaḥ .. 4 ..
1.169.d:
सम्मार्जनं तु यः कुर्यात्पुरुषः केशवालये ॥
रजस्तमोभ्यां निर्मुक्तः स भवेन्नात्र संशयः ॥ 4 ॥
1.169.m: The man who would perform sweeping in the temple of Keśava / becomes freed from passion and darkness; there is no doubt about this.

1.169.s:
pāṃsūnāṃ yāvatāṃ rājankuryātsammārjanaṃ naraḥ ..
tāvantyabdāni sa sukhī nākamāsādya modate ..5 ..
1.169.d:
पांसूनां यावतां राजन्कुर्यात्सम्मार्जनं नरः ॥
तावन्त्यब्दानि स सुखी नाकमासाद्य मोदते ॥5 ॥
1.169.m: As many particles of dust as a man sweeps away, O king, / for that many years, happy, having reached heaven, he rejoices.

1.169.s:
abhyukṣaṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryātpānīyena surālaye..
sa śāntapāpo bhavati nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..6..
1.169.d:
अभ्युक्षणं तु यः कुर्यात्पानीयेन सुरालये॥
स शान्तपापो भवति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥6॥
1.169.m: One who performs sprinkling with water in the temple of the god / has his sins stilled; there should be no doubt about this.

1.169.s:
kṛtvopalepanaṃ viṣṇornarastvāyatane sadā ..
gomayena śubhām̐llokānayatnādeva gacchati .. 7 ..
1.169.d:
कृत्वोपलेपनं विष्णोर्नरस्त्वायतने सदा ॥
गोमयेन शुभाम्̐ल्लोकानयत्नादेव गच्छति ॥ 7 ॥
1.169.m: Having always performed the smearing of Viṣṇu's temple / with cow dung, a man goes to auspicious worlds without any effort.

1.169.s:
hastapramāṇaṃ bhūbhāgamupalipya narādhipa ..
devarāmāśataṃ nākaṃ labheta satataṃ naraḥ .. 8 ..
1.169.d:
हस्तप्रमाणं भूभागमुपलिप्य नराधिप ॥
देवरामाशतं नाकं लभेत सततं नरः ॥ 8 ॥
1.169.m: Having smeared a plot of ground measuring a cubit, O ruler of men, / a man would continually obtain heaven with a hundred divine maidens.

1.169.s:
tato'nusāreṇa phalaṃ vistṛtāyāṃ kṣitau smṛtam ..
nityāsamarthastu tathā devaveśmopalepane .. 9 ..
1.169.d:
ततोऽनुसारेण फलं विस्तृतायां क्षितौ स्मृतम् ॥
नित्यासमर्थस्तु तथा देववेश्मोपलेपने ॥ 9 ॥
1.169.m: In accordance with that, the fruit on an expanded ground is recorded. / But one incapable of daily [action] in smearing the temple of the god

1.169.s:
triḥ pakṣasya tu kurvīta devaveśmopalepanam ..
pañcamīṃ daśamīṃ caiva tathā pañcadaśīṃ nṛpa .. 1.169.10 ..
1.169.d:
त्रिः पक्षस्य तु कुर्वीत देववेश्मोपलेपनम् ॥
पञ्चमीं दशमीं चैव तथा पञ्चदशीं नृप ॥ 1.169.10 ॥
1.169.m: should perform the smearing of the deity's temple three times in a fortnight: / on the fifth, the tenth, and the fifteenth [lunar day], O king.

1.169.s:
triḥ pakṣasya sadā kṛtvā devaveśmopalepanam ..
saṃvatsarāttadāpnoti yatphalaṃ tannibodha me ..11 ..
1.169.d:
त्रिः पक्षस्य सदा कृत्वा देववेश्मोपलेपनम् ॥
संवत्सरात्तदाप्नोति यत्फलं तन्निबोध मे ॥11 ॥
1.169.m: Hear from me the fruit which one obtains after a year, / having constantly smeared the temple of the god three times a fortnight.

1.169.s:
janmāntaramathāsādya gṛhaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam ..
sarvopabhogasaṃyuktaṃ gṛhaprāsādasaṅkulam ..12..
1.169.d:
जन्मान्तरमथासाद्य गृहं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
सर्वोपभोगसंयुक्तं गृहप्रासादसङ्कुलम् ॥12॥
1.169.m: Attaining another birth, he gains an unsurpassed house, / endowed with every enjoyment, crowded with chambers and mansions,

1.169.s:
vṛkṣodyānalatāgulmatoyavāpīvibhūṣitam ..
gavāśvadhanadhānyāḍhyaṃ sarvopakaraṇairyutam .. 13 ..
1.169.d:
वृक्षोद्यानलतागुल्मतोयवापीविभूषितम् ॥
गवाश्वधनधान्याढ्यं सर्वोपकरणैर्युतम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.169.m: adorned with trees, gardens, creepers, shrubs, and water-reservoirs, / rich in cattle, horses, wealth, and grain, equipped with every implement,

1.169.s:
priyaṃvadābhirhṛdyābhiḥ svarūpābhiśca pārthiva ..
vṛtaṃ ca bahubhiḥ strībhiścāruvaṃśābhireva ca .. 14 ..
1.169.d:
प्रियंवदाभिर्हृद्याभिः स्वरूपाभिश्च पार्थिव ॥
वृतं च बहुभिः स्त्रीभिश्चारुवंशाभिरेव च ॥ 14 ॥
1.169.m: and surrounded by many women of charming lineage, O king, / sweet-spoken, delightful, and beautiful.

1.169.s:
gārhasthyaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ tatra sa cāpnoti mahītale ..
na ca pracyavanaṃ tasmājjīvannāpnoti karhicit .. 15 ..
1.169.d:
गार्हस्थ्यं च दृढं तत्र स चाप्नोति महीतले ॥
न च प्रच्यवनं तस्माज्जीवन्नाप्नोति कर्हिचित् ॥ 15 ॥
1.169.m: And there on the earth he attains a steadfast householder's life, / and while alive he never suffers a fall from it.

1.169.s:
tasya ye bāndhavāstatra sarve te dīrghajīvinaḥ ..
bhavanti na bhavantyasya ādhayo vyādhayastathā ..16..
1.169.d:
तस्य ये बान्धवास्तत्र सर्वे ते दीर्घजीविनः ॥
भवन्ति न भवन्त्यस्य आधयो व्याधयस्तथा ॥16॥
1.169.m: All his kinsmen there become long-lived; / mental anxieties and bodily diseases do not come to him.

1.169.s:
na tasya mṛtaniṣkrāntirgṛhe bhavati karhicit..
yāvajjīvatyasau tatra gṛhe śrīmānmudā yutaḥ .. 17 ..
1.169.d:
न तस्य मृतनिष्क्रान्तिर्गृहे भवति कर्हिचित्॥
यावज्जीवत्यसौ तत्र गृहे श्रीमान्मुदा युतः ॥ 17 ॥
1.169.m: A corpse is never carried out of his house / as long as he lives there, prosperous and full of joy.

1.169.s:
caurajaṃ na bhayaṃ tasya na ca vyādhikṛtaṃ bhayam ..
vyālabhūpālajaṃ vāpi na ca tasya phalaṃ bhavet .. 18 ..
1.169.d:
चौरजं न भयं तस्य न च व्याधिकृतं भयम् ॥
व्यालभूपालजं वापि न च तस्य फलं भवेत् ॥ 18 ॥
1.169.m: He has no fear arising from thieves, nor fear caused by disease, / nor fear arising from snakes or kings, nor does that bear fruit against him.

1.169.s:
svarūpaḥ sarvasiddhārtho dīrghāyurvyādhivarjitaḥ ..
ājñāvidheyabhṛtyaśca dhruvaṃ syānmanujeśvara .. 19 ..
1.169.d:
स्वरूपः सर्वसिद्धार्थो दीर्घायुर्व्याधिवर्जितः ॥
आज्ञाविधेयभृत्यश्च ध्रुवं स्यान्मनुजेश्वर ॥ 19 ॥
1.169.m: He is handsome, has accomplished all his aims, is long-lived, free from disease, / and has servants obedient to his command, O lord of men.

1.169.s:
bhuñjāno yaḥ sadā kuryāttasyaitatkathitaṃ phalam ..
naktabhojī tathā kṛtvā dviguṇaṃ phalamāpnuyāt .. 1.169.20 ..
1.169.d:
भुञ्जानो यः सदा कुर्यात्तस्यैतत्कथितं फलम् ॥
नक्तभोजी तथा कृत्वा द्विगुणं फलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 1.169.20 ॥
1.169.m: This fruit is proclaimed for him who, while eating [normally], always performs it; / eating only at night, having done so, he would obtain twice that fruit.

1.169.s:
upoṣitastu riktāsu pūrṇāsu tu harergṛhe ..
kṛtvopalepanaṃ nityaṃ cānantyaṃ phalamaśnute .. 21 ..
1.169.d:
उपोषितस्तु रिक्तासु पूर्णासु तु हरेर्गृहे ॥
कृत्वोपलेपनं नित्यं चानन्त्यं फलमश्नुते ॥ 21 ॥
1.169.m: Fasting on empty lunar days and on full ones, having continually performed / smearing in the house of Hari, he enjoys endless fruit.

1.169.s:
upalepanakṛdyastu kṛṣṇasyāyatane bhavet ..
pāpasaṃmārjanaṃ tasya śīghrameva bhaviṣyati .. 22 ..
1.169.d:
उपलेपनकृद्यस्तु कृष्णस्यायतने भवेत् ॥
पापसंमार्जनं तस्य शीघ्रमेव भविष्यति ॥ 22 ॥
1.169.m: One who performs the smearing in the abode of Kṛṣṇa / will quickly have his sins wiped away.

1.169.s:
niṣpādyametatsasukhaṃ narendra ārādhanaṃ devavarasya viṣṇoḥ ..
proktaṃ mayā te dhanavarjitānāṃ dhanānvitānāṃ saphalaṃ viśeṣam .. 23 ..
1.169.d:
निष्पाद्यमेतत्ससुखं नरेन्द्र आराधनं देववरस्य विष्णोः ॥
प्रोक्तं मया ते धनवर्जितानां धनान्वितानां सफलं विशेषम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.169.m: This worship of Viṣṇu, the best of gods, is to be performed with ease, O king; / it has been proclaimed by me to you for those devoid of wealth, and especially fruitful for those endowed with wealth.

1.170.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam ..
phalamāsādya yadgītaṃ devaveśmopalepane .. 1 ..
1.170.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥
फलमासाद्य यद्गीतं देववेश्मोपलेपने ॥ 1 ॥
1.170.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Here too they cite this ancient narrative / which was sung upon obtaining the fruit of smearing the house of the god.

1.170.s:
babhūva śūdrajātīyaḥ kaścidbhāgyavivarjitaḥ ..
kṛtavānsa tu vāṇijyaṃ dhanaśeṣeṇa kenacit .. 2 ..
1.170.d:
बभूव शूद्रजातीयः कश्चिद्भाग्यविवर्जितः ॥
कृतवान्स तु वाणिज्यं धनशेषेण केनचित् ॥ 2 ॥
1.170.m: There was a certain man of the śūdra caste, devoid of fortune; / he engaged in trade with the remainder of some wealth.

1.170.s:
tasminvipanne sa kṛṣiṃ cakāra nṛpasattama ..
tasyāmapi vipannāyāṃ cakre sevāṃ punaḥpunaḥ .. 3 ..
1.170.d:
तस्मिन्विपन्ने स कृषिं चकार नृपसत्तम ॥
तस्यामपि विपन्नायां चक्रे सेवां पुनःपुनः ॥ 3 ॥
1.170.m: When that failed, he undertook agriculture, O best of kings; / when that too failed, he repeatedly performed service.

1.170.s:
tato'pyanāsādya phalaṃ siddhiṃ tīramupāśritaḥ ..
gaṅgāyāḥ saptamo bhāgaḥ sindhurnaranarottama .. 4 ..
1.170.d:
ततोऽप्यनासाद्य फलं सिद्धिं तीरमुपाश्रितः ॥
गङ्गायाः सप्तमो भागः सिन्धुर्नरनरोत्तम ॥ 4 ॥
1.170.m: Failing to obtain success or fruit even from that, he resorted to the bank / of the Sindhu, the seventh part of the Gaṅgā, O best of men,

1.170.s:
śītalāmalapānīyaḥ svargalokapradāyakaḥ ..
yatra snātvā gatiṃ yānti brāhmaṇāśca tapasvinaḥ ..5..
1.170.d:
शीतलामलपानीयः स्वर्गलोकप्रदायकः ॥
यत्र स्नात्वा गतिं यान्ति ब्राह्मणाश्च तपस्विनः ॥5॥
1.170.m: having cool and pure water, bestowing the heavenly world, / where, having bathed, brahmins and ascetics go to their goal.

1.170.s:
tasya tīre varāhārcā purāṇarṣivinirmitā ..
tāṃ samāsādya śūdrastu nityaṃ bhaikṣyaparāyaṇaḥ .. 6 ..
1.170.d:
तस्य तीरे वराहार्चा पुराणर्षिविनिर्मिता ॥
तां समासाद्य शूद्रस्तु नित्यं भैक्ष्यपरायणः ॥ 6 ॥
1.170.m: On its bank was an image of Varāha fashioned by an ancient sage; / reaching it, the śūdra, constantly devoted to begging for alms,

1.170.s:
nityopalepanaparastadarcādevaveśmani ..
uvāsa bhāryayā sārdhaṃ tatra nityānuraktayā .. 7 ..
1.170.d:
नित्योपलेपनपरस्तदर्चादेववेश्मनि ॥
उवास भार्यया सार्धं तत्र नित्यानुरक्तया ॥ 7 ॥
1.170.m: constantly intent on smearing [the ground] in the divine temple of that image, / lived there together with his wife, who was constantly devoted to him.

1.170.s:
etasminneva kāle tu varāhārcādidṛkṣayā ..
sauvīrarājaḥ samprāptastaṃ deśaṃ citravāhanaḥ .. 8 ..
1.170.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु वराहार्चादिदृक्षया ॥
सौवीरराजः सम्प्राप्तस्तं देशं चित्रवाहनः ॥ 8 ॥
1.170.m: At that very time, wishing to see the image of Varāha, / Citravāhana, the king of Sauvīra, arrived in that region.

1.170.s:
sindhau snānaṃ samāsādya pūjayitvā jagatpatim ..
sabhāryaḥ pṛthivīpālaḥ prāyādrājanyathāgataḥ .. 9 ..
1.170.d:
सिन्धौ स्नानं समासाद्य पूजयित्वा जगत्पतिम् ॥
सभार्यः पृथिवीपालः प्रायाद्राजन्यथागतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.170.m: Having bathed in the Sindhu and worshipped the Lord of the world, / the ruler of the earth, accompanied by his wife, departed as he had come, O king.

1.170.s:
śriyaṃ tasya tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa śūdro bhāryayā saha ..
bhūpālatvaspṛhāṃ kṛtvā kālātkālavaśaṅgataḥ .. 1.170.10 ..
1.170.d:
श्रियं तस्य तु तां दृष्ट्वा स शूद्रो भार्यया सह ॥
भूपालत्वस्पृहां कृत्वा कालात्कालवशङ्गतः ॥ 1.170.10 ॥
1.170.m: Seeing his splendour, that śūdra, together with his wife, / conceived a desire for kingship, and in the course of time fell subject to Time.

1.170.s:
vanātkāṣṭhānyupāhatya kṛtvā bhartustataścitim ..
anvāruroha taṃ bhāryā śūdraṃ pañcatvamāgatam .. 11 ..
1.170.d:
वनात्काष्ठान्युपाहत्य कृत्वा भर्तुस्ततश्चितिम् ॥
अन्वारुरोह तं भार्या शूद्रं पञ्चत्वमागतम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.170.m: Bringing wood from the forest and then making a pyre for her husband, / the wife ascended [the pyre] after that śūdra who had met his demise.

1.170.s:
sa śūdro bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nākapṛṣṭhamito gataḥ ..
satataṃ dharmaśīlastu devaveśmopalepanāt .. 12 ..
1.170.d:
स शूद्रो भार्यया सार्धं नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः ॥
सततं धर्मशीलस्तु देववेश्मोपलेपनात् ॥ 12 ॥
1.170.m: That śūdra, together with his wife, went from here to the vault of heaven, / being constantly of righteous conduct because of smearing the house of the god.

1.170.s:
etasminneva kāle tu yuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ ..
viṣṇuṃ sampūjayāmāsa putrīyeṇa vratena tu .. 13 ..
1.170.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु युवनाश्वो महीपतिः ॥
विष्णुं सम्पूजयामास पुत्रीयेण व्रतेन तु ॥ 13 ॥
1.170.m: At that very time, King Yuvanāśva / worshipped Viṣṇu with a vow to obtain a son.

1.170.s:
rājñastasya vratasyānte svapne prāha janārdanaḥ ..
bhārgavaṃ cyavanaṃ gaccha tataḥ putramavāpsyasi .. 14 ..
1.170.d:
राज्ञस्तस्य व्रतस्यान्ते स्वप्ने प्राह जनार्दनः ॥
भार्गवं च्यवनं गच्छ ततः पुत्रमवाप्स्यसि ॥ 14 ॥
1.170.m: At the conclusion of the vow, Janārdana said to that king in a dream: / 'Go to Cyavana, the descendant of Bhṛgu; from him you will obtain a son.'

1.170.s:
yuvanāśvastathoktastu svapne devena cakriṇā ..
prātaḥ padbhyāṃ yayau tasya cyavanasyāśramaṃ śubham .. 15 ..
1.170.d:
युवनाश्वस्तथोक्तस्तु स्वप्ने देवेन चक्रिणा ॥
प्रातः पद्भ्यां ययौ तस्य च्यवनस्याश्रमं शुभम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.170.m: Yuvanāśva, thus addressed in a dream by the discus-bearing god, / went on foot in the morning to the auspicious hermitage of that Cyavana.

1.170.s:
sampūjayitvā cyavanaṃ cyavanena ca pūjitaḥ ..
vratasvapnāvubhau tasya jagāda nṛpasattamaḥ .. 16 ..
1.170.d:
सम्पूजयित्वा च्यवनं च्यवनेन च पूजितः ॥
व्रतस्वप्नावुभौ तस्य जगाद नृपसत्तमः ॥ 16 ॥
1.170.m: Having worshipped Cyavana and being honoured by Cyavana, / the best of kings related to him both the vow and the dream.

1.170.s:
ṛṣisaṅghānupādāya cyavano'pi mahātapāḥ ..
avijñātaṃ narendreṇa putrīyaṃ kṛtavāñjalam .. 17 ..
1.170.d:
ऋषिसङ्घानुपादाय च्यवनोऽपि महातपाः ॥
अविज्ञातं नरेन्द्रेण पुत्रीयं कृतवाञ्जलम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.170.m: Cyavana too, of great austerities, having gathered hosts of sages, / prepared water that produces a son, unbeknownst to the ruler of men.

1.170.s:
kalaśasthaṃ jalaṃ tacca sthāpayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ ..
tato niśīthe saṃprāpte tṛṣārtaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ .. 18 ..
1.170.d:
कलशस्थं जलं तच्च स्थापयामास भार्गवः ॥
ततो निशीथे संप्राप्ते तृषार्तः स महीपतिः ॥ 18 ॥
1.170.m: And the descendant of Bhṛgu placed that water in a pot; / then, when midnight arrived, that ruler of the earth, afflicted with thirst,

1.170.s:
ṛṣimadhye tu sa suptānṛṣīnvākyamathā'bravīt ..
tṛṣārto'smi bhṛśaṃ viprāḥ pānīyaṃ me prayacchata ..19 ..
1.170.d:
ऋषिमध्ये तु स सुप्तानृषीन्वाक्यमथाऽब्रवीत् ॥
तृषार्तोऽस्मि भृशं विप्राः पानीयं मे प्रयच्छत ॥19 ॥
1.170.m: spoke these words to the sages who were asleep among the sages: / 'I am exceedingly afflicted with thirst, O brahmins! Give me water!'

1.170.s:
ṛṣistasya na śuśrāva kaścidbhāvyarthacoditaḥ ..
tataḥ khinno mahīpālaḥ kalaśasthaṃ jalaṃ papau .. 1.170.20 ..
1.170.d:
ऋषिस्तस्य न शुश्राव कश्चिद्भाव्यर्थचोदितः ॥
ततः खिन्नो महीपालः कलशस्थं जलं पपौ ॥ 1.170.20 ॥
1.170.m: Impelled by destiny, not one sage heard him; / then, distressed, the ruler of the earth drank the water in the pot.

1.170.s:
pītvā suṣvāpa ṛṣayaḥ prātaḥ sarve samutthitāḥ ..
apaśyamānāḥ kalaśaṃ papracchuste para sparam .. 21 ..
1.170.d:
पीत्वा सुष्वाप ऋषयः प्रातः सर्वे समुत्थिताः ॥
अपश्यमानाः कलशं पप्रच्छुस्ते पर स्परम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.170.m: Having drunk, he slept; in the morning, all the sages arose; / not seeing the pot, they asked one another:

1.170.s:
putrīyaṃ kalaśaṃ rājñaḥ kṛtaṃ yattadgataṃ kva nu ..
tadovāca sa rājendrastānṛṣīnsaṃśitavratān .. 22 ..
1.170.d:
पुत्रीयं कलशं राज्ञः कृतं यत्तद्गतं क्व नु ॥
तदोवाच स राजेन्द्रस्तानृषीन्संशितव्रतान् ॥ 22 ॥
1.170.m: 'Where has the pot prepared for the king to obtain a son gone?' / Then that best of kings said to those sages of strict vows:

1.170.s:
tṛṣārtena mayā pītaḥ kalaśastvapavāhitaḥ ..
te hocustaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ bhāvyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ tvayā .. 23 ..
1.170.d:
तृषार्तेन मया पीतः कलशस्त्वपवाहितः ॥
ते होचुस्तं नृपश्रेष्ठं भाव्यं कर्म कृतं त्वया ॥ 23 ॥
1.170.m: 'Afflicted with thirst, I drank [it] and removed the pot.' / And they said to that best of kings: 'You have done an act that was fated.'

1.170.s:
bhāryā pītvaiva tattoyaṃ putraṃ te janayiṣyati ..
ityevaṃ mantrakalaśaḥ so'smābhirbhūpate kṛtaḥ .. 24 ..
1.170.d:
भार्या पीत्वैव तत्तोयं पुत्रं ते जनयिष्यति ॥
इत्येवं मन्त्रकलशः सोऽस्माभिर्भूपते कृतः ॥ 24 ॥
1.170.m: 'Having drunk that water, your wife would give birth to a son'— / thus that consecrated pot of water was prepared by us, O king.

1.170.s:
putrīyamudakaṃ tacca tvayā pītamabuddhinā ..
tasmāttvameva tanayaṃ svakukṣau janayiṣyasi .. 25 ..
1.170.d:
पुत्रीयमुदकं तच्च त्वया पीतमबुद्धिना ॥
तस्मात्त्वमेव तनयं स्वकुक्षौ जनयिष्यसि ॥ 25 ॥
1.170.m: And that water that produces a son was drunk by you without thought; / therefore, you yourself will give birth to a son in your own belly.

1.170.s:
nāvāpsyasi tathā mṛtyuṃ varadānāddvijanmanām ..
evamuktastu sampūjya brāhmaṇānsvagṛhaṅgataḥ .. 26 ..
1.170.d:
नावाप्स्यसि तथा मृत्युं वरदानाद्द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
एवमुक्तस्तु सम्पूज्य ब्राह्मणान्स्वगृहङ्गतः ॥ 26 ॥
1.170.m: And you will not meet death, due to the granting of a boon by the twice-born.' / Thus addressed, having worshipped the brahmins, he went to his own home.

1.170.s:
rājñaḥ kukṣiṃ vinirbhidya jajñe bālārkasannibhaḥ ..
punaḥ putravatāṃ śreṣṭha śūdro'sau nākavicyutaḥ .. 27 ..
1.170.d:
राज्ञः कुक्षिं विनिर्भिद्य जज्ञे बालार्कसन्निभः ॥
पुनः पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठ शूद्रोऽसौ नाकविच्युतः ॥ 27 ॥
1.170.m: Bursting open the belly of the king, that śūdra, fallen from heaven, / was born, resembling the rising sun, O best of those who have sons.

1.170.s:
jātamātrasya tasyendro dadau prādeśinīṃ mukhe ..
āsādya yāṃ sa bālatvaṃ śiśustatyāja tatkṣaṇāt .. 28 .....
1.170.d:
जातमात्रस्य तस्येन्द्रो ददौ प्रादेशिनीं मुखे ॥
आसाद्य यां स बालत्वं शिशुस्तत्याज तत्क्षणात् ॥ 28 ॥॥।
1.170.m: As soon as he was born, Indra placed his forefinger in his mouth; / reaching it, the infant abandoned infancy that very moment.

1.170.s:
kukṣiṃ pasparśa rājñastu rājasiṃhaśatakratuḥ ..
rājā śakrakarāmṛṣṭo vijvaraścāvraṇo'bhavat .. 29 ..
1.170.d:
कुक्षिं पस्पर्श राज्ञस्तु राजसिंहशतक्रतुः ॥
राजा शक्रकरामृष्टो विज्वरश्चाव्रणोऽभवत् ॥ 29 ॥
1.170.m: Śatakratu, a lion among kings, touched the belly of the king; / touched by the hand of Śakra, the king became free from fever and unblemished.

1.170.s:
yuvanāśvaḥ sa tasyāpi nāma cakre śatakratuḥ ...
māṃ dhāsyatīti māndhātā khyātiṃ tribhuvane gataḥ ..1.170.30 ..
1.170.d:
युवनाश्वः स तस्यापि नाम चक्रे शतक्रतुः ॥।
मां धास्यतीति मान्धाता ख्यातिं त्रिभुवने गतः ॥1.170.30 ॥
1.170.m: And Śatakratu gave that son of Yuvanāśva a name: / thinking 'he will suckle me' (māṃ dhāsyati), he became known as Māndhātṛ throughout the three worlds.

1.170.s:
tamāviveśa bhagavāṃstejasā svena mādhavaḥ ..
sāpi svargacyutā bhāryā tasya śūdrasya yādava .. 31 ..
1.170.d:
तमाविवेश भगवांस्तेजसा स्वेन माधवः ॥
सापि स्वर्गच्युता भार्या तस्य शूद्रस्य यादव ॥ 31 ॥
1.170.m: The blessed Mādhava entered him with his own splendor. / And that fallen-from-heaven wife of that śūdra, O descendant of Yadu,

1.170.s:
kāśirājasutā jātā bhīmavegasya mānada ..
nāmnā prabhāvatī subhrūstryailokyasyaikasundarī .. 32 ..
1.170.d:
काशिराजसुता जाता भीमवेगस्य मानद ॥
नाम्ना प्रभावती सुभ्रूस्त्र्यैलोक्यस्यैकसुन्दरी ॥ 32 ॥
1.170.m: was born as the daughter of the king of Kāśi, Bhīmavega, O granter of honor, / named Prabhāvatī, fair-browed, the singular beauty of the three worlds.

1.170.s:
yuvanāśvastu tāṃ vavre māndhāturlakṣaṇānvitām ..
sa rājā pradadau tāṃ tu māndhātuścitravāhanaḥ .. 33 ..
1.170.d:
युवनाश्वस्तु तां वव्रे मान्धातुर्लक्षणान्विताम् ॥
स राजा प्रददौ तां तु मान्धातुश्चित्रवाहनः ॥ 33 ॥
1.170.m: Yuvanāśva chose her, endowed with auspicious marks, for Māndhātṛ; / and that king, Citravāhana, gave her to Māndhātṛ.

1.170.s:
ekaiva bhāryā sā tasya babhūvātyantasundarī ..
rūpayauvanasampannā prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī ..
kṛtvodvāhamayodhyāyāmabhiṣicya sa taṃ nṛpam .. 34 ..
1.170.d:
एकैव भार्या सा तस्य बभूवात्यन्तसुन्दरी ॥
रूपयौवनसम्पन्ना प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी ॥
कृत्वोद्वाहमयोध्यायामभिषिच्य स तं नृपम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.170.m: She was his only wife, exceedingly beautiful, / endowed with beauty and youth, dearer to him than his own breaths. / Having performed the wedding in Ayodhyā and consecrated that king,

1.170.s:
yuvanāśvo vanaṃ prāyādvanādapi triviṣṭapam ..
rājyastho'pi sa māndhātā trailokyaṃ saptabhirdinaiḥ .. 35 ..
1.170.d:
युवनाश्वो वनं प्रायाद्वनादपि त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
राज्यस्थोऽपि स मान्धाता त्रैलोक्यं सप्तभिर्दिनैः ॥ 35 ॥
1.170.m: Yuvanāśva departed to the forest, and from the forest to heaven. / Established in his kingdom, that Māndhātṛ, within seven days,

1.170.s:
rathenaikena vaśagaṃ cakāra khaḍgadarpitaḥ ..
pātāle gagane śaile samudre ca mahātmanaḥ .. 36 ..
1.170.d:
रथेनैकेन वशगं चकार खड्गदर्पितः ॥
पाताले गगने शैले समुद्रे च महात्मनः ॥ 36 ॥
1.170.m: brought the three worlds under his control with a single chariot, proud of his sword. / In the underworld, in the sky, on mountains, and in the ocean,

1.170.s:
āsīttasyāpratihatā gatiścakrasya pārthiva ..
cakravartī sa dharmātmā vaiṣṇavaśca tathā'bhavat .. 37 ..
1.170.d:
आसीत्तस्याप्रतिहता गतिश्चक्रस्य पार्थिव ॥
चक्रवर्ती स धर्मात्मा वैष्णवश्च तथाऽभवत् ॥ 37 ॥
1.170.m: the progress of that great-souled one's chariot was unobstructed, O king. / He became a righteous universal monarch and a Vaiṣṇava.

1.170.s:
samāyutānāṃ bubhuje sa rājyaṃ daśa mānada ..
brahmāṇḍamaṇḍapaṃ yāvatsūryastapati raśmibhiḥ ..
tāvatkṣetraṃ mahībharturyuvanāśvasya kīrtyate .. 38 ..
1.170.d:
समायुतानां बुभुजे स राज्यं दश मानद ॥
ब्रह्माण्डमण्डपं यावत्सूर्यस्तपति रश्मिभिः ॥
तावत्क्षेत्रं महीभर्तुर्युवनाश्वस्य कीर्त्यते ॥ 38 ॥
1.170.m: He enjoyed the kingdom for ten myriad years, O granter of honor. / As far as the sun warms the pavilion of the universe with its rays, / that whole territory is renowned as belonging to Yuvanāśva's son, the lord of the earth.

1.170.s:
evaṃ sa rājā vijitāripakṣo devājirālepanakṛdbabhūva ...
bhāryā ca sā tasya babhūva bhāryā loke variṣṭhā pramadāvarābhyaḥ .. 39 ..
1.170.d:
एवं स राजा विजितारिपक्षो देवाजिरालेपनकृद्बभूव ॥।
भार्या च सा तस्य बभूव भार्या लोके वरिष्ठा प्रमदावराभ्यः ॥ 39 ॥
1.170.m: Thus that king, having conquered his adversaries, smeared the courtyards of the gods [with his offerings]; / and that wife of his was the foremost wife in the world among excellent women.

1.171.s:
1.171
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
sa tu rājā mayā brahmanmāṃdhātā bhuvaneśvaraḥ ..
māheśvareṇa śūlena lavaṇena hataḥ śrutaḥ .. 1 ..
1.171.d:
1.171
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥ ॥
स तु राजा मया ब्रह्मन्मांधाता भुवनेश्वरः ॥
माहेश्वरेण शूलेन लवणेन हतः श्रुतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.171.m:
1.171
Vajra said: / But that king Māndhātṛ, the lord of the world, O brahmin, / has been heard by me to have been slain by Lavaṇa with the trident of Maheśvara.

1.171.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ajeyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tejastatra nityaṃ ca jantuṣu ..
nāśamāyānti te sarve hīnā vaiṣṇava tejasā ..2 ..
1.171.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अजेयं वैष्णवं तेजस्तत्र नित्यं च जन्तुषु ॥
नाशमायान्ति ते सर्वे हीना वैष्णव तेजसा ॥2 ॥
1.171.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The splendor of Viṣṇu is unconquerable and eternal among living beings there; / all of them go to destruction when deprived of the splendor of Viṣṇu.

1.171.s:
avināśi jagatyasminna kiñcidatha vidyate ..
ṛte tu mahatastasmāttejaso nṛpa vaiṣṇavāt .. 3 ..
1.171.d:
अविनाशि जगत्यस्मिन्न किञ्चिदथ विद्यते ॥
ऋते तु महतस्तस्मात्तेजसो नृप वैष्णवात् ॥ 3 ॥
1.171.m: Nothing whatsoever in this world is imperishable, / except indeed for that great splendor of Viṣṇu, O king.

1.171.s:
tejastasya sudurvāhyaṃ dehibhirnapa sarvadā ..
tasmāttena vihīnāste kṣayaṃ gacchanti mānada .. 4 ..
1.171.d:
तेजस्तस्य सुदुर्वाह्यं देहिभिर्नप सर्वदा ॥
तस्मात्तेन विहीनास्ते क्षयं गच्छन्ति मानद ॥ 4 ॥
1.171.m: His splendor is always exceedingly difficult to bear for embodied beings, O king; / therefore, abandoned by it, they go to ruin, O granter of honor.

1.171.s:
matsyaḥ kūrmo varāhaśca narasiṃho'tha vāmanaḥ ..
brahmā śambhustathaivārkaścandramāśca śatakratuḥ .. 5 ..
1.171.d:
मत्स्यः कूर्मो वराहश्च नरसिंहोऽथ वामनः ॥
ब्रह्मा शम्भुस्तथैवार्कश्चन्द्रमाश्च शतक्रतुः ॥ 5 ॥
1.171.m: The Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Narasiṃha, and the Dwarf, / Brahmā, Śambhu, as well as the Sun, the Moon, and Śatakratu—

1.171.s:
evamādyāstathaivānye yuktā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
gajacchāyānumānena viyujyante ca tejasā .. 6 ..
1.171.d:
एवमाद्यास्तथैवान्ये युक्ता वैष्णवतेजसा ॥
गजच्छायानुमानेन वियुज्यन्ते च तेजसा ॥ 6 ॥
1.171.m: these and other [beings] endowed with the splendor of Viṣṇu / are separated from that splendor according to the measure of an elephant's shadow.

1.171.s:
vitejasaśca te sarve pañcatvamupayānti ca ..
pañcabhūtātmakaṃ sthūlaṃ yatkiñcijjagatīgatam .. 7 ..
1.171.d:
वितेजसश्च ते सर्वे पञ्चत्वमुपयान्ति च ॥
पञ्चभूतात्मकं स्थूलं यत्किञ्चिज्जगतीगतम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.171.m: And bereft of that splendor, all of them meet dissolution. / Whatever gross thing exists in the world, composed of the five elements,

1.171.s:
sarvaṃ vināśi tajjñeyaṃ tvayā pārthivasattama ..
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena viśvamidaṃ tatam .. 8 ..
1.171.d:
सर्वं विनाशि तज्ज्ञेयं त्वया पार्थिवसत्तम ॥
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन विश्वमिदं ततम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.171.m: you must understand all of that to be perishable, O best of kings. / But know that to be imperishable by which this entire universe is pervaded:

1.171.s:
yattu gandhaguṇairhīnaṃ rūpasparśavivarjitam ..
śabdahīnaṃ ca virasaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvagaṃ ca yat .. 9 ..
1.171.d:
यत्तु गन्धगुणैर्हीनं रूपस्पर्शविवर्जितम् ॥
शब्दहीनं च विरसं सर्वेशं सर्वगं च यत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.171.m: that which is devoid of the quality of smell, devoid of form and touch, / free of sound, devoid of taste, the ruler of all, and omnipresent;

1.171.s:
nirguṇaṃ tadguṇātītamantikasthaṃ ca dūragam ..
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam .. 1.171.10 ..
1.171.d:
निर्गुणं तद्गुणातीतमन्तिकस्थं च दूरगम् ॥
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ॥ 1.171.10 ॥
1.171.m: quality-less, beyond qualities, situated near and far away, / appearing through the qualities of all senses, yet devoid of all senses;

1.171.s:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukham ..
sarvendriyaguṇaṃ devaṃ sarvataḥ parameśvaram ..11..
1.171.d:
सर्वतः पाणिपादान्तं सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ॥
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणं देवं सर्वतः परमेश्वरम् ॥11॥
1.171.m: having hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, / the god possessing the qualities of all senses, the supreme lord everywhere.

1.171.s:
avināśi tadevaikaṃ yasyodaragataṃ jagat ..
sadāśiveti taṃ kecidāhurdevaṃ jagatpatim ..12..
1.171.d:
अविनाशि तदेवैकं यस्योदरगतं जगत् ॥
सदाशिवेति तं केचिदाहुर्देवं जगत्पतिम् ॥12॥
1.171.m: That alone is imperishable, in whose belly rests the universe. / Some call that god, the lord of the universe, Sadāśiva;

1.171.s:
vāsudeveti cāpyanye kālamityeva cāpare..
devamityapare taṃ ca svabhāvamiti cāpare .. 13 ..
1.171.d:
वासुदेवेति चाप्यन्ये कालमित्येव चापरे॥
देवमित्यपरे तं च स्वभावमिति चापरे ॥ 13 ॥
1.171.m: and others call him Vāsudeva, while others call him Time; / others call him God, and others call him Nature;

1.171.s:
karmeti cāpare prāhuḥ puruṣeti tathā pare ..
praṇavākhyaṃ tathā taṃ ca vidurvedavido janāḥ .. 14 ..
1.171.d:
कर्मेति चापरे प्राहुः पुरुषेति तथा परे ॥
प्रणवाख्यं तथा तं च विदुर्वेदविदो जनाः ॥ 14 ॥
1.171.m: others call him Action, and others likewise call him the Cosmic Person; / and people who know the Vedas know him by the name of Praṇava.

1.171.s:
tadekamajamavyaktamavināśaṃ narādhipa ..
ṛte tamekamīśānamaṃtavatsakalaṃ jagat .. 15 ..
1.171.d:
तदेकमजमव्यक्तमविनाशं नराधिप ॥
ऋते तमेकमीशानमंतवत्सकलं जगत् ॥ 15 ॥
1.171.m: That alone is unborn, unmanifest, and imperishable, O ruler of men; / except for that single ruler, the entire universe has an end.

1.171.s:
etattavoktaṃ bhuvanasya patyurmayā svarūpaṃ yaduvaṃśacandra ..
bhaktiṃ vinā buddhimatāpi yasya śakyaṃ na vaktuṃ grahaṇaṃ nareṇa .. 16 ..
1.172
.. vajra uvāca ..
prādurbhāvā varāhādyāḥ sarveśasyāmitātmanaḥ ..
mahābhūtacayāḥ sarve janmamṛtyuyutāśca ye .. 1 ..
yadyevaṃ prāṇibhisteṣāṃ ko viśeṣo bhṛgūttama ..
etattvaṃ saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 2 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sarve jīvā mahīpāla karmabandhanibandhanāḥ ..
jāyante ca mriyante ca paratantrāḥ sadaiva ca .. 3 ..
īśvarapreritairnityaṃ karmabandhaiḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ ..
janmāntarakṛtairbhūpa sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ .. 4 ..
vāsudevastu dharmātmā prādurbhāveṣu yādava ..
ātmanaḥ svecchayā janma vidhatte maraṇaṃ tathā .. 5 ..
karmāṇi na ca limpanti prādurbhāveṣvapi prabhum ..
karmasvapi sadā saktaṃ padmapatramivāmbhasā .. 6 ..
1.171.d:
एतत्तवोक्तं भुवनस्य पत्युर्मया स्वरूपं यदुवंशचन्द्र ॥
भक्तिं विना बुद्धिमतापि यस्य शक्यं न वक्तुं ग्रहणं नरेण ॥ 16 ॥
1.172
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
प्रादुर्भावा वराहाद्याः सर्वेशस्यामितात्मनः ॥
महाभूतचयाः सर्वे जन्ममृत्युयुताश्च ये ॥ 1 ॥
यद्येवं प्राणिभिस्तेषां को विशेषो भृगूत्तम ॥
एतत्त्वं संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥ 2 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सर्वे जीवा महीपाल कर्मबन्धनिबन्धनाः ॥
जायन्ते च म्रियन्ते च परतन्त्राः सदैव च ॥ 3 ॥
ईश्वरप्रेरितैर्नित्यं कर्मबन्धैः शुभाशुभैः ॥
जन्मान्तरकृतैर्भूप सुखदुःखसमन्विताः ॥ 4 ॥
वासुदेवस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रादुर्भावेषु यादव ॥
आत्मनः स्वेच्छया जन्म विधत्ते मरणं तथा ॥ 5 ॥
कर्माणि न च लिम्पन्ति प्रादुर्भावेष्वपि प्रभुम् ॥
कर्मस्वपि सदा सक्तं पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ 6 ॥
1.171.m:
Thus the true nature of the lord of the world has been told to you by me, O moon of the Yadu dynasty, / the comprehension of which cannot be expressed by man, even if intelligent, without devotion.
1.172
Vajra said: / The manifestations beginning with the Boar belonging to the ruler of all, the boundless soul, / and all the aggregates of elements are accompanied by birth and death.
If so, what is their difference from ordinary living beings, O foremost of the Bhṛgus? / Dispel this doubt of mine, for great indeed is my curiosity.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / All individual souls, O ruler of earth, are tied by the bonds of karma; / they are born and they die, always dependent on others,
constantly driven by the Lord through auspicious and inauspicious bonds of karma / performed in other births, O king, accompanied by happiness and sorrow.
Vāsudeva, however, the righteous soul, in his manifestations, O descendant of Yadu, / ordains his own birth and death by his own will.
And actions do not cling to the Lord even in his manifestations, / even while always engaged in actions, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.

1.171.s:
phalānāṃ karmajātānāṃ bhogaṃ tatrāpi yādava ..
nṛṇāṃ darśayate mithyā maryādābhedabhīrnṛpa .. 7 ..
yadāyadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati yādava ..
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjatyasau .. 8 ..
devatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu gandharvoragapakṣiṣu ..
yoniṣvanyeṣvapi tathā buddhvā kāryabalābalam .. 9 ..
yasyāṃ yasyāṃ yadā yonau prādurbhavati kāraṇāt ..
tadyonisadṛśaṃ tatsa tadā loke viceṣṭate .. 1.172.10 ..
saṃhartuṃ jagadīśānaḥ samartho'pi tadā nṛpa ..
tadyonisadṛśopāyairvadhyānhiṃsati yādava .. 11 ..
hārdaṃ tamastathā naiśaṃ mūrtaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ ..
eka eva sa lokānāṃ nāśayatyamaladyutiḥ .. 12 ..
hārdaṃ dhvastaṃ tamastena jagato devamūrtinā ..
jyotīrūpeṇa ca dhvastaṃ tamo naiśaṃ sudāruṇam .. 13 ..
tamo nāśayituṃ mūrtaṃ prādurbhāvagataḥ sadā ..
mūrtaṃ tamaśca rājendra daityadānavarākṣasāḥ .. 14 ..
1.171.d:
फलानां कर्मजातानां भोगं तत्रापि यादव ॥
नृणां दर्शयते मिथ्या मर्यादाभेदभीर्नृप ॥ 7 ॥
यदायदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति यादव ॥
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजत्यसौ ॥ 8 ॥
देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्येषु गन्धर्वोरगपक्षिषु ॥
योनिष्वन्येष्वपि तथा बुद्ध्वा कार्यबलाबलम् ॥ 9 ॥
यस्यां यस्यां यदा योनौ प्रादुर्भवति कारणात् ॥
तद्योनिसदृशं तत्स तदा लोके विचेष्टते ॥ 1.172.10 ॥
संहर्तुं जगदीशानः समर्थोऽपि तदा नृप ॥
तद्योनिसदृशोपायैर्वध्यान्हिंसति यादव ॥ 11 ॥
हार्दं तमस्तथा नैशं मूर्तं च पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
एक एव स लोकानां नाशयत्यमलद्युतिः ॥ 12 ॥
हार्दं ध्वस्तं तमस्तेन जगतो देवमूर्तिना ॥
ज्योतीरूपेण च ध्वस्तं तमो नैशं सुदारुणम् ॥ 13 ॥
तमो नाशयितुं मूर्तं प्रादुर्भावगतः सदा ॥
मूर्तं तमश्च राजेन्द्र दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः ॥ 14 ॥
1.171.m:
Even there, O descendant of Yadu, fearing the rupture of righteous order, / he falsely displays to men the experience of the fruits born of karma, O king.
For whenever there is a decline of dharma, O descendant of Yadu, / and an uprising of adharma, then he projects himself.
Among gods, animals, and humans, among gandharvas, serpents, and birds, / and in other wombs as well, having considered the relative weight of the task,
in whatever womb he manifests on any occasion due to a specific cause, / he acts in the world in a manner appropriate to that womb.
Though capable of destroying [all at once], the ruler of the universe then, O king, / destroys those who deserve to be slain through means appropriate to that womb, O descendant of Yadu.
The darkness of the heart, the darkness of night, and embodied darkness— / Puruṣottama, of spotless splendor, destroys all three for the worlds entirely alone.
The darkness of the heart of the world was dispelled by him in the form of a deity; / and the terrible darkness of night was dispelled by him in the form of light.
To destroy embodied darkness, he continually assumes manifestations; / and embodied darkness, O king of kings, consists of daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas.

1.171.s:
vandhyānāmapi daityānāṃ dehastho'pi janārdanaḥ ..
na vimuñcati dehāni yuktyā tāṃśca jighāṃsati .. 15 ..
daivatānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca dvijānāṃ ca gurupriyaḥ ..
śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā bhavatyārādhane rataḥ .. 16 ..
1.171.d:
वन्ध्यानामपि दैत्यानां देहस्थोऽपि जनार्दनः ॥
न विमुञ्चति देहानि युक्त्या तांश्च जिघांसति ॥ 15 ॥
दैवतानां गुरूणां च द्विजानां च गुरुप्रियः ॥
शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना भवत्याराधने रतः ॥ 16 ॥
1.171.m:
Even when dwelling in the bodies of demons who cannot be slain,
Janārdana does not abandon their bodies, and by skilful means he seeks to slay them.
Affectionate toward elders, he is devoted to the worship
of gods, elders, and twice-born men according to the rule set forth in scripture.

1.171.s:
na ca tasyāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana ..
naivānāptamavāptavyaṃ vartate'tha ca karmasu .. 17 ..
1.171.d:
न च तस्यास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ॥
नैवानाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्ततेऽथ च कर्मसु ॥ 17 ॥
1.171.m:
There is nothing for him to do in the three worlds,
nor is there anything unattained to be attained, yet he engages in actions.

1.171.s:
sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca sarvaśaktirapi prabhuḥ ..
tathāpyadhīte yajate tapastapyati pārthiva .. 18 ..
1.171.d:
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च सर्वशक्तिरपि प्रभुः ॥
तथाप्यधीते यजते तपस्तप्यति पार्थिव ॥ 18 ॥
1.171.m:
Though all-knowing, all-seeing, all-powerful, and sovereign,
he nevertheless studies, offers sacrifices, and performs austerities, O king.

1.171.s:
maryādāsthāpanārthāya jagato hitakāmyayā ..
karoti rājankarmāṇi kīnāśa iva durbalaḥ .. 19 ..
1.171.d:
मर्यादास्थापनार्थाय जगतो हितकाम्यया ॥
करोति राजन्कर्माणि कीनाश इव दुर्बलः ॥ 19 ॥
1.171.m:
For the sake of establishing limits, out of a desire for the welfare of the world,
he performs actions, O king, like a feeble laborer.

1.171.s:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ ..
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanu vartate .. 1.172.20 ..
1.171.d:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ॥
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनु वर्तते ॥ 1.172.20 ॥
1.171.m:
Whatever an exemplary person does, other people do as well;
whatever standard he sets, the world follows after it.

1.171.s:
etatkāraṇamāsthāya sadā karmasu vartate ..
prādurbhāvakṛto viṣṇuryathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā .. 21 ..
1.171.d:
एतत्कारणमास्थाय सदा कर्मसु वर्तते ॥
प्रादुर्भावकृतो विष्णुर्यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.171.m:
Taking recourse to this reason, Viṣṇu manifested [as an incarnation]
always engages in actions, like any ordinary person.

1.171.s:
devebhyaśca ṛṣibhyaśca varānprārthayate sadā ..
varāṃśca varadasteṣāṃ mānayatyapi pāṇḍava .. 22 ..
1.171.d:
देवेभ्यश्च ऋषिभ्यश्च वरान्प्रार्थयते सदा ॥
वरांश्च वरदस्तेषां मानयत्यपि पाण्डव ॥ 22 ॥
1.171.m:
He always requests boons from the gods and the ṛṣis;
and though he is the grantor of boons, he honors their boons, O descendant of Pāṇḍu.

1.171.s:
prādurbhāvaratastasmātparo'yamiti mānavāḥ ..
puruṣaṃ nādhigacchanti mohitāstasya māyayā .. 23 ..
1.171.d:
प्रादुर्भावरतस्तस्मात्परोऽयमिति मानवाः ॥
पुरुषं नाधिगच्छन्ति मोहितास्तस्य मायया ॥ 23 ॥
1.171.m:
Deluded by his māyā, human beings do not recognize the supreme Person,
[thinking,] 'He is merely engaged in an incarnation.'

1.171.s:
prādurbhāvaṃ gato'pyevaṃ saṃhatya sa carācaram ..
nimeṣāntaramāttreṇa śaktimāñjagataḥ prabhuḥ ..24 ..
1.171.d:
प्रादुर्भावं गतोऽप्येवं संहत्य स चराचरम् ॥
निमेषान्तरमात्त्रेण शक्तिमाञ्जगतः प्रभुः ॥24 ॥
1.171.m:
Even when he has entered upon an incarnation, having drawn together all moving and unmoving beings,
that capable sovereign of the world [can dissolve them] in the mere span of a blink.

1.171.s:
