prādurbhāvagatasyāpi tasya sarvagatā smṛtā ..
svatantratā ca sarvatra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 25 ..
1.171.d:
प्रादुर्भावगतस्यापि तस्य सर्वगता स्मृता ॥
स्वतन्त्रता च सर्वत्र नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 25 ॥
1.171.m:
Even when he has assumed an incarnation, his omnipresence is remembered,
as is his absolute autonomy everywhere; in this matter no doubt is to be entertained.

1.171.s:
mahadviśeṣametatte prāṇibhiḥ prāṇināṃ pateḥ ..
mayoktaṃ tasya devasya sarvagasya svayambhuvaḥ .. 26 ..
1.171.d:
महद्विशेषमेतत्ते प्राणिभिः प्राणिनां पतेः ॥
मयोक्तं तस्य देवस्य सर्वगस्य स्वयम्भुवः ॥ 26 ॥
1.171.m:
This great distinction of the Lord of living beings from living beings
has been explained to you by me, regarding that self-existent, omnipresent deity.

1.171.s:
ākṣiptāḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyaiḥ kaiścidyaduvarottama ..
teṣāmāviśate devastejasā tena sarvaśaḥ .. 27 ..
1.171.d:
आक्षिप्ताः कर्मभिः पुण्यैः कैश्चिद्यदुवरोत्तम ॥
तेषामाविशते देवस्तेजसा तेन सर्वशः ॥ 27 ॥
1.171.m:
Impelled by some meritorious deeds, O best of the Yadus,
the god enters into them entirely by means of that power.

1.171.s:
āviṣṭāstejasā tena devena parameṣṭhinā ..
tadvatkarmāṇi kurvanti pūjyamānā maharṣibhiḥ .. 28 ..
1.171.d:
आविष्टास्तेजसा तेन देवेन परमेष्ठिना ॥
तद्वत्कर्माणि कुर्वन्ति पूज्यमाना महर्षिभिः ॥ 28 ॥
1.171.m:
Possessed by that power by the god Parameṣṭhin,
they perform deeds in that manner, honored by great ṛṣis.

1.171.s:
tathā tu kāle saṃnyastāstena vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
diṣṭāntavaśamāyānti tasyaiva rucitaṃ yathā .. 29 ..
1.171.d:
तथा तु काले संन्यस्तास्तेन वैष्णवतेजसा ॥
दिष्टान्तवशमायान्ति तस्यैव रुचितं यथा ॥ 29 ॥
1.171.m:
Then, at the [appointed] time, abandoned by that Vaiṣṇava power,
they come under the sway of their ordained end, just as it pleases him.

1.171.s:
ye ca kecana loke'smindṛśyante tejasānvitāḥ ..
teṣāṃ tadvaiṣṇavaṃ tejastvayā jñeyaṃ mahīpate .. 1.172.30 ..
1.171.d:
ये च केचन लोकेऽस्मिन्दृश्यन्ते तेजसान्विताः ॥
तेषां तद्वैष्णवं तेजस्त्वया ज्ञेयं महीपते ॥ 1.172.30 ॥
1.171.m:
And whatever beings in this world are seen endowed with splendor,
their splendor is to be understood by you as Vaiṣṇava, O lord of the earth.

1.171.s:
yaccandramasi yaccāgnau yacca sūrye jagatpatau ..
tejaḥ paśyati tatsarvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viddhi pārthiva .. 31 ..
1.171.d:
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ यच्च सूर्ये जगत्पतौ ॥
तेजः पश्यति तत्सर्वं वैष्णवं विद्धि पार्थिव ॥ 31 ॥
1.171.m:
What splendor one sees in the moon, in fire, and in the sun, the lord of the world,
know all that to be Vaiṣṇava, O king.

1.171.s:
agastyapramukhānāṃ ca yā ca śaktiratīndriyā ..
tatsthasya rājansā jñeyā tvayā vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 32 ..
1.171.d:
अगस्त्यप्रमुखानां च या च शक्तिरतीन्द्रिया ॥
तत्स्थस्य राजन्सा ज्ञेया त्वया वैष्णवतेजसा ॥ 32 ॥
1.171.m:
And the power beyond the senses of Agastya and other [sages]—
you should know that it belongs to him abiding within it through Vaiṣṇava power, O king.

1.171.s:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā ..
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ yuktaṃ vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 33 ..
1.171.d:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा ॥
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं युक्तं वैष्णवतेजसा ॥ 33 ॥
1.171.m:
Whatever being possesses majesty, prosperity, or great energy,
understand that every such being is endowed with Vaiṣṇava power.

1.171.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca sādhvīnāṃ ca tathā gavām ..
jagatāṃ dhāriṇīṃ śaktiṃ viddhi tāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ vibho ..34..
1.171.d:
ब्राह्मणानां सुराणां च साध्वीनां च तथा गवाम् ॥
जगतां धारिणीं शक्तिं विद्धि तां वैष्णवीं विभो ॥34॥
1.171.m:
The power of brahmins, gods, virtuous women, and cattle
that sustains the worlds—know that to be the power of Viṣṇu, O mighty lord.

1.171.s:
rājānastejasā yuktā vaiṣṇavena vasundharām ..
pālayanti mahīpāla vīryodagrā yaśasvinaḥ .. 35 ..
1.171.d:
राजानस्तेजसा युक्ता वैष्णवेन वसुन्धराम् ॥
पालयन्ति महीपाल वीर्योदग्रा यशस्विनः ॥ 35 ॥
1.171.m:
Kings endowed with Vaiṣṇava power protect the earth,
O protector of the earth, exalted in valour and renowned.

1.171.s:
ṛṣayaśca tathā viprā vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ ..
pālayanti jagatkṛtsnaṃ yuktā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..36..
1.171.d:
ऋषयश्च तथा विप्रा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः ॥
पालयन्ति जगत्कृत्स्नं युक्ता वैष्णवतेजसा ॥36॥
1.171.m:
And the ṛṣis and the twice-born who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas
protect the entire world, endowed with Vaiṣṇava power.

1.171.s:
tretāyugādau ye kecijjāyante cakravartinaḥ ..
guruṇā viddhi tānsarvānsaṃyuktānviṣṇutejasā ..37..
1.171.d:
त्रेतायुगादौ ये केचिज्जायन्ते चक्रवर्तिनः ॥
गुरुणा विद्धि तान्सर्वान्संयुक्तान्विष्णुतेजसा ॥37॥
1.171.m:
Whatever universal monarchs are born at the beginning of the Tretā age,
know them all to be endowed with the mighty power of Viṣṇu.

1.171.s:
ājānubāhavaḥ sarve nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalāḥ ..
jihvayā sakalaṃ vaktraṃ parimārjanti te tathā ..38..
1.171.d:
आजानुबाहवः सर्वे न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलाः ॥
जिह्वया सकलं वक्त्रं परिमार्जन्ति ते तथा ॥38॥
1.171.m:
All of them have arms reaching down to their knees and the proportions of a banyan tree;
they can wipe their entire face with their tongue;

1.171.s:
ṣaṣṭyā dantaiśca saṃyuktā daṃṣṭrābhiśca tathāṣṭabhiḥ ..
aurṇeyaṃ ca śubhaṃ teṣāṃ bhavatyantarbhruvornṛpa..39..
1.171.d:
षष्ट्या दन्तैश्च संयुक्ता दंष्ट्राभिश्च तथाष्टभिः ॥
और्णेयं च शुभं तेषां भवत्यन्तर्भ्रुवोर्नृप॥39॥
1.171.m:
they are endowed with sixty teeth and eight canine teeth;
and they have an auspicious whorl of hair between their eyebrows, O king;

1.171.s:
cakrāṅkitaiḥ pādatalaiḥ karaiścāpi śarāṅkitaiḥ ..
jālapādakarāścaiva tathā turagamehanāḥ ..1.172.40..
1.171.d:
चक्राङ्कितैः पादतलैः करैश्चापि शराङ्कितैः ॥
जालपादकराश्चैव तथा तुरगमेहनाः ॥1.172.40॥
1.171.m:
their soles are marked with wheels and their hands with arrows;
they have webbed hands and feet, and equine privities;

1.171.s:
rūpavantaḥ prabhāvanto vapuṣmantaśca yādava ..
atīndriyajñānabalāḥ pṛthivyāṃ cakravartinaḥ..41..
1.171.d:
रूपवन्तः प्रभावन्तो वपुष्मन्तश्च यादव ॥
अतीन्द्रियज्ञानबलाः पृथिव्यां चक्रवर्तिनः॥41॥
1.171.m:
they are handsome, majestic, magnificent, O Yādava,
possessing knowledge and strength that transcend the senses—the universal monarchs on earth.

1.171.s:
teṣāṃ tu sapta ratnāni bhavantīha mahītale..
hastyaśvaratharatnāni bhāryāratnaṃ tathaiva ca ..42..
1.171.d:
तेषां तु सप्त रत्नानि भवन्तीह महीतले॥
हस्त्यश्वरथरत्नानि भार्यारत्नं तथैव च ॥42॥
1.171.m:
And seven jewels belong to them here on the surface of the earth:
the jewels of an elephant, a horse, a chariot, and likewise the jewel of a wife,

1.171.s:
tathaivāyudharatnaṃ ca maṇiratnanidhistathā ..
catasraścāpratihatāsteṣāṃ tu gatayastathā..43..
1.171.d:
तथैवायुधरत्नं च मणिरत्ननिधिस्तथा ॥
चतस्रश्चाप्रतिहतास्तेषां तु गतयस्तथा॥43॥
1.171.m:
and likewise the jewel of a weapon, the jewel of a gem, and a treasure.
And four unimpeded courses belong to them:

1.171.s:
pātāle gagane śaile samudre ca mahīpate..
samudraḥ stambhitajalaḥ prayāṇe cakravartinām .. 44 ..
1.171.d:
पाताले गगने शैले समुद्रे च महीपते॥
समुद्रः स्तम्भितजलः प्रयाणे चक्रवर्तिनाम् ॥ 44 ॥
1.171.m:
in the underworld, in the sky, upon a mountain, and upon the ocean, O lord of the earth;
the ocean has its waters stilled during the march of the universal monarchs,

1.171.s:
bhūsamāśca tathā śailā mārge teṣāṃ bhavanti tu ..
bhūmirdadāti vivaraṃ pātālamupayāsyatām .. 45 ..
1.171.d:
भूसमाश्च तथा शैला मार्गे तेषां भवन्ति तु ॥
भूमिर्ददाति विवरं पातालमुपयास्यताम् ॥ 45 ॥
1.171.m:
and mountains become level with the ground in their path;
the earth opens a fissure for those about to enter the underworld;

1.171.s:
na viṣīdanti gagane tathā teṣāṃ turaṅgamāḥ ..
śrutena tapasā yajñairvīryeṇāstrabalena ca .. 46 ..
1.171.d:
न विषीदन्ति गगने तथा तेषां तुरङ्गमाः ॥
श्रुतेन तपसा यज्ञैर्वीर्येणास्त्रबलेन च ॥ 46 ॥
1.171.m:
nor do their horses falter in the sky.
By sacred learning, austerity, sacrifices, valour, and mastery of weapons,

1.171.s:
sarvebhyaste'tiricyante prāṇibhyo manujeśvara ..
ārādhitajagannāthāḥ prāpnuvantīha tatpadam .. 47 ..
1.171.d:
सर्वेभ्यस्तेऽतिरिच्यन्ते प्राणिभ्यो मनुजेश्वर ॥
आराधितजगन्नाथाः प्राप्नुवन्तीह तत्पदम् ॥ 47 ॥
1.171.m:
they surpass all living beings, O ruler of men;
having worshipped the Lord of the Universe, they attain his station here.

1.171.s:
varṣāyutāni jīvanti ṣaḍaṣṭau sapta vā nṛpa ..
teṣāṃ ca tejasā viṣṇuḥ karotyāpyāyanaṃ sadā .. 48 ..
1.171.d:
वर्षायुतानि जीवन्ति षडष्टौ सप्त वा नृप ॥
तेषां च तेजसा विष्णुः करोत्याप्यायनं सदा ॥ 48 ॥
1.171.m:
They live for ten thousand, eight thousand, or seven thousand years, O king,
and Viṣṇu constantly invigorates them with his power,

1.171.s:
yena te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ prāpnuvanti guṇodayam ..
sthānāntaragatenāpi te'pi vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 49 ..
1.171.d:
येन ते कथितं सर्वं प्राप्नुवन्ति गुणोदयम् ॥
स्थानान्तरगतेनापि तेऽपि वैष्णवतेजसा ॥ 49 ॥
1.171.m:
by which they attain every rise of excellence that has been described to you.
Even when it has passed to another place, they also, through that Vaiṣṇava power,

1.171.s:
saṃhāramupagacchanti kṣayakāla upasthite ..
kṣayakāle ca māndhātustejastadatiduḥsaham .. 1.172.50 ..
1.171.d:
संहारमुपगच्छन्ति क्षयकाल उपस्थिते ॥
क्षयकाले च मान्धातुस्तेजस्तदतिदुःसहम् ॥ 1.172.50 ॥
1.171.m:
undergo destruction when the time of demise arrives.
And at the time of Māndhātṛ's demise, that unbearable power,

1.171.s:
vaiṣṇavaṃ śūliśūlāgramāśrayāmāsa yādava ..
arjunasya narendrasya yuktasya haritejasā .. 51 ..
1.171.d:
वैष्णवं शूलिशूलाग्रमाश्रयामास यादव ॥
अर्जुनस्य नरेन्द्रस्य युक्तस्य हरितेजसा ॥ 51 ॥
1.171.m:
Vaiṣṇava [in origin], resorted to the tip of the trident of the Trident-bearer, O Yādava.
For King Arjuna, who was endowed with Hari's power,

1.171.s:
harirevāntakṛccāsīdrāmo bhṛgukulodvaha ..
bhārgavasya ca rāmasya tejastadatiduḥsaham .. 52 ..
1.171.d:
हरिरेवान्तकृच्चासीद्रामो भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
भार्गवस्य च रामस्य तेजस्तदतिदुःसहम् ॥ 52 ॥
1.171.m:
Hari himself was the bringer of the end, as Rāma, scion of Bhṛgu's lineage.
And that utterly unbearable power of Rāma the Bhārgava,

1.171.s:
ādatte vaiṣṇavaṃ ghoraṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ ..
kāñcittanumadhiṣṭhāya tena ghoreṇa tejasā .. 53 ..
1.171.d:
आदत्ते वैष्णवं घोरं रामो दशरथात्मजः ॥
काञ्चित्तनुमधिष्ठाय तेन घोरेण तेजसा ॥ 53 ॥
1.171.m:
terrible and Vaiṣṇava, Rāma son of Daśaratha took away.
Having presided over a certain body through that terrible power,

1.171.s:
karoti devakāryāṇi kṛtakarmā tataḥ prabhuḥ ..
ādānaṃ tejasastasya vidhatte sa svatejasā .. 54 ..
1.171.d:
करोति देवकार्याणि कृतकर्मा ततः प्रभुः ॥
आदानं तेजसस्तस्य विधत्ते स स्वतेजसा ॥ 54 ॥
1.171.m:
the Lord carries out the works of the gods; then, his task accomplished,
he undertakes the withdrawal of that power by his own power.

1.171.s: nānyaḥ śamayitā loke nṛpa vaiṣṇavatejasaḥ ..55..
1.171.d: नान्यः शमयिता लोके नृप वैष्णवतेजसः ॥55॥
1.171.m: There is no other pacifier of Vaiṣṇava power in the world, O king.

1.171.s:
tasyāvatāreṣu mayā svarūpametattavoktaṃ bhuvanasya patyuḥ ..
rahasyametatparamaṃ munīnāṃ jñānāmṛtaṃ kalmaṣanāśakāri .. 56..
1.173
vajra uvāca ..
yuvanāśvena yadrājñā putrīyaṃ tu kṛtaṃ vratam ..
tamahaṃ śrotumicchāmi janānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 1 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
putrīyaṃ te pravakṣyāmi vrataṃ bhūpāla sattama ..
anantavratamityuktaṃ sevatāṃ putrajanmadam .. 2 ..
māsimāsi tu nakṣatraṃ māsanāmnā tu cihnitam ..
samprāpya pūjayeddevaṃ sopavāso narottama .. 3 ..
ekaikamaṅgaṃ devasya pratimāsaṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
pūjayetprayataḥ śuddhaḥ śṛṇu cāṅgakramaṃ mama .. 4 ..
mārgaśīrṣādathārabhya vratametatsamārabhet ..
devasya mārgaśīrṣe tu vāmaṃ jānuṃ samarcayet..5 ..
kaṭibhāgaṃ tathā vāmaṃ pauṣe māsi samarcayet ..
māghe maghāsu vāmaṃ ca bhujaṃ devasya pūjayet ..6..
1.171.d:
तस्यावतारेषु मया स्वरूपमेतत्तवोक्तं भुवनस्य पत्युः ॥
रहस्यमेतत्परमं मुनीनां ज्ञानामृतं कल्मषनाशकारि ॥ 56॥
1.173
वज्र उवाच ॥
युवनाश्वेन यद्राज्ञा पुत्रीयं तु कृतं व्रतम् ॥
तमहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि जनानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 1 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पुत्रीयं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि व्रतं भूपाल सत्तम ॥
अनन्तव्रतमित्युक्तं सेवतां पुत्रजन्मदम् ॥ 2 ॥
मासिमासि तु नक्षत्रं मासनाम्ना तु चिह्नितम् ॥
सम्प्राप्य पूजयेद्देवं सोपवासो नरोत्तम ॥ 3 ॥
एकैकमङ्गं देवस्य प्रतिमासं विशेषतः ॥
पूजयेत्प्रयतः शुद्धः शृणु चाङ्गक्रमं मम ॥ 4 ॥
मार्गशीर्षादथारभ्य व्रतमेतत्समारभेत् ॥
देवस्य मार्गशीर्षे तु वामं जानुं समर्चयेत्॥5 ॥
कटिभागं तथा वामं पौषे मासि समर्चयेत् ॥
माघे मघासु वामं च भुजं देवस्य पूजयेत् ॥6॥
1.171.m:
This true nature of the Lord of the universe during his incarnations has been told to you by me—
this supreme secret of the sages, the nectar of knowledge that destroys sins.
1.173
Vajra said:
I wish to hear about that son-yielding observance which was performed by King Yuvanāśva,
out of a desire for the welfare of mankind.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall explain to you the son-yielding observance, O best of kings,
called the Anantavrata, which grants the birth of a son to those who practice it.
Month by month, when the asterism marked by the name of that month arrives, / fasting, best of men, one should worship the God.
Particularly, one limb after another of the God should be worshipped each month, / restrained and pure; listen to my sequence of the limbs.
Beginning from Mārgaśīrṣa, one should undertake this observance: / In Mārgaśīrṣa, one should worship the left knee of the God.
And in the month of Pauṣa, one should worship the left portion of the waist; / in Māgha, under Maghā, one should worship the left arm of the God.

1.171.d:
उत्तराफल्गुनीऋक्षे स्कन्धं वामं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
चतुर्ष्वेतेषु वामेषु गोमूत्रस्नानमाचरेत् ॥ 7 ॥
पूजनं देवदेवस्य रक्तैः पुष्पादिभिस्तथा ॥
होमो घृतेन कर्तव्यस्तिलदानं द्विजातिषु ॥ 8 ॥
ताम्रस्य च तथा दानं गोमूत्रप्राशनं ततः ॥
हविष्यान्नेन चाहारं ततः कार्यं विजानता ॥ 9 ॥
देवस्य दक्षिणं स्कन्धं चैत्रे चित्रासु पूजयेत् ॥
वैशाखे च विशाखासु बाहुं देवस्य दक्षिणम् ॥ 1.173.10 ॥
दक्षिणं कटिभागं च ज्येष्ठे ज्येष्ठासु पूजयेत् ॥
दक्षिणं च तथा जानुमाषाढे वैश्वदेवके 51 1॥
चतुर्ष्वेतेषु मासेषु क्षीरस्नानं विधीयते ॥
पीतपुष्पादिपूजा च देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥ 12 ॥
होमं च शालिभिः कुर्याद्यवा देया द्विजातिषु ॥
रजतं च तथा देयं यथान्नेन भुजिक्रिया ॥13॥
तथा कार्या मनुष्येन्द्र श्रावणेश्रावणे ततः ॥
पादादौ पूजयेत्तस्य यस्येदं सकलं जगत् ॥ 14 ॥
1.171.m:
Under the asterism Uttarāphalguni, one should worship the left shoulder. / In these four left [phases], one should perform bathing with cow urine.
The worship of the God of gods should be performed with red flowers and other offerings; / the fire offering should be made with clarified butter, and a gift of sesame seeds to the twice-born.
And likewise a gift of copper; then the drinking of cow urine, / and then the wise person should take food consisting of sacrificial fare.
In Caitra under Citrā, one should worship the right shoulder of the God; / and in Vaiśākha under Viśākhā, the right arm of the God.
In Jyeṣṭha under Jyeṣṭhā, one should worship the right portion of the waist; / and in Āṣāḍha under Vaiśvadeva, the right knee.
In these four months, bathing with milk is prescribed, / and worship with yellow flowers and the like for the discus-bearing God of gods.
One should make the fire offering with śāli rice; barley should be given to the twice-born, / and silver should also be given, just as food is taken.
So it should be done, lord of men. Then, in Śrāvaṇa under Śravaṇa, / one should worship first the feet of Him whose whole world this is.

1.171.d:
गुप्तं भाद्रपदे मासि आश्विने हृदयं ततः ॥
शिरसः पूजनं कार्यं कार्तिके कृत्तिकासु च ॥ 15 ॥
चतुर्ष्वेतेषु एतेषु मासेषु दध्ना स्नानं विधीयते ॥
पूजनं देवदेवस्य शुक्लैः पुष्पादिभिस्तथा ॥ 16 ॥
क्षीरेण होमः कर्तव्यो घृतं देयं द्विजातिषु ॥
सुवर्णं तु तथा राजन्दध्ना कार्यां भुजिक्रिया ॥ 17 ॥
अनन्तनाम जप्तव्यं सर्वमासेषु पार्थिव॥
तेनैव नाम्ना देवस्य होमकर्माणि निर्दिशेत् ॥ 18 ॥
व्रतावसाने दातव्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तु भोजनम् ॥
दानं शक्त्या च दातव्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नराधिप ॥ 19 ॥
संवत्सरादवाप्नोति सर्वानेव मनोरथान् ॥
पुत्रार्थिभिर्वृत्तिकामैर्भृत्यदारधनेप्सुभिः ॥ 1.173.20 ॥
प्रार्थयद्भिश्च कर्तव्यं बलमारोग्यसम्पदम् ॥
एतद्व्रतं महाराज पुण्यं स्वस्त्ययनं परम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.171.m:
In the month of Bhādrapada, the private parts; then in Āśvina, the heart; / and in Kārtika under Kṛttikā, the worship of the head should be done.
In these four months, bathing with curds is prescribed, / and worship of the God of gods with white flowers and the like.
The fire offering should be made with milk; clarified butter should be given to the twice-born, / and gold likewise, O King; eating should be done with curds.
The name of Ananta should be chanted in all months, O King; / with that very name, one should perform the fire-offering rites for the God.
At the conclusion of the observance, food should be given to brahmins; / and gifts should be given according to one's capacity to brahmins, O ruler of men.
After a year, one attains all wishes whatsoever. / It should be observed by those desiring sons, those desiring a livelihood, those seeking servants, wives, and wealth,
and by those praying for strength, health, and prosperity. / This observance, great king, is auspicious and brings supreme well-being.

1.171.d:
अनन्तव्रतमित्युक्तं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
व्रतमेतत्पुरा कृत्वा युवनाश्वो महीपतिः ॥22 ॥
मान्धातारं सुतं लेभे राजानं चक्रवर्तिनम् ॥
कृतवीर्यस्य राजेन्द्र भार्या शीलधरा तथा ॥ 23 ॥
व्रतेनानेन सा लेभे पुत्रं बाहुसहस्रिणम् ॥
कार्तवीर्यार्जुनं नाम राजानं चक्रवर्तिनम् ॥ 24 ॥
यमाविवेश भगवांस्तेजसा स्वेन माधवः ॥
नमस्ते कार्तवीर्याय अर्जुनाय महात्मने ॥ 25 ॥
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायां मेदिन्यामीश्वराय च ॥
एतावदुक्ता पुण्येन तिलप्रस्थस्य युज्यते ॥26॥
राजन्दत्तस्य विधिवद्ब्राह्मणाय यतात्मने ॥
यस्य वै जातमात्रस्य प्रववावनिलः शुभः ॥ 27 ॥
नीरजस्कमभूद्व्योम मुदं प्रापाखिलं जगत्॥
समाश्रयार्थं नृपतिं दैत्या मानुष्यतां गताः ॥28 ॥
1.171.m:
It is called the Anantavrata, destroying all defilements. / Having performed this observance in the past, King Yuvanāśva
obtained a son, Māndhātṛ, a universal sovereign king; / and likewise, O foremost of kings, Śīladharā, the wife of Kṛtavīrya,
by means of this observance obtained a thousand-armed son, / named Kārtavīryārjuna, a universal sovereign king,
whom the blessed Mādhava entered with His own splendor: / 'Homage to you, Kārtavīrya, the great-souled Arjuna,
and the sovereign over the earth with its seven continents and oceans!' / By that much merit, it equals [the gift of] a prastha measure of sesame seeds,
duly given, O King, to a self-controlled brahmin. / At whose very birth an auspicious wind blew,
the sky became dustless, and the entire world experienced joy; / seeking refuge with the king, Daityas entered human form

1.174
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इदमन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि मासनक्षत्रपूजनम् ॥
यत्फलं देवदेवस्य पुरुषः समुपाश्नुते ॥ 1 ॥
आरभ्य कार्तिकादेतद्व्रतं कार्यं विजानता ॥
पारणत्रितयेनैतद्व्रतं परिसमाप्यते ॥ 2 ॥
चातुर्मास्यं तथैवात्र पारणं नृप कीर्तितम् ॥
पारणेपारणे राजन्प्रतिमासविधिं शृणु ॥ 3 ॥
पञ्चगव्यजलस्नानं सदैव च समाचरेत् ॥
पुष्पादिपूजा कर्तव्या यथालाभमुपाहृतैः ॥ 4 ॥
नैवेद्यं कृसरं पूर्वमत्र मासचतुष्टयम् ॥
यावकेन तथा कार्यं मध्यमं च चतुष्टयम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.171.m:
and resorted [to him] untroubled, by hundreds and thousands; / under whom the earth, having an excellent king, distressed by heavy burden, / maintained herself with difficulty, her body turbid with waters, O King.
This ancient observance bestowing sons has been declared by me to you, lion among kings; / it should be performed on earth by those who desire sons, removing sin and increasing dharma.
1.174
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I shall declare this other worship of the asterisms of the months, / the fruit of which a man obtains from the God of gods.
Beginning from Kārtika, this observance should be performed by the wise person; / with three meal-breakings, this observance is brought to completion.
A four-month period is proclaimed here for each meal-breaking, O King; / at each meal-breaking, O King, hear the rule for each month.
One should always perform bathing with water mixed with the five products of the cow; / worship with flowers and the like should be performed with whatever is obtained.
The food offering for the first four months here should be kṛsara; / for the middle four, it should be made with barley gruel;

चतुष्टये तृतीये च नैवेद्यं पायसं भवेत् ॥
तेनैवान्नेन राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्बुधः ॥ 6 ॥
नक्तं नैवेद्यमश्नीयाद्वाग्यतः सुसमाहितः ॥
संयतस्तां भवेद्रात्रिं तथा स्थण्डिलशायकः ॥ 7 ॥
एवं कुर्यात्पुनस्तावद्यावत्कार्तिककृत्तिका ॥
तत्र सम्पूज्य देवेशमारम्भ विधिना नृप ॥ 8 ॥
भाजनं घृतसंपूर्णं सहिरण्यं द्विजातये ॥
दातव्यं भोजनं कार्यं ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः ॥ 9 ॥
संवत्सरमिदं कृत्वा व्रतं पुरुष सत्तमः ॥
लब्ध्वा स्थानं च मोदेत तथा नारी च यादव ॥ 1.174.10 ॥

आस्थां सुदीर्घां त्रिदिवे च कुर्याद्व्रतं नृणामेतदतीव पुण्यम् ॥ 11 ॥

1.171.m:
and in the third four, the food offering should be milk-rice. / With that very food, O foremost of kings, the wise person should feed brahmins.
At night, one should eat the offered food, restrained in speech and well-composed; / restrained, one should spend that night lying on the bare ground.
One should do so again until Kṛttikā in Kārtika; / there, having worshipped the Lord of gods according to the initial rule, O King,
a vessel filled with clarified butter, along with gold, should be given to a twice-born, / and a feast should especially be provided for brahmins.
Having performed this observance for a year, the best of men, / having attained his abode, rejoices, and likewise a woman, O descendant of Yadu.
It produces lasting fortune, a mind set on dharma, strength, good fortune, vitality, and steadfast courage, / and a very long stay in heaven; this observance for human beings brings immense merit.
1.175
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Here I shall narrate to you a story that destroys sin, / which took place in heaven, concerning the worship of the asterisms of the months.

1.171.s:
pūrvaistu caritaṃ śakra nāhaṃ jānāmi kiñcana ..
bhavataḥ samakālīnaṃ viddhi māṃ surasattama ..2 ..
iyaṃ siddhā vijānāti prakhyātā śāmbarāyaṇī ..
evamuktastataḥ śakraḥ papraccha balasūdanaḥ .. 3 ..
jagāda sā ca śakrasya pūrvendracaritaṃ mahat ..
śakrāṇāṃ sā vyatītānāṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 4 ..
jagāda tatra caritaṃ kalpeṣvanyeṣvapi prabho ..
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
sarveṣāmapi śakrāṇāṃ ye tu dāyādabāndhavāḥ .. 5..
sarve vināśitāstena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
sarve śakrāstathā yuktāstena vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 6..
bhūtebhyastvatiricyante tena te guṇasampadaḥ ..
dānena yajñaiḥ śauryeṇa tapasā ca balena ca .. 7 ..
śrutena dharmiṣṭhatayā devadaityamahoragān ..
ṛṣayaśca mahābhāgāstepi pārthivasattama .. 8 ..
1.171.d:
पूर्वैस्तु चरितं शक्र नाहं जानामि किञ्चन ॥
भवतः समकालीनं विद्धि मां सुरसत्तम ॥2 ॥
इयं सिद्धा विजानाति प्रख्याता शाम्बरायणी ॥
एवमुक्तस्ततः शक्रः पप्रच्छ बलसूदनः ॥ 3 ॥
जगाद सा च शक्रस्य पूर्वेन्द्रचरितं महत् ॥
शक्राणां सा व्यतीतानां शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 4 ॥
जगाद तत्र चरितं कल्पेष्वन्येष्वपि प्रभो ॥
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
सर्वेषामपि शक्राणां ये तु दायादबान्धवाः ॥ 5॥
सर्वे विनाशितास्तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥
सर्वे शक्रास्तथा युक्तास्तेन वैष्णवतेजसा ॥ 6॥
भूतेभ्यस्त्वतिरिच्यन्ते तेन ते गुणसम्पदः ॥
दानेन यज्ञैः शौर्येण तपसा च बलेन च ॥ 7 ॥
श्रुतेन धर्मिष्ठतया देवदैत्यमहोरगान् ॥
ऋषयश्च महाभागास्तेपि पार्थिवसत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
1.171.m:
I know nothing at all, O Śakra, of the deeds of former beings; / know me, O best of gods, to be contemporary with yourself.
"This accomplished female ascetic knows, the renowned Śāmbarāyaṇī."
Having been addressed thus, Śakra, the slayer of Bala, asked [her].
And she narrated to Śakra the great deeds of earlier Indras,
of the past Śakras by the hundreds and thousands.
She related their deeds in other aeons as well, O lord.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
All the cousin-kinsmen of every one of the Śakras
were destroyed by that mighty Viṣṇu;
likewise, all the Śakras were endowed with that Vaiṣṇava splendour.
Therefore, their abundance of virtues surpassed [all] beings,
through generosity, sacrifices, heroism, austerity, and strength,
through sacred learning and righteousness, [surpassing] gods, Daityas, and great serpents.
And the illustrious sages, even they, O best of earthly rulers,

1.171.s:
varaṃ sampāvanaṃ taiśca kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ svayaṃbhuvā ..
parājayaṃ yataḥ prāptā dāyādebhyaḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. 9 ..
sarveśvarā vīryabalopapannā dharme niviṣṭā jagataḥ pradhānāḥ ..
tyaktādhikārāśca tataḥ krameṇa sarve gatā viṣṇusahāyatāṃ ca ..1.175.10..
1.171.d:
वरं सम्पावनं तैश्च कृतं सर्वं स्वयंभुवा ॥
पराजयं यतः प्राप्ता दायादेभ्यः पुनःपुनः ॥ 9 ॥
सर्वेश्वरा वीर्यबलोपपन्ना धर्मे निविष्टा जगतः प्रधानाः ॥
त्यक्ताधिकाराश्च ततः क्रमेण सर्वे गता विष्णुसहायतां च ॥1.175.10॥
1.171.m:
granted the purifying boon, all done by the Self-born,
since they suffered defeat from their kinsmen again and again.
Sovereigns of all, endowed with valour and strength, established in dharma, foremost of the world,
having relinquished their office in due course, they all attained companionship with Viṣṇu.

1.176
.. indra uvāca ..
yasminkāle vyatītā ye ṣaḍindrā bhūritejasaḥ ..
teṣāṃ caritamicchāmi śrotuṃ vistaraśaḥ śubhe .. 1 ..
1.172.d:
1.176
॥ इन्द्र उवाच ॥
यस्मिन्काले व्यतीता ये षडिन्द्रा भूरितेजसः ॥
तेषां चरितमिच्छामि श्रोतुं विस्तरशः शुभे ॥ 1 ॥
1.172.m:
1.176
Indra said:
At which time the six Indras of vast splendour passed away,
I desire to hear their deeds in detail, O auspicious one.

1.172.s:
prati śakraṃ manuṃ bhadre manuputrāṃstathaiva ca ..
devānsaptaṛṣīṃścaiva tathā dāyādabāṃdhavān .. 2 ..
1.172.d:
प्रति शक्रं मनुं भद्रे मनुपुत्रांस्तथैव च ॥
देवान्सप्तऋषींश्चैव तथा दायादबांधवान् ॥ 2 ॥
1.172.m:
For each Śakra, [tell of] the Manu, O blessed lady, and likewise the Manu’s sons,
the gods, the seven sages, and likewise their cousin-kinsmen,

1.172.s:
śakrasya teṣāṃ ca vadhaṃ tathā devājjanārdanāt ..
tvattohaṃ śrotu micchāmi sarvaṃ tvaṃ vetsi sundari ..3..
1.172.d:
शक्रस्य तेषां च वधं तथा देवाज्जनार्दनात् ॥
त्वत्तोहं श्रोतु मिच्छामि सर्वं त्वं वेत्सि सुन्दरि ॥3॥
1.172.m:
and the slaying of them by god Janārdana for Śakra’s sake.
I wish to hear everything from you; you know all, O fair one.

1.172.s:
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca..
brahmaṇo mānasaḥ putraḥ prathamastu manuḥ smṛtaḥ ..
daśa putrāśca tasyeme khyātāstribhuvaneśvara .. ..4..
1.172.d:
शाम्बरायण्युवाच॥
ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रः प्रथमस्तु मनुः स्मृतः ॥
दश पुत्राश्च तस्येमे ख्यातास्त्रिभुवनेश्वर ॥ ॥4॥
1.172.m:
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
The mind-born son of Brahmā is remembered as the first Manu,
and these ten sons of his are renowned, O lord of the three worlds:

1.172.s:
agnīdhraścātibāhuśca medhā medhātithirvasuḥ ..
jyotiṣmāndyutimānhavyaḥ savanaḥ satra eva ca ..5..
1.172.d:
अग्नीध्रश्चातिबाहुश्च मेधा मेधातिथिर्वसुः ॥
ज्योतिष्मान्द्युतिमान्हव्यः सवनः सत्र एव च ॥5॥
1.172.m:
Agnīdhra, Atibāhu, Medhā, Medhātithi, Vasu,
Jyotiṣmat, Dyutimat, Havya, Savana, and Satra.

1.172.s:
marīciratryaṅgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ..
vasiṣṭhaśca mahātejā ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ ..6..
1.172.d:
मरीचिरत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥
वसिष्ठश्च महातेजा ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥6॥
1.172.m:
Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,
and the immensely splendid Vasiṣṭha are declared as the seven sages.

1.172.s:
jayākhyāścājitākhyāśca śukrayāmāstathaiva ca ..
gaṇā dvādaśakā ete catvāraḥ somapīthinaḥ .. 7 ..
1.172.d:
जयाख्याश्चाजिताख्याश्च शुक्रयामास्तथैव च ॥
गणा द्वादशका एते चत्वारः सोमपीथिनः ॥ 7 ॥
1.172.m:
Those named Jaya, those named Ajita, and likewise the Śukras and Yāmas—
these four groups of twelve are the drinkers of soma.

1.172.s:
viśvabhuṅnāma devānāṃ teṣāmindro babhūva ha ..
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ .. 8 ..
1.172.d:
विश्वभुङ्नाम देवानां तेषामिन्द्रो बभूव ह ॥
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥ 8 ॥
1.172.m:
Viśvabhuj by name was the Indra of those gods.
At that time, fierce Asuras were his cousin-kinsmen,

1.172.s:
babhūva nṛpatiryeṣāṃ bāṣkalo nāma nāmataḥ ..
yasya hastādubhau lokau vāmanena hṛtau purā .. 9 ..
1.172.d:
बभूव नृपतिर्येषां बाष्कलो नाम नामतः ॥
यस्य हस्तादुभौ लोकौ वामनेन हृतौ पुरा ॥ 9 ॥
1.172.m:
whose king was named Bāṣkala by name,
from whose hand both worlds were formerly taken by Vāmana.

1.172.s:
kramadvayena tu hṛtaṃ pātālaṃ ca sureśvara ..
yasya putravatastvāsītkeśī nāma balotkaṭaḥ .. 1.176.10 ..
1.172.d:
क्रमद्वयेन तु हृतं पातालं च सुरेश्वर ॥
यस्य पुत्रवतस्त्वासीत्केशी नाम बलोत्कटः ॥ 1.176.10 ॥
1.172.m:
And with two strides the netherworld was taken, O lord of gods.
That [king], who had a son, had [one] named Keśin of extraordinary strength.

1.172.s:
jahāra bhūyastrailokyaṃ śakrasyākramya durmatiḥ ..
tamāhūya raṇe viṣṇustārkṣyapravaravāhanaḥ..11..
1.172.d:
जहार भूयस्त्रैलोक्यं शक्रस्याक्रम्य दुर्मतिः ॥
तमाहूय रणे विष्णुस्तार्क्ष्यप्रवरवाहनः॥11॥
1.172.m:
Having attacked, that evil-minded one seized once again the three worlds from Śakra.
Challenging him in battle, Viṣṇu, whose mount is the foremost Tārkṣya,
cleft him in two with his discus, desiring the welfare of the three worlds.

1.172.s:
evaṃ hatastena purārimukhyo mahātmanā kālasamaprabhāvaḥ ...
śakrapriyārthaṃ jagatāṃ hitārthaṃ deveśvareṇāpratimena tena ..13..
1.177
.. śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
manuḥ svārociṣo nāma babhūva tadanantarama ..
yasyāsansumahābhāgāḥ putrā bhūmaṇḍaleśvarāḥ .. 1 ..
caitraḥ kavirutaścaiva kṛtānto vidyuto raviḥ ..
bṛhadgraho nabhaścaiva mahābalaparākramaḥ .. 2 ..
ūrjastasya tathā prāṇa ṛṣabho niścalastathā ..
dantobhiḥ śākvarīvāṃśca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ .. 3 ..
bhūṣitā dvādaśa proktāstathā pārāvatāśca ye ..
teṣāmindro vipaścicca mahātmā lokaviśrutaḥ .. 4 ..
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..
teṣāmāsīttadā rājā purukutso balādhikaḥ .. 5 ..
śakrasya vipriyāsakto mṛgayāyai vanaṅgataḥ ..
vyadhamatkuñjarānmattānbahuvīryasamāśrayaḥ ..
hastī bhūpālasacivaḥ sa jaghāna harīnvane .. 6 ..
1.172.d:
एवं हतस्तेन पुरारिमुख्यो महात्मना कालसमप्रभावः ॥।
शक्रप्रियार्थं जगतां हितार्थं देवेश्वरेणाप्रतिमेन तेन ॥13॥
1.177
॥ शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
मनुः स्वारोचिषो नाम बभूव तदनन्तरम ॥
यस्यासन्सुमहाभागाः पुत्रा भूमण्डलेश्वराः ॥ 1 ॥
चैत्रः कविरुतश्चैव कृतान्तो विद्युतो रविः ॥
बृहद्ग्रहो नभश्चैव महाबलपराक्रमः ॥ 2 ॥
ऊर्जस्तस्य तथा प्राण ऋषभो निश्चलस्तथा ॥
दन्तोभिः शाक्वरीवांश्च ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥ 3 ॥
भूषिता द्वादश प्रोक्तास्तथा पारावताश्च ये ॥
तेषामिन्द्रो विपश्चिच्च महात्मा लोकविश्रुतः ॥ 4 ॥
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥
तेषामासीत्तदा राजा पुरुकुत्सो बलाधिकः ॥ 5 ॥
शक्रस्य विप्रियासक्तो मृगयायै वनङ्गतः ॥
व्यधमत्कुञ्जरान्मत्तान्बहुवीर्यसमाश्रयः ॥
हस्ती भूपालसचिवः स जघान हरीन्वने ॥ 6 ॥
1.172.m:
Thus formerly was that chief of enemies slain by that great soul whose power equalled Death,
for the pleasure of Śakra, for the welfare of the worlds, by that peerless lord of the gods.
1.177
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
The Manu named Svārociṣa arose immediately after that,
whose sons were greatly fortunate rulers of the terrestrial orb:
Caitra, Kaviruta, Kṛtānta, Vidyuta, Ravi,
Bṛhadgraha, Nabha, of great strength and valour.
His [sages were] Ūrja, Prāṇa, Ṛṣabha, Niścala,
Dantobhi, and Śākvarīvat; [these] are proclaimed as the seven sages.
Twelve are spoken of as the Bhūṣitas, and likewise those [called] Pārāvatas;
their Indra was the high-souled Vipaścit, world-renowned.
At that time, fierce Asuras were his cousin-kinsmen;
their king then was Purukutsa, superior in strength.
Intent upon doing disservice to Śakra, he went to the forest to hunt;
resorting to great prowess, he destroyed rutting elephants.
An elephant [form], the king's companion, killed the lions in the forest.

1.172.s:
jaghāna saḥ śaila ivātivarṣmā nīlāñjanābho racitāgrahastaḥ ..
jaghāna taṃ daityavaraṃ prasahya devāsurāṇāṃ samareṣvavadhyam .. 7 ..
1.178
.. śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca .. ..
auttamasya manoḥ putrāstṛtīyasya nibodha me ..
ajaśca paraśuścaiva devadevo vṛdho nayaḥ .. 1 ..
devāvṛdhaścāpratimo mahotsāho gajastathā ..
vinītaśca suketuśca sumitraḥ subalaḥ śuciḥ .. 2 ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi ṛṣayaḥ sapta vai tadā ..
rajobāhūrdhvabāhū ca savanaścānaghaśca yaḥ .. 3 ..
sutapāḥ śaktirityete ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ ..
vaśavartinaḥ svadhāsāno vaśā satyahā matārdanāḥ .. 4 ..
pañca devagaṇāḥ proktāḥ sarve dvādaśakāstu te ..
teṣāṃ sucittirnāmā'bhūcchakraḥ parapurañjayaḥ..5..
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..
yeṣāmāsīdbalī rājā pralambo nāma nāmataḥ .. 6 ..
1.172.d:
जघान सः शैल इवातिवर्ष्मा नीलाञ्जनाभो रचिताग्रहस्तः ॥
जघान तं दैत्यवरं प्रसह्य देवासुराणां समरेष्ववध्यम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.178
॥ शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥ ॥
औत्तमस्य मनोः पुत्रास्तृतीयस्य निबोध मे ॥
अजश्च परशुश्चैव देवदेवो वृधो नयः ॥ 1 ॥
देवावृधश्चाप्रतिमो महोत्साहो गजस्तथा ॥
विनीतश्च सुकेतुश्च सुमित्रः सुबलः शुचिः ॥ 2 ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि ऋषयः सप्त वै तदा ॥
रजोबाहूर्ध्वबाहू च सवनश्चानघश्च यः ॥ 3 ॥
सुतपाः शक्तिरित्येते ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥
वशवर्तिनः स्वधासानो वशा सत्यहा मतार्दनाः ॥ 4 ॥
पञ्च देवगणाः प्रोक्ताः सर्वे द्वादशकास्तु ते ॥
तेषां सुचित्तिर्नामाऽभूच्छक्रः परपुरञ्जयः॥5॥
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥
येषामासीद्बली राजा प्रलम्बो नाम नामतः ॥ 6 ॥
1.172.m:
Massive as a mountain, radiant like black collyrium, with outstretched trunk,
he violently killed that foremost Daitya who could not be slain in battles by gods or Asuras.
1.178
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Learn from me the sons of Auttama, the third Manu:
Aja, Paraśu, Devadeva, Vṛdha, Naya,
Devāvṛdha, Apratima, Mahotsāha, Gaja,
Vinīta, Suketu, Sumitra, Subala, and Śuci.
Hereafter I shall proclaim the seven sages at that time:
Rajobāhu, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, and Anagha,
Sutapas, and Śakti—these are declared as the seven sages.
The Vaśavartins, the Svadhāsans, the Vaśas, the Satyahās, and the Matārdanas—
these five classes of gods are declared, and each consists of twelve.
Their Śakra was Sucitti by name, conqueror of enemies' citadels.
At that time, fierce Asuras were his cousin-kinsmen,
whose mighty king was Pralamba by name.

1.172.s:
śakrasya vipriyāsaktaṃ taṃ samudrāmbuvāhinam ..
matsyarūpadharo viṣṇurgrastavānbalavattaram .. 7 ..
kālānalābhaṃ tu videśaśatruṃ rūpeṇa mātsyena jagatpracāraḥ ..
jaghāna taṃ parvatakūṭamātraṃ samudra madhye śaradānatṛptam .. 8 ..
1.179
..śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca .. ..
tāmasasya manoḥ putrāṃścaturthasya nibodha me ..
jānujaṅghaḥ śāntabhayo naraḥ khyātirnarastathā .. 1 ..
priyabhṛtyo hyavikṣicca prasthilaśca dṛḍheṣudhiḥ ..
kṛtaśca kṛtagandhaśca tāmasasya manoḥ sutāḥ .. 2 ..
ṛṣirvanaḥ kaṭhīyānvai gātraścaitro'gnireva ca ..
jyotirvāsāḥ pṛthuḥ kārya ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ .. 3 ..
satyāḥ supādāḥ surihā haraśceti prakīrtitāḥ ..
devatānāṃ gaṇā ete catvāraḥ pañcaviṃśakāḥ ..4..
satyānāmapi bhedau dvau satyā viśvāśca kīrtitāḥ ..
satyā dvādaśa nirdiṣṭā viśvā proktāstrayodaśa..5..
1.172.d:
शक्रस्य विप्रियासक्तं तं समुद्राम्बुवाहिनम् ॥
मत्स्यरूपधरो विष्णुर्ग्रस्तवान्बलवत्तरम् ॥ 7 ॥
कालानलाभं तु विदेशशत्रुं रूपेण मात्स्येन जगत्प्रचारः ॥
जघान तं पर्वतकूटमात्रं समुद्र मध्ये शरदानतृप्तम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.179
॥शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥ ॥
तामसस्य मनोः पुत्रांश्चतुर्थस्य निबोध मे ॥
जानुजङ्घः शान्तभयो नरः ख्यातिर्नरस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
प्रियभृत्यो ह्यविक्षिच्च प्रस्थिलश्च दृढेषुधिः ॥
कृतश्च कृतगन्धश्च तामसस्य मनोः सुताः ॥ 2 ॥
ऋषिर्वनः कठीयान्वै गात्रश्चैत्रोऽग्निरेव च ॥
ज्योतिर्वासाः पृथुः कार्य ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥ 3 ॥
सत्याः सुपादाः सुरिहा हरश्चेति प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
देवतानां गणा एते चत्वारः पञ्चविंशकाः ॥4॥
सत्यानामपि भेदौ द्वौ सत्या विश्वाश्च कीर्तिताः ॥
सत्या द्वादश निर्दिष्टा विश्वा प्रोक्तास्त्रयोदश॥5॥
1.172.m:
Intent upon doing disservice to Śakra, carrying the waters of the ocean,
Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a fish, swallowed that exceedingly powerful one.
Resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution, an enemy in foreign lands, [Viṣṇu] moving through the worlds in the form of a fish,
slew him, who was as large as a mountain peak and unsatisfied by autumn, in the midst of the ocean.
1.179
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Learn from me the sons of Tāmasa, the fourth Manu:
Jānujaṅgha, Śāntabhaya, Nara, Khyāti, and Nara.
Priyabhṛtya, indeed Avikṣit, Prasthila, and Dṛḍheṣudhi, / and Kṛta and Kṛtagandha are the sons of Manu Tāmasa.
The sage Vana, Kaṭhīyān indeed, Gātra, Caitra, and Agni, / Jyotirvāsas, Pṛthu, and Kāvya are proclaimed the seven sages.
The Satyas, Supādas, Surihas, and Haras are proclaimed / as these four groups of deities, consisting of twenty-five each.
Of the Satyas, two divisions are proclaimed: the Satyas and the Viśvas; / twelve are designated as Satyas, and thirteen are declared as Viśvas.

1.172.s:
teṣāmāsīnmahātejā śibiriṃdraḥ pratāpavān..
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..6..
yeṣāmāsīnmahātejā rājā bhīmarathaḥ prabhuḥ ..
prasādya yena brahmāṇamavadhyatvaṃ sthale vṛtam .. ..7..
jalaṃ sa varjayāmāsa tataḥ prabhṛti durmatiḥ ..
sa dadarśa marau kūrmaṃ parvatākāradarśanam .. 8 ..
tamāruroha durbuddhiḥ kautūhalasamanvitaḥ ..
samārūḍhaṃ mahākāyamādāya bhagavānhariḥ .. 9 ..
kūrmarūpadharo vegātpātālajalamāviśat ..
pātālajalamānīya majjayitvā jaghāna tam ..
ākramya taṃ mahākāyaṃ mahatā kūrmavarṣmaṇā .. 1.179.10 ..
evaṃ sa kūrmeṇa jale prasahya deveśvarasyāpratimasya śatruḥ ..
nipātitaḥ sarvasurapradhānaḥ sarveśvareṇā pratimena tena .. 11 ..
1.180
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
raivatasya manoḥ putrānpañcamasya nibodha me ..
mahāpurāṇaḥ sambhāvyaḥ pratyaṅgaḥ parahā śuciḥ .. 1 ..
1.172.d:
तेषामासीन्महातेजा शिबिरिंद्रः प्रतापवान्॥
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥6॥
येषामासीन्महातेजा राजा भीमरथः प्रभुः ॥
प्रसाद्य येन ब्रह्माणमवध्यत्वं स्थले वृतम् ॥ ॥7॥
जलं स वर्जयामास ततः प्रभृति दुर्मतिः ॥
स ददर्श मरौ कूर्मं पर्वताकारदर्शनम् ॥ 8 ॥
तमारुरोह दुर्बुद्धिः कौतूहलसमन्वितः ॥
समारूढं महाकायमादाय भगवान्हरिः ॥ 9 ॥
कूर्मरूपधरो वेगात्पातालजलमाविशत् ॥
पातालजलमानीय मज्जयित्वा जघान तम् ॥
आक्रम्य तं महाकायं महता कूर्मवर्ष्मणा ॥ 1.179.10 ॥
एवं स कूर्मेण जले प्रसह्य देवेश्वरस्याप्रतिमस्य शत्रुः ॥
निपातितः सर्वसुरप्रधानः सर्वेश्वरेणा प्रतिमेन तेन ॥ 11 ॥
1.180
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
रैवतस्य मनोः पुत्रान्पञ्चमस्य निबोध मे ॥
महापुराणः सम्भाव्यः प्रत्यङ्गः परहा शुचिः ॥ 1 ॥
1.172.m:
Their Indra was the valorous Śibi of great splendour. / At that time there were terrible asuras, kinsmen sharing inheritance with him,
whose master was the king Bhīmaratha of great splendour, / by whom, having propitiated Brahmā, invulnerability on dry land was chosen [as a boon].
From then on, that evil-minded one avoided water. / In the desert he saw a tortoise looking like a mountain.
Filled with curiosity, the foolish-minded one mounted upon it. / Lord Hari, taking that enormous-bodied one who had mounted [him],
bearing the form of a tortoise, swiftly entered the waters of the netherworld. / Having brought him to the waters of the netherworld and submerged him, he killed him, / having overwhelmed that huge body with his immense tortoise form.
Thus, that foremost of all asuras, the enemy of the peerless lord of the gods, / was forcibly struck down in the water with a tortoise [form] by that peerless Lord of All.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said: / Learn from me the sons of the fifth Manu, Raivata: / Mahāpurāṇa, Sambhāvya, Pratyaṅga, Parahan, Śuci,

1.172.s:
calabindurnirāmitraḥ ketuśṛṃgo dṛḍhavrataḥ ..
raivatasya manoḥ putrā ṛṣayastasya vacmi te .. 2 ..
vedaśrutirvedabāhurūrdhvabāhuryajustathā ..
hiraṇyaromā parjanyaḥ satyanetrastathaiva ca .. 3 ..
ābhūtarājasaścaiva tathā devāḥ sumedhasaḥ ..
vaikuṇṭhāścāmṛtāścaiva catvāro devatāgaṇāḥ .. 4 ..
ekaikasmingaṇe devāḥ kathitāstu caturdaśa ..
teṣāmindro vibhurnāma loke vikhyātavikramaḥ .. 5 ..
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..
teṣāmasīnmahātejāḥ śaṃbhurnāma maheśvaraḥ .. 6 ..
brahmalokena maraṇaṃ vṛtaṃ yena pitāmahāt ..
sa kadācinmahākāyaṃ samudrajalacāriṇam .. 7 ..
haṃsaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva jagrāha tañcārohati durmatiḥ ..
ārūḍhamātramādāya brahmalokaṃ jagāma saḥ ..
haṃsarūpeṇa tatraiva jaghāna bhagavānhariḥ .. 8 ..
1.172.d:
चलबिन्दुर्निरामित्रः केतुशृंगो दृढव्रतः ॥
रैवतस्य मनोः पुत्रा ऋषयस्तस्य वच्मि ते ॥ 2 ॥
वेदश्रुतिर्वेदबाहुरूर्ध्वबाहुर्यजुस्तथा ॥
हिरण्यरोमा पर्जन्यः सत्यनेत्रस्तथैव च ॥ 3 ॥
आभूतराजसश्चैव तथा देवाः सुमेधसः ॥
वैकुण्ठाश्चामृताश्चैव चत्वारो देवतागणाः ॥ 4 ॥
एकैकस्मिन्गणे देवाः कथितास्तु चतुर्दश ॥
तेषामिन्द्रो विभुर्नाम लोके विख्यातविक्रमः ॥ 5 ॥
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥
तेषामसीन्महातेजाः शंभुर्नाम महेश्वरः ॥ 6 ॥
ब्रह्मलोकेन मरणं वृतं येन पितामहात् ॥
स कदाचिन्महाकायं समुद्रजलचारिणम् ॥ 7 ॥
हंसं दृष्ट्वैव जग्राह तञ्चारोहति दुर्मतिः ॥
आरूढमात्रमादाय ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम सः ॥
हंसरूपेण तत्रैव जघान भगवान्हरिः ॥ 8 ॥
1.172.m:
Calabindu, Nirāmitra, Ketuśṛṅga, and Dṛḍhavrata / are the sons of Manu Raivata; I tell you his sages:
Vedaśruti, Vedabāhu, Ūrdhvabāhu, and Yajus, / Hiraṇyaroman, Parjanya, and likewise Satyanetra.
The Ābhūtarajasas and likewise the Sumedhas gods, / the Vaikuṇṭhas and the Amṛtas are the four groups of deities.
Fourteen gods are declared in each single group. / Their Indra, renowned for valour in the world, was named Vibhu.
At that time there were terrible asuras, kinsmen sharing inheritance with him; / among them was a great lord of great splendour named Śambhu,
by whom death [only] through the world of Brahmā was chosen [as a boon] from the Grandfather. / Once, upon seeing an enormous swan moving in the waters of the ocean,
the evil-minded one seized it and mounted it. / As soon as he mounted, taking him, it went to the world of Brahmā; / right there, Lord Hari in the form of a swan killed him.

1.172.s:
evaṃ sa haṃsena hato mahātmā sarveśvareṇāpratimena tena ..
mahābalaḥ parvatamātrakāyaḥ surāntakārī samareṣvajeyaḥ .. 9 ..
1.172.d:
एवं स हंसेन हतो महात्मा सर्वेश्वरेणाप्रतिमेन तेन ॥
महाबलः पर्वतमात्रकायः सुरान्तकारी समरेष्वजेयः ॥ 9 ॥
1.172.m: Thus that great-spirited one, of mighty power, whose body was the measure of a mountain, / an ender of the gods, invincible in battles, was slain with a swan [form] by that peerless Lord of All.

1.173.s:
1.181
.. śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
cākṣuṣasya manoḥ putrānṣaṣṭhasya śṛṇu vāsava ..
ūruḥ pūruḥ śatadyumnaḥ tapasvī satyavāndhṛtiḥ .. 1 ..
1.173.d:
1.181
॥ शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
चाक्षुषस्य मनोः पुत्रान्षष्ठस्य शृणु वासव ॥
ऊरुः पूरुः शतद्युम्नः तपस्वी सत्यवान्धृतिः ॥ 1 ॥
1.173.m: Śāmbarāyaṇī said: / Hear, O Vāsava, the sons of the sixth Manu, Cākṣuṣa: / Ūru, Pūru, Śatadyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavat, Dhṛti,

1.173.s:
agniṣṭudatirātraśca sudyumnaśca tathānagha ..
haviṣmānunnataḥ śrīmānsudhāmā vijayastathā .. 2 ..
1.173.d:
अग्निष्टुदतिरात्रश्च सुद्युम्नश्च तथानघ ॥
हविष्मानुन्नतः श्रीमान्सुधामा विजयस्तथा ॥ 2 ॥
1.173.m: Agniṣṭut, and Atirātra, and Sudyumna, O sinless one. / Haviṣmat, Unnata, the glorious Sudhāman, and Vijaya,

1.173.s:
abhimānaḥ sahiṣṇuśca madhuśrīrṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
āḍhyāḥ prasūtā bhāvyāśca lekhāśca pṛthukāstathā .. 3 ..
1.173.d:
अभिमानः सहिष्णुश्च मधुश्रीरृषयः स्मृताः ॥
आढ्याः प्रसूता भाव्याश्च लेखाश्च पृथुकास्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.173.m: Abhimāna, Sahiṣṇu, and Madhuśrī are remembered as the sages. / The Āḍhyas, the Prasūtas, the Bhāvyas, the Lekhas, and the Pṛthukas,

1.173.s:
aṣṭakāśca gaṇāḥ pañca tadā proktā divaukasām ..
teṣāṃ manojavo nāma babhūvendraḥ pratāpavān .. 4 ..
1.173.d:
अष्टकाश्च गणाः पञ्च तदा प्रोक्ता दिवौकसाम् ॥
तेषां मनोजवो नाम बभूवेन्द्रः प्रतापवान् ॥ 4 ॥
1.173.m: consisting of eight each, are declared to be the five groups of heaven-dwellers at that time. / Their Indra was the valorous one named Manojava.

1.173.s:
āsaṃstasyāsurā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ babhūva nṛpatirmahāmālo balādhikaḥ .. 5 ..
1.173.d:
आसंस्तस्यासुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥
येषां बभूव नृपतिर्महामालो बलाधिकः ॥ 5 ॥
1.173.m: At that time there were terrible asuras, kinsmen sharing inheritance with him, / whose king was Mahāmāla, pre-eminent in power.

1.173.s:
sa kadācidvanaṃ yāto mṛgayāṃ pāpaniścayaḥ ..
tatra candrāṃśusaṃkāśaṃ dadarśāśvaṃ manoharam .. 6 ..
1.173.d:
स कदाचिद्वनं यातो मृगयां पापनिश्चयः ॥
तत्र चन्द्रांशुसंकाशं ददर्शाश्वं मनोहरम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.173.m: Once that one of wicked resolve went to the forest for the hunt. / There he saw a captivating horse resembling a moonbeam.

1.173.s:
tamāruroha durbuddhirmṛgāghātacikīrṣayā ..
tamārūḍhaṃ samādāya tadā vegātturaṅgamaḥ .. 7 ..
1.173.d:
तमारुरोह दुर्बुद्धिर्मृगाघातचिकीर्षया ॥
तमारूढं समादाय तदा वेगात्तुरङ्गमः ॥ 7 ॥
1.173.m: Wishing to strike down deer, the foolish-minded one mounted it. / Taking him who had mounted, the steed then swiftly

1.173.s:
gatvā pāre samudrasya cikṣepopari durmatim ..
kṣiptamātraḥ sa durbuddhiḥ pavanenāpavāhitaḥ .. 8 ..
1.173.d:
गत्वा पारे समुद्रस्य चिक्षेपोपरि दुर्मतिम् ॥
क्षिप्तमात्रः स दुर्बुद्धिः पवनेनापवाहितः ॥ 8 ॥
1.173.m: went to the other shore of the ocean and hurled the evil-minded one aloft. / As soon as he was thrown, that foolish-minded one was blown away by the wind;

1.173.s:
anāsāditatoyaśca pavanena sa tṛhyate ..
adyāpi sumahātejā lokālokasya bāhyataḥ .. 9 ..
1.173.d:
अनासादिततोयश्च पवनेन स तृह्यते ॥
अद्यापि सुमहातेजा लोकालोकस्य बाह्यतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.173.m: not reaching water, he is tossed about by the wind / even today, though of very great splendour, outside the Lokāloka [mountain].

1.173.s:
amṛtyuvaradānena sa tu pāpaḥ svayambhuvaḥ ..
vāyumārgaṃ samāśritya na tu prāṇairviyujyate .. 1.181.10 ..
1.173.d:
अमृत्युवरदानेन स तु पापः स्वयम्भुवः ॥
वायुमार्गं समाश्रित्य न तु प्राणैर्वियुज्यते ॥ 1.181.10 ॥
1.173.m: Because of the boon of deathlessness granted by Svayambhū, that wicked one, / having entered the path of the wind, is not separated from his vital breaths.

1.173.s:
evaṃ sa ghoro varadānadarpādamṛtyurastīti kṛtāparādhaḥ ..
devadvijānāṃ hayarūpadhārī cikṣepa viṣṇuḥ pavanapravāhe .. 11 ..
1.182
.. śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
athānyasya bhaviṣyasya manovairvasvatasya ca ..
saptamasya pravakṣyāmi tava putrānyaśasvinaḥ..1..
ikṣvākuratha nābhāgo viṣṇuḥ śaryātireva ca ..
avṛdhyatustathā prāṃśurmahātmā diṣṭa eva ca .. 2 ..
karūṣaśca pṛthudhraśca sudyumnaśca manoḥ sutāḥ ..
atrirvasiṣṭho bhagavāñjamadagniśca kaśyapaḥ .. 3 ..
gautamaśca bharadvājo viśvāmitro'tha saptamaḥ ..
devā hyekonapañcāśanmarutaḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 4 ..
dvāvaśvinau vinirdiṣṭau viśvedevāstathā daśa ..
daśaivāṅgiraso devā hyevaṃ devagaṇā nava .. 5 ..
yeṣāṃ śakrastu mojaṃbī nāmnā śatrukṣayaṅkaraḥ ..
ghorāstathāpi ye tvāsandaityā dāyādabāndhavāḥ .. 6 ..
1.173.d:
एवं स घोरो वरदानदर्पादमृत्युरस्तीति कृतापराधः ॥
देवद्विजानां हयरूपधारी चिक्षेप विष्णुः पवनप्रवाहे ॥ 11 ॥
1.182
॥ शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
अथान्यस्य भविष्यस्य मनोवैर्वस्वतस्य च ॥
सप्तमस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि तव पुत्रान्यशस्विनः॥1॥
इक्ष्वाकुरथ नाभागो विष्णुः शर्यातिरेव च ॥
अवृध्यतुस्तथा प्रांशुर्महात्मा दिष्ट एव च ॥ 2 ॥
करूषश्च पृथुध्रश्च सुद्युम्नश्च मनोः सुताः ॥
अत्रिर्वसिष्ठो भगवाञ्जमदग्निश्च कश्यपः ॥ 3 ॥
गौतमश्च भरद्वाजो विश्वामित्रोऽथ सप्तमः ॥
देवा ह्येकोनपञ्चाशन्मरुतः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 4 ॥
द्वावश्विनौ विनिर्दिष्टौ विश्वेदेवास्तथा दश ॥
दशैवाङ्गिरसो देवा ह्येवं देवगणा नव ॥ 5 ॥
येषां शक्रस्तु मोजंबी नाम्ना शत्रुक्षयङ्करः ॥
घोरास्तथापि ये त्वासन्दैत्या दायादबान्धवाः ॥ 6 ॥
1.173.m:
Thus that terrible one, proud on account of the boon, who committed offences against the gods and twice-born / saying 'I am deathless', was cast into the current of the wind by Viṣṇu wearing the form of a horse.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said: / Now I shall tell you the renowned sons of the other, / future seventh Manu, Vaivasvata:
Ikṣvāku, then Nābhāga, Viṣṇu, and Śaryāti, / Avṛdhyatu, as well as Prāṃśu, and the great-spirited Diṣṭa,
Karūṣa, Pṛthudhra, and Sudyumna are the sons of the Manu. / Atri, the venerable Vasiṣṭha, Jamadagni, Kaśyapa,
Gautama, Bharadvāja, and Viśvāmitra the seventh. / The gods, the Maruts, are proclaimed forty-nine;
the two Aśvins are designated, as well as the ten Viśvedevas, / and ten are the Āṅgirasa gods; thus there are nine groups of gods,
whose Śakra, the destroyer of foes, is named Mojaṃbī. / There were also terrible Daityas, kinsmen sharing inheritance with them;

1.173.s:
teṣāṃ babhūva nṛpatirhiraṇyākṣo mahābalaḥ ..
nṛvarāheṇa vapuṣā taṃ jaghāna hariḥ purā ..7..
daityeśvaraṃ taṃ surasaṃghabhīmaṃ mahābalaṃ parvatamātrakāyam ..
jaghāna cakreṇa hariḥ prasahya rūpaṃ samāsthāya varāhaśīrṣam ..8..
1.173.d:
तेषां बभूव नृपतिर्हिरण्याक्षो महाबलः ॥
नृवराहेण वपुषा तं जघान हरिः पुरा ॥7॥
दैत्येश्वरं तं सुरसंघभीमं महाबलं पर्वतमात्रकायम् ॥
जघान चक्रेण हरिः प्रसह्य रूपं समास्थाय वराहशीर्षम् ॥8॥
1.173.m:
their king was the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa. / In ancient times, Hari killed him with the body of a man-boar.
Assuming a boar-headed form, Hari with his discus forcibly slew / that lord of the Daityas, terrible to the host of gods, of great strength, whose body was the measure of a mountain.

1.173.s:
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde saptamavaivasvatamanvantaravarṇanannāma dvyaśītyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. ..182 ..
1.183
śakra uvāca ..
asminkalpe mahābhāge bhaviṣyā manavastu ye ..
teṣāṃ putrānnṛṣīndevāñchakra dāyādabāndhavān .. 1 ..
tasya ghātaṃ tathā kṛṣṇātsarvametatprakīrtaya ..
sarvajñakalpā bhavatī divyajñānā matā mama .. 2 ..
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
aṣṭamasya bhaviṣyasya sāvarṇasya manoḥ sutān ..
kathayiṣyāmi te śakra mahābalaparākramān .. 3 ..
vijayaścāvarīvāṃśca nirdohassatyavākkṛtiḥ ..
cariṣṇuścāpyadhṛṣṇuśca vācaḥ samatireva ca .. 4 ..
sāvarṇasya manoḥ putrānṛṣīṃścaiva nibodha me ..
aśvatthāmā kṛpo vyāso gālavo dīptimānatha .. 5 ..
ṛṣyaśṛṅgastathā rāma ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
sutapā amṛtābhāśca ātreyāśca gaṇāstrayaḥ .. 6 ..
1.173.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे सप्तमवैवस्वतमन्वन्तरवर्णनन्नाम द्व्यशीत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥182 ॥
1.183
शक्र उवाच ॥
अस्मिन्कल्पे महाभागे भविष्या मनवस्तु ये ॥
तेषां पुत्रान्नृषीन्देवाञ्छक्र दायादबान्धवान् ॥ 1 ॥
तस्य घातं तथा कृष्णात्सर्वमेतत्प्रकीर्तय ॥
सर्वज्ञकल्पा भवती दिव्यज्ञाना मता मम ॥ 2 ॥
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
अष्टमस्य भविष्यस्य सावर्णस्य मनोः सुतान् ॥
कथयिष्यामि ते शक्र महाबलपराक्रमान् ॥ 3 ॥
विजयश्चावरीवांश्च निर्दोहस्सत्यवाक्कृतिः ॥
चरिष्णुश्चाप्यधृष्णुश्च वाचः समतिरेव च ॥ 4 ॥
सावर्णस्य मनोः पुत्रानृषींश्चैव निबोध मे ॥
अश्वत्थामा कृपो व्यासो गालवो दीप्तिमानथ ॥ 5 ॥
ऋष्यशृङ्गस्तथा राम ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
सुतपा अमृताभाश्च आत्रेयाश्च गणास्त्रयः ॥ 6 ॥
1.173.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Seventh Vaivasvata Manvantara', in the first book of the holy Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
1.183
Śakra said:
Those Manus who will be in this aeon, O blessed lady— / their sons, sages, gods, heirs, and kinsmen, [and likewise]
the destruction of them by Kṛṣṇa: tell all of this! / You are almost omniscient, possessed of divine knowledge, in my view.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
I will tell you of the sons of the eighth future Manu, / Sāvarṇa, O Śakra—sons of great strength and valor:
Vijaya, Varīvas, Nirdoha, Satyavāc, Kṛti, / Cariṣṇu, Adhṛṣṇu, Vācas, and Samati.
Hear from me the sons of Manu Sāvarṇa, and also the sages: / Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, Vyāsa, Gālava, and Dīptimat,
Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, and Rāma—these are proclaimed as the sages. / The Sutapases, the Amṛtābhas, and the Ātreyas are the three classes [of gods],

1.173.s:
sarve viṃśatibhirdevagaṇairyuktā mahātmanām ..
yeṣāmindro bhaviṣyastu balirdānavasattamaḥ .. 7..
tvatkṛte devadevena baddho yastridaśeśvaraḥ ..
dāyādā bāndhavāstasya na bhaviṣyanti vāsava .. 8 ..
śakratvaṃ tena kartavyaṃ manvantaramakaṇṭakam ..
devadevakaranyastaṃ dānameta nmahāsuraḥ .. 9 ..
trailokyarājā bhavati sāvarṇasyāntare manoḥ .. ..
tasminmanvantare prāpte himaśailālayo balī .. 1.183.10 ..
bhaviṣyati durācāro nānolo nāma rākṣasaḥ ..
brahmalabdhavaro raudrastrailokyotsādane rataḥ .. 11 ..
taṃ vadhiṣyati dharmātmā viṣṇurgaruḍavāhanaḥ ..
cakreṇa śatadhāreṇa jagatāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 12 ..
daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ vikaṭograveṣaṃ nīlāñjanābhaṃ bhayadaṃ triloke ..
cakreṇa devaḥ pravidārya kartā lokaṃ samagraṃ bhayaviprayuktam .. 13 ..
1.173.d:
सर्वे विंशतिभिर्देवगणैर्युक्ता महात्मनाम् ॥
येषामिन्द्रो भविष्यस्तु बलिर्दानवसत्तमः ॥ 7॥
त्वत्कृते देवदेवेन बद्धो यस्त्रिदशेश्वरः ॥
दायादा बान्धवास्तस्य न भविष्यन्ति वासव ॥ 8 ॥
शक्रत्वं तेन कर्तव्यं मन्वन्तरमकण्टकम् ॥
देवदेवकरन्यस्तं दानमेत न्महासुरः ॥ 9 ॥
त्रैलोक्यराजा भवति सावर्णस्यान्तरे मनोः ॥ ॥
तस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे प्राप्ते हिमशैलालयो बली ॥ 1.183.10 ॥
भविष्यति दुराचारो नानोलो नाम राक्षसः ॥
ब्रह्मलब्धवरो रौद्रस्त्रैलोक्योत्सादने रतः ॥ 11 ॥
तं वधिष्यति धर्मात्मा विष्णुर्गरुडवाहनः ॥
चक्रेण शतधारेण जगतां हितकाम्यया ॥ 12 ॥
दंष्ट्राकरालं विकटोग्रवेषं नीलाञ्जनाभं भयदं त्रिलोके ॥
चक्रेण देवः प्रविदार्य कर्ता लोकं समग्रं भयविप्रयुक्तम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.173.m:
all composed of twenty divine beings of great soul; / their future Indra will be Bali, the best of the Dānavas,
the lord of the gods who was bound by the God of gods for your sake. / He shall have no heirs or kinsmen, O Vāsava.
The role of Indra, free from thorns, is to be held by him throughout that manvantara. / That great Asura made a gift placed in the hands of the God of gods;
he will become the king of the three worlds during the period of Manu Sāvarṇa. / When that manvantara arrives, a mighty,
evil-doing rākṣasa named Nānola, residing in the Snowy Mountains, / having obtained a boon from Brahmā, terrifying and intent on destroying the three worlds, will arise.
Viṣṇu, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, the righteous-souled one, / will slay him with his hundred-edged discus, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
Tearing apart with his discus that [demon] terrible with fangs, monstrous and dreadful in guise, / shining like dark collyrium and striking terror in the three worlds, the god will make the whole world free from fear.

1.173.s:
1.184
śāṃbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
brahmaputrasya tu manornavamasya sutāñchṛṇu ..
dhṛtiketurdīptiketuḥ pañcahasto nirākṛtiḥ .. 1 ..
pṛthuśravā bṛhaddyumna ṛcīko bṛhatāṃ gaṇaḥ ..
brahmaputrasya te putrā ṛṣayaśca nibodha me .. 2 ..
medhātithirdyutiścaiva savano vasureva ca ..
jyotiṣmānhavyasatyau ca ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 3 ..
pārā marīcigarbhāśca svadharmāṇaśca te trayaḥ ..
gaṇā dvādaśakāḥ proktā yeṣāmindro bhaviṣyati .. 4 ..
vibhurnāma mahātejāḥ sarvadeveśvaro valī ..
dāyādā bāndhavāstasya ye bhaviṣyanti dhārmikāḥ .. 5 ..
kālakakṣa iti khyātāsteṣāṃ rājā bhaviṣyati ..
tasminmanvantare rājā vasunābho bhaviṣyati..6..
putrastu bhāvatā tasya vāsudevo mahīpatiḥ ..
cakravartī mahātejāḥ padmanābha iti śrutaḥ .. 7 ..
1.173.d:
1.184
शांबरायण्युवाच ॥
ब्रह्मपुत्रस्य तु मनोर्नवमस्य सुताञ्छृणु ॥
धृतिकेतुर्दीप्तिकेतुः पञ्चहस्तो निराकृतिः ॥ 1 ॥
पृथुश्रवा बृहद्द्युम्न ऋचीको बृहतां गणः ॥
ब्रह्मपुत्रस्य ते पुत्रा ऋषयश्च निबोध मे ॥ 2 ॥
मेधातिथिर्द्युतिश्चैव सवनो वसुरेव च ॥
ज्योतिष्मान्हव्यसत्यौ च ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 3 ॥
पारा मरीचिगर्भाश्च स्वधर्माणश्च ते त्रयः ॥
गणा द्वादशकाः प्रोक्ता येषामिन्द्रो भविष्यति ॥ 4 ॥
विभुर्नाम महातेजाः सर्वदेवेश्वरो वली ॥
दायादा बान्धवास्तस्य ये भविष्यन्ति धार्मिकाः ॥ 5 ॥
कालकक्ष इति ख्यातास्तेषां राजा भविष्यति ॥
तस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे राजा वसुनाभो भविष्यति॥6॥
पुत्रस्तु भावता तस्य वासुदेवो महीपतिः ॥
चक्रवर्ती महातेजाः पद्मनाभ इति श्रुतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.173.m:
1.184
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear now of the sons of the ninth Manu, the son of Brahmā: / Dhṛtiketu, Dīptiketu, Pañcahasta, Nirākṛti,
Pṛthuśravas, Bṛhaddyumna, Ṛcīka, and Bṛhatgaṇa. / Those are the sons of the son of Brahmā; and hear from me the sages:
Medhātithi, Dyuti, Savana, and Vasu, / Jyotiṣmat, Havya, and Satya are proclaimed as the sages.
The Pāras, the Marīcigarbhas, and the Svadharmans—these three / classes of gods are declared to consist of twelve each; and their Indra will be
the mighty Vibhu of great splendor, lord of all the gods. / His righteous kinsmen and heirs who will arise
will have a king known as Kālakākṣa. / In that manvantara, there will be a king named Vasunābha;
his son, by his disposition, will be King Vāsudeva, / an emperor of great splendor, known as Padmanābha.

1.173.s:
devāsure tu saṃgrāme kālakākṣaṃ raṇotkaṭam ..
naravadhyaṃ mahātejāḥ padmanābho vadhiṣyati.. 8 ..
śareṇa jāmbūnadabhūṣitena brahmāstrayuktena raṇapracaṇḍam..
hatvāsuraṃ kālasamaprabhāvaṃ rājā sa lokasya bhayaṃ nihantā .. 9 .. ..
1.185
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
dharmaputrasya tu manordaśamasya sutāñchṛṇu ..
sukṣetra uttamaujāśca bhūriśoṇaśca vīryavān .. 1 ..
śatānīko nimirmitro vṛṣaseno jayadrathaḥ ..
bhūridyumnaḥ suvarmā ca dharmaputramanoḥ sutāḥ .. 2 ..
āpomūrtirhaviṣmāṃśca sṛtikiścāvyayastathā ..
nābhāgaḥ pramitaścaiva saurabhā ṛṣayastathā .. 3 ..
prāṇākhyāḥ śatasaṃkhyāśca devatānāṃ gaṇāstathā ..
bhavitā tasya bhavitā śāntirindraḥ pratāpavān .. 4 ..
dāyādābāndhavāstasya bhaviṣyantyasurāśca ye ..
teṣāṃ ca bhavitā rājā bālī nāma mahāsuraḥ .. 5 ..
1.173.d:
देवासुरे तु संग्रामे कालकाक्षं रणोत्कटम् ॥
नरवध्यं महातेजाः पद्मनाभो वधिष्यति॥ 8 ॥
शरेण जाम्बूनदभूषितेन ब्रह्मास्त्रयुक्तेन रणप्रचण्डम्॥
हत्वासुरं कालसमप्रभावं राजा स लोकस्य भयं निहन्ता ॥ 9 ॥ ॥
1.185
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
धर्मपुत्रस्य तु मनोर्दशमस्य सुताञ्छृणु ॥
सुक्षेत्र उत्तमौजाश्च भूरिशोणश्च वीर्यवान् ॥ 1 ॥
शतानीको निमिर्मित्रो वृषसेनो जयद्रथः ॥
भूरिद्युम्नः सुवर्मा च धर्मपुत्रमनोः सुताः ॥ 2 ॥
आपोमूर्तिर्हविष्मांश्च सृतिकिश्चाव्ययस्तथा ॥
नाभागः प्रमितश्चैव सौरभा ऋषयस्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
प्राणाख्याः शतसंख्याश्च देवतानां गणास्तथा ॥
भविता तस्य भविता शान्तिरिन्द्रः प्रतापवान् ॥ 4 ॥
दायादाबान्धवास्तस्य भविष्यन्त्यसुराश्च ये ॥
तेषां च भविता राजा बाली नाम महासुरः ॥ 5 ॥
1.173.m:
In the war between the gods and the Asuras, the mighty Padmanābha / will slay Kālakākṣa, fierce in battle, who could only be killed by a man.
Having slain with a gold-adorned arrow charged with the weapon of Brahmā / that demon fierce in battle and possessing the might of Death, that king will dispel the fear of the world.
1.185
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear now of the sons of the tenth Manu, the son of Dharma: / Sukṣetra, Uttamaujas, and the heroic Bhūriśoṇa,
Śatānīka, Nimi, Mitra, Vṛṣasena, Jayadratha, / Bhūridyumna, and Suvarman—the sons of Manu, the son of Dharma.
Āpomūrti, Haviṣmat, Sṛtiki, and the changeless one, / Nābhāga, Pramita, and Saurabha are the sages;
and the classes of deities, numbering a hundred, are named Prāṇas. / His glorious Indra will be Śānti.
His heirs and kinsmen, who will be Asuras, / will have a king, a great Asura named Bālī.

1.173.s:
dyotayiṣyati taṃ viṣṇurgadayā bhīmavegayā ..
devāsure tu saṃgrāme devānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 6 ..
gadānipātābhihate surendre mahābale devavareṇa tena ..
trailokyametadbhavitā samagraṃ vinaṣṭadoṣaṃ suraviprajuṣṭam .. 7 ..
1.173.d:
द्योतयिष्यति तं विष्णुर्गदया भीमवेगया ॥
देवासुरे तु संग्रामे देवानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 6 ॥
गदानिपाताभिहते सुरेन्द्रे महाबले देववरेण तेन ॥
त्रैलोक्यमेतद्भविता समग्रं विनष्टदोषं सुरविप्रजुष्टम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.173.m:
Viṣṇu will strike him down with his mace of terrible speed / in the war between the gods and the Asuras, desiring the welfare of the gods.
When that lord of the Asuras of great strength is struck down by the blow of the mace by that foremost of gods, / this entire threefold world will be free of fault, enjoyed by gods and brahmins.

1.173.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde śakraśāmbarāyaṇīsaṃvāde daśamadharmaputramanvantvavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcāśītyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 185 ..
1.173.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे शक्रशाम्बरायणीसंवादे दशमधर्मपुत्रमन्वन्त्ववर्णनं नाम पञ्चाशीत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 185 ॥
1.173.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Tenth Dharmaputra Manvantara', in the first book of the holy Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the conversation between Śakra and Śāmbarāyaṇī.

1.186

dharmanityānmahābhāgāṃstrailokyasya parāyaṇān .. 1 ..
1.174.d:
1.186
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
रुद्रपुत्रस्य ते पुत्रान्वक्ष्याम्येकादशस्य तु ॥
धर्मनित्यान्महाभागांस्त्रैलोक्यस्य परायणान् ॥ 1 ॥
1.174.m:
1.186
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
I will tell you of the sons of the eleventh Manu, the son of Rudra: / ever devoted to dharma, highly blessed, refuges of the three worlds:

1.174.s:
sarvartugaḥ suśarmā ca senānīkaḥ puroddhataḥ ..
kṣemadhanvā dṛḍhendraśca cādarśaḥ puṇḍrakastathā ..2..
1.174.d:
सर्वर्तुगः सुशर्मा च सेनानीकः पुरोद्धतः ॥
क्षेमधन्वा दृढेन्द्रश्च चादर्शः पुण्ड्रकस्तथा ॥2॥
1.174.m: Sarvartuga, Suśarman, Senānīka, Puroddhata, / Kṣemadhanvan, Dṛḍhendra, Cādarśa, and Puṇḍraka.

1.174.s:
manuputrāḥ smṛtā hyete ṛṣayaśca nibodha me..
haviṣmāṃśca vapuṣmāṃśca varuṇābdhiśca nistaraḥ ..3..
1.174.d:
मनुपुत्राः स्मृता ह्येते ऋषयश्च निबोध मे॥
हविष्मांश्च वपुष्मांश्च वरुणाब्धिश्च निस्तरः ॥3॥
1.174.m: These are remembered as the sons of Manu; and hear from me the sages: / Haviṣmat, Vapuṣmat, Varuṇābdhi, Nistara,

1.174.s:
viṣṇuścaivāgnitejāśca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ ..
nirmathyā rathayaścaiva kāmagāśca gaṇāstrayaḥ .. 4 ..
1.174.d:
विष्णुश्चैवाग्नितेजाश्च ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥
निर्मथ्या रथयश्चैव कामगाश्च गणास्त्रयः ॥ 4 ॥
1.174.m: Viṣṇu, and Agnitejas—these are proclaimed as the seven sages. / The Nirmathyas, the Rathayas, and the Kāmagas are the three classes [of gods];

1.174.s:
triṃśattriṃśattathā devā ekaikasmingaṇe smṛtāḥ ..
teṣāmindro vṛṣo nāma bhaviṣyati mahābalaḥ .. 5 ..
1.174.d:
त्रिंशत्त्रिंशत्तथा देवा एकैकस्मिन्गणे स्मृताः ॥
तेषामिन्द्रो वृषो नाम भविष्यति महाबलः ॥ 5 ॥
1.174.m: thirty gods are recorded in each single class. / Their Indra will be the very powerful one named Vṛṣa.

1.174.s:
dāyādā bāndhavāścaiva bhaviṣyanti surāśca ye ..
teṣāṃ tu bhavitā rājā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān .. 6 ..
1.174.d:
दायादा बान्धवाश्चैव भविष्यन्ति सुराश्च ये ॥
तेषां तु भविता राजा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् ॥ 6 ॥
1.174.m: His heirs and kinsmen will be Asuras; / their king will be the powerful Daśagrīva.

1.174.s:
ghātayiṣyati taṃ viṣṇustraiṇaṃ rūpamupāśritaḥ ..
śūlāgreṇa vinirbhidya raṇe devā'sure tadā .. 7 ..
1.174.d:
घातयिष्यति तं विष्णुस्त्रैणं रूपमुपाश्रितः ॥
शूलाग्रेण विनिर्भिद्य रणे देवाऽसुरे तदा ॥ 7 ॥
1.174.m: Viṣṇu, having assumed a female form, will slay him, / piercing him with the tip of a trident then in the war between the gods and the Asuras.

1.174.s:
tamavadhyaṃ durādharṣaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ svayambhuvā ..
gataṃ tapaḥprabhāve sā viṣṇustaṃ ghātayiṣyati .. 8 ..
1.174.d:
तमवध्यं दुराधर्षं पुरुषाणां स्वयम्भुवा ॥
गतं तपःप्रभावे सा विष्णुस्तं घातयिष्यति ॥ 8 ॥
1.174.m: Him who was invincible to men, made invulnerable by the Self-born One, / Viṣṇu, in that [female form], will slay, [for] his power of asceticism was exhausted.

1.174.s:
nīlotpalābhaṃ tapanīyavarṇaṃ suvṛttajānūruyugaṃ svarūpam ..
rūpaṃ striyāṃścārutaraṃ sa kṛtvā surārimugraṃ sahasā'rihantā .. 9..
1.187
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
manostvaṃ dakṣaputrasya dvādaśasyātmajāñchṛṇu ..
devavānupadevaśca devaśreṣṭho vidūrathaḥ..1..
mitravānmitradevaśca mitrasenaśca vīryavān..
mitrabāhuḥ suvarcāśca dakṣaputramanoḥ sutāḥ .. 2 ..
sattamo dyaurdyutiścaiva tapanaḥ sutapāstathā ..
taporatistapasvī ca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ .. 3 ..
suśarmāṇaḥ sutapaso haritā rohitāstathā ..
sutārākhyā gaṇāḥ pañca pratyekaṃ daśako guṇaḥ .. 4 ..
ṛtadhāmā ca dharmātmā teṣāmindraḥ pratāpavān ..
dāyādā bāndhavāstasya bhaviṣyantyasurāśca ye ..5..
teṣāṃ ca bhavitā rājā narako nāma nāmataḥ ..
strīpuṃsoḥ sattvavadhyaśca varadānātsvayambhuvaḥ ..6 ..
harirnapuṃsako bhūtvā ghātayiṣyati taṃ tadā ..7..
1.174.d:
नीलोत्पलाभं तपनीयवर्णं सुवृत्तजानूरुयुगं स्वरूपम् ॥
रूपं स्त्रियांश्चारुतरं स कृत्वा सुरारिमुग्रं सहसाऽरिहन्ता ॥ 9॥
1.187
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
मनोस्त्वं दक्षपुत्रस्य द्वादशस्यात्मजाञ्छृणु ॥
देववानुपदेवश्च देवश्रेष्ठो विदूरथः॥1॥
मित्रवान्मित्रदेवश्च मित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान्॥
मित्रबाहुः सुवर्चाश्च दक्षपुत्रमनोः सुताः ॥ 2 ॥
सत्तमो द्यौर्द्युतिश्चैव तपनः सुतपास्तथा ॥
तपोरतिस्तपस्वी च ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥ 3 ॥
सुशर्माणः सुतपसो हरिता रोहितास्तथा ॥
सुताराख्या गणाः पञ्च प्रत्येकं दशको गुणः ॥ 4 ॥
ऋतधामा च धर्मात्मा तेषामिन्द्रः प्रतापवान् ॥
दायादा बान्धवास्तस्य भविष्यन्त्यसुराश्च ये ॥5॥
तेषां च भविता राजा नरको नाम नामतः ॥
स्त्रीपुंसोः सत्त्ववध्यश्च वरदानात्स्वयम्भुवः ॥6 ॥
हरिर्नपुंसको भूत्वा घातयिष्यति तं तदा ॥7॥
1.174.m:
With the lustre of a blue lotus, the colour of molten gold, his own form having beautifully rounded pairs of knees and thighs, / having made a most beautiful female form, that slayer of foes will suddenly [slay] that fierce enemy of the gods.
1.187
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear from me the sons of the twelfth Manu, the son of Dakṣa: / Devavān, Upadeva, Devaśreṣṭha, Vidūratha,
Mitravān, Mitradeva, and the powerful Mitrasena, / Mitrabāhu, and Suvarcas—these are the sons of Manu, the son of Dakṣa.
Sattama, Dyaus, Dyuti, Tapana, Sutapas, / Taporati, and Tapasvin are proclaimed as the seven sages.
The Suśarmans, the Sutapases, the Haritas, the Rohitas, / and those called the Sutāras are the five classes [of gods], each having a group of ten.
And their Indra will be the righteous, majestic Ṛtadhāman. / Those who will be his heirs, kinsmen, and the asuras—
of them there will be a king named Naraka by name; / and by the granting of a boon by the Self-born, he cannot be slain by female or male beings.
Hari, having assumed a neuter form, will then cause him to be slain.

1.174.s:
devāntakaṃ kālasamaprabhāvaṃ mahāsuraṃ klībavapurmahātmā ..
nihatya taṃ lokamidaṃ samagraṃ bhītyā vihīnaṃ bhagavānsa kartā .. 8 ..
1.188
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
trayodaśasya raucyasya manoḥ putrannibodha me ..
citraseno vicitraśca nayo dharmabhṛto dhṛtiḥ ..1..
sunetro vṛkṣavṛddhiśca sunayo dharmayo dṛḍhaḥ ..
raucyasyaite manoḥ putrāḥ śṛṇuṣva ṛṣayo mama..2..
dhṛtimānavyayaścaiva niḥprakopo nirutsukaḥ ..
nirmāṇastattvadarśī ca davayāyata kīrtitāḥ ..3..
sutrāmāṇaḥ sudharmāṇaḥ śubhakarmāṇa eva ca ..
ete śakra tadā proktā devatānāṃ gaṇāstrayaḥ..4..
ekaikasmingaṇe devā ekādaśa tadā śubhāḥ..
devendraśca tadā teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati bṛhaspatiḥ .. 5 ..
dāyādā bāndhadāstasya ye bhaviṣyanti vāsava ..
ṭiṭṭibho nāma duṣṭātmā teṣāṃ rājā bhaviṣyati .. 6 ..
1.174.d:
देवान्तकं कालसमप्रभावं महासुरं क्लीबवपुर्महात्मा ॥
निहत्य तं लोकमिदं समग्रं भीत्या विहीनं भगवान्स कर्ता ॥ 8 ॥
1.188
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
त्रयोदशस्य रौच्यस्य मनोः पुत्रन्निबोध मे ॥
चित्रसेनो विचित्रश्च नयो धर्मभृतो धृतिः ॥1॥
सुनेत्रो वृक्षवृद्धिश्च सुनयो धर्मयो दृढः ॥
रौच्यस्यैते मनोः पुत्राः शृणुष्व ऋषयो मम॥2॥
धृतिमानव्ययश्चैव निःप्रकोपो निरुत्सुकः ॥
निर्माणस्तत्त्वदर्शी च दवयायत कीर्तिताः ॥3॥
सुत्रामाणः सुधर्माणः शुभकर्माण एव च ॥
एते शक्र तदा प्रोक्ता देवतानां गणास्त्रयः॥4॥
एकैकस्मिन्गणे देवा एकादश तदा शुभाः॥
देवेन्द्रश्च तदा तेषां भविष्यति बृहस्पतिः ॥ 5 ॥
दायादा बान्धदास्तस्य ये भविष्यन्ति वासव ॥
टिट्टिभो नाम दुष्टात्मा तेषां राजा भविष्यति ॥ 6 ॥
1.174.m:
Having slain that destroyer of gods, that great asura of power equal to Death, with a eunuch body, / that exalted, noble Lord will make this entire world free from fear.
1.188
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Learn from me the sons of the thirteenth Manu, Raucya: / Citrasena, Vicitra, Naya, Dharmabhṛt, Dhṛti,
Sunetra, Vṛkṣavṛddhi, Sunaya, Dharmaya, and Dṛḍha. / These are the sons of the Manu Raucya; hear my sages [of this period]:
Dhṛtimān, Avyaya, Niḥprakopa, Nirutsuka, / Nirmāṇa, Tattvadarśin, and Davayāyata are proclaimed.
The Sutrāmāṇas, the Sudharmāṇas, and the Śubhakarmāṇas— / these, O Śakra, are then declared to be the three classes of deities.
In each class there are then eleven auspicious gods; / and their lord of gods then will be Bṛhaspati.
Those who will be his heirs and kinsmen, O Vāsava— / of them, an evil-minded one named Ṭiṭṭibha will be king.

1.174.s:
tasyāpi bhavitā mṛtyurdevadevājjanārdanāt ..
māyūreṇa ca rūpeṇa satataṃ pannagāśinā .. 7 ..
sa tu devāsure yuddhe sarparūpeṇa durmatiḥ ..
yuddhaṃ kṛtvā nirutsāhānsarvāndevagaṇāṃstathā .. 8 ..
niṣprayatneṣu deveṣu māyūraṃ rūpamāśritaḥ..
ghātayiṣyati taṃ duṣṭaṃ devadevo janārdanaḥ..9..
1.174.d:
तस्यापि भविता मृत्युर्देवदेवाज्जनार्दनात् ॥
मायूरेण च रूपेण सततं पन्नगाशिना ॥ 7 ॥
स तु देवासुरे युद्धे सर्परूपेण दुर्मतिः ॥
युद्धं कृत्वा निरुत्साहान्सर्वान्देवगणांस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
निष्प्रयत्नेषु देवेषु मायूरं रूपमाश्रितः॥
घातयिष्यति तं दुष्टं देवदेवो जनार्दनः॥9॥
1.174.m:
His death, too, will come from Janārdana, god of gods, / by means of the form of a peacock, an eater of snakes at all times.
That evil-minded one, having waged war in the form of a serpent in the war between the gods and asuras, / and [having rendered] all the hosts of gods dispirited—
when the gods are exertionless, having taken the form of a peacock, / Janārdana, god of gods, will slay that wicked one.

1.174.s:
mahākalāpaḥ saśikhī mahātmā prabuddhanīlotpalacārukaṇṭhaḥ ..
taṃ dānavaṃ tatra raṇe prasahya hatvā trilokīṃ muditāṃ hi kartā .. 1.188.10 ..
1.189
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
caturdaśasya bhautyasya śṛṇu putrānmanormama ..
taraṅge bhedabhidbudhnyastarasvānugra eva ca .. 1 ..
abhimānī pravīraśca jiṣṇuḥ saṃkrandana stathā ..
tejasvī sulabhaścaiva bhautyasyaite manoḥ sutāḥ .. 2 ..
agnīdhraścātibāhuśca māgadhaśca tathā śuciḥ ..
ajito yuktagośakyaṃ ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ .. 3 ..
cākṣuṣāśca kaniṣṭhāśca pavitrā bhajirāstathā ..
vayovṛddhā devagaṇāḥ pañca proktāstu saptakāḥ .. 4 ..
teṣāmindraḥ śucirnāma tasya dāyādabāndhavāḥ ..
ye bhaviṣyanti bhavitā rājā teṣāṃ mahāsukhaḥ .. 5 ..
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu yuddhaṃ devāsuraṃ tadā ..
bhaviṣyati mahāghoraṃ tasyānte taṃ mahāsuram .. 6 ..
1.174.d:
महाकलापः सशिखी महात्मा प्रबुद्धनीलोत्पलचारुकण्ठः ॥
तं दानवं तत्र रणे प्रसह्य हत्वा त्रिलोकीं मुदितां हि कर्ता ॥ 1.188.10 ॥
1.189
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
चतुर्दशस्य भौत्यस्य शृणु पुत्रान्मनोर्मम ॥
तरङ्गे भेदभिद्बुध्न्यस्तरस्वानुग्र एव च ॥ 1 ॥
अभिमानी प्रवीरश्च जिष्णुः संक्रन्दन स्तथा ॥
तेजस्वी सुलभश्चैव भौत्यस्यैते मनोः सुताः ॥ 2 ॥
अग्नीध्रश्चातिबाहुश्च मागधश्च तथा शुचिः ॥
अजितो युक्तगोशक्यं ऋषयः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥ 3 ॥
चाक्षुषाश्च कनिष्ठाश्च पवित्रा भजिरास्तथा ॥
वयोवृद्धा देवगणाः पञ्च प्रोक्तास्तु सप्तकाः ॥ 4 ॥
तेषामिन्द्रः शुचिर्नाम तस्य दायादबान्धवाः ॥
ये भविष्यन्ति भविता राजा तेषां महासुखः ॥ 5 ॥
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु युद्धं देवासुरं तदा ॥
भविष्यति महाघोरं तस्यान्ते तं महासुरम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.174.m:
Endowed with an expansive plumage, crested, magnificent, with a neck lovely as a blossoming blue lotus, / having forcibly slain that dānava there in battle, he will surely make the three worlds joyful.
1.189
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear the sons of the fourteenth Manu, Bhautya, from me: / Taraṅga, Bhedabhid, Budhnya, Tarasvān, and Ugra,
Abhimānin, Pravīra, Jiṣṇu, and Saṃkrandana, / Tejasvin, and Sulabha—these are the sons of Manu Bhautya.
Agnīdhra, Atibāhu, Māgadha, Śuci, / Ajita, Yuktaga, and Śakya are proclaimed as the seven sages.
The Cākṣuṣas, the Kaniṣṭhas, the Pavitras, and the Bhajiras, / and the Vayovṛddhas are declared to be the five classes of gods, each of seven.
Their Indra will be named Śuci; and those who will be his heirs and kinsmen— / of them, Mahāsukha will be king.
A war between the gods and asuras, lasting a thousand divine years, / will then take place, extremely terrible; at its end, Keśava will slay that great asura

1.174.s:
āsthitaṃ tāmasīṃ māyāṃ ghātayiṣyati keśavaḥ ..
ārūḍhaḥ kuñjaraṃ divyaṃ caratparvatasannibham .. 7 ..
utkhātaparvatasamaṃ cakreṇa madhusūdanaḥ ..
rathasthaṃ taṃ mahādaityaṃ ghātayiṣyati durmatim .. 8 ..
tasminhate vāsavadevaśatrau mahābale kālasamaprabhāve ..
trailokyametadvirujaṃ samantāttadā bhaviṣyatyamalapratāpam .. 9 ..
1.190
śakra uvāca ..
asminmanvantare bhadre garuḍasya ca sambhavaḥ ..
mayā dṛṣṭamatīteṣu kathaṃ garuḍavāhanaḥ .. 1 ..
asurānghātayāmāsa bhaviṣyeṣu tathaiva ca ..
garuḍaṃ tu samāruhya ghātayiṣyati tatkatham .. 2 ..
manvantarānte sarveṣāṃ kṣayo yasmātprakīrtitaḥ ...
tasmādetanmamācakṣva kuśalā hyasi dhārmikā .. 3 ..
śāmbarāyaṇyuvāca ..
devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca pratimanvantaraṃ yathā ..
sambhavastridaśaśreṣṭha gandharvāṇāṃ tathā smṛtaḥ .. 4 ..
1.174.d:
आस्थितं तामसीं मायां घातयिष्यति केशवः ॥
आरूढः कुञ्जरं दिव्यं चरत्पर्वतसन्निभम् ॥ 7 ॥
उत्खातपर्वतसमं चक्रेण मधुसूदनः ॥
रथस्थं तं महादैत्यं घातयिष्यति दुर्मतिम् ॥ 8 ॥
तस्मिन्हते वासवदेवशत्रौ महाबले कालसमप्रभावे ॥
त्रैलोक्यमेतद्विरुजं समन्तात्तदा भविष्यत्यमलप्रतापम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.190
शक्र उवाच ॥
अस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे भद्रे गरुडस्य च सम्भवः ॥
मया दृष्टमतीतेषु कथं गरुडवाहनः ॥ 1 ॥
असुरान्घातयामास भविष्येषु तथैव च ॥
गरुडं तु समारुह्य घातयिष्यति तत्कथम् ॥ 2 ॥
मन्वन्तरान्ते सर्वेषां क्षयो यस्मात्प्रकीर्तितः ॥।
तस्मादेतन्ममाचक्ष्व कुशला ह्यसि धार्मिका ॥ 3 ॥
शाम्बरायण्युवाच ॥
देवानामसुराणां च प्रतिमन्वन्तरं यथा ॥
सम्भवस्त्रिदशश्रेष्ठ गन्धर्वाणां तथा स्मृतः ॥ 4 ॥
1.174.m:
who relies on dark illusory power, / having mounted a divine elephant resembling a moving mountain.
Resembling an uprooted mountain, Madhusūdana with his discus / will slay that evil-minded great daitya who stands upon a chariot.
When that enemy of the gods and of Vāsava, possessing great strength and splendour equal to Death, is slain, / this threefold world will then become free from distress on all sides, with spotless radiance.
1.190
Śakra said:
O gentle lady, the origin of Garuḍa in this manvantara / has been witnessed by me; in the past ones, how, having Garuḍa as his mount,
did he slay the asuras, and likewise in future ones, / having mounted Garuḍa, how will he slay [them]? Tell me that.
Since the destruction of all is declared to occur at the end of a manvantara, / therefore explain this to me, for you are skilled and righteous.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Just as the origin of the gods and the asuras takes place in each manvantara, / O best of the thirty [gods], so is recorded that of the gandharvas,

1.174.s:
nāgānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca yakṣāṇāmatha pakṣiṇām ..
suparṇānāṃ tathā śakra prāṇināmapyaśeṣataḥ .. 5 ..
suparṇānāṃ pradhānastu tatra manvantare tadā ..
sadaiva rājanbhavati garuḍaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ .. 6 ..
vāhanatve tathā tasya deveśasya prapadyate ..
prādurbhāvāṇyathoktāni yathā viṣṇormayā tava .. 7 ..
tathaiva tasya jñeyāni garuḍasya mahātmanaḥ ..
devāstu kṛtakarmāṇaḥ śakra manvantarakṣaye .. 8 ..
tyaktādhikārā gacchanti paralokamitaḥ prabho ..
talliṅgāśca tathā mantrāstaireva sahitāḥ suraiḥ .. 9 ..
samūhaścaiva mantrāṇāṃ devastridaśapūjitaḥ ..
śarīrī brahmasadane sa tu nityaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 1.190.10 ..
1.174.d:
नागानां राक्षसानां च यक्षाणामथ पक्षिणाम् ॥
सुपर्णानां तथा शक्र प्राणिनामप्यशेषतः ॥ 5 ॥
सुपर्णानां प्रधानस्तु तत्र मन्वन्तरे तदा ॥
सदैव राजन्भवति गरुडः पततां वरः ॥ 6 ॥
वाहनत्वे तथा तस्य देवेशस्य प्रपद्यते ॥
प्रादुर्भावाण्यथोक्तानि यथा विष्णोर्मया तव ॥ 7 ॥
तथैव तस्य ज्ञेयानि गरुडस्य महात्मनः ॥
देवास्तु कृतकर्माणः शक्र मन्वन्तरक्षये ॥ 8 ॥
त्यक्ताधिकारा गच्छन्ति परलोकमितः प्रभो ॥
तल्लिङ्गाश्च तथा मन्त्रास्तैरेव सहिताः सुरैः ॥ 9 ॥
समूहश्चैव मन्त्राणां देवस्त्रिदशपूजितः ॥
शरीरी ब्रह्मसदने स तु नित्यः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 1.190.10 ॥
1.174.m:
of the nāgas, of the rākṣasas, of the yakṣas, and then of the birds, / and of the suparṇas, O Śakra, and of living creatures entirely without exception.
The foremost of the suparṇas in that manvantara at that time, / always becomes Garuḍa, O king, best among the winged ones.
In the same way, he attains the status of vehicle to that lord of gods. / Just as the manifestations of Viṣṇu have been declared by me to you,
so also are those of the noble Garuḍa to be known. / But the gods whose duties are accomplished, O Śakra, at the end of a manvantara,
relinquishing their offices, depart from here to the other world, O Lord; / and so do the mantras bearing their marks along with those very gods.
And the collection of mantras is a deity worshipped by the thirty [gods];
embodied in the abode of Brahmā, it is proclaimed to be eternal.

1.174.s:
yāvajjīvati vai brahmā sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ ..
tadā tu puruṣaṃ brahmā devadevaṃ prapadyate .. 11 ..
1.174.d:
यावज्जीवति वै ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ॥
तदा तु पुरुषं ब्रह्मा देवदेवं प्रपद्यते ॥ 11 ॥
1.174.m:
As long as Brahmā, bowed to by all the worlds, lives,
so long does Brahmā take refuge in the Cosmic Person, the god of gods.

1.174.s:
tyaktvā śarīraṃ devo'pi puruṣaṃ pratipadyate ..
puruṣo'pi mahāsṛṣṭiṃ mahābhūtagaṇaṃ tathā .. 12 ..
1.174.d:
त्यक्त्वा शरीरं देवोऽपि पुरुषं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
पुरुषोऽपि महासृष्टिं महाभूतगणं तथा ॥ 12 ॥
1.174.m:
Having cast off his body, the god too attains the Cosmic Person.
The Cosmic Person also [effects] the great creation, as well as the host of primary elements.

1.174.s:
karoti tadvadeveha devaḥ prāgvacchatakrato ..
evaṃ sarvamidaṃ nityaṃ tvanityaṃ vā taveritam .. 13 ..
1.174.d:
करोति तद्वदेवेह देवः प्राग्वच्छतक्रतो ॥
एवं सर्वमिदं नित्यं त्वनित्यं वा तवेरितम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.174.m:
The god here does so just as before, O Śatakratu.
Thus all this has been declared to you as eternal or as non-eternal.

1.174.s:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ ..
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ .. 14 ..
1.174.d:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ॥
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ 14 ॥
1.174.m:
There is no being of the non-existent, nor is there non-being of the existent;
the final truth of both these indeed has been seen by those who perceive reality.

1.174.s:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam ..
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati .. 15 ..
1.174.d:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ 15 ॥
1.174.m:
Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded;
no one is able to effect the destruction of this imperishable [reality].

1.174.s:
tasyāvināśinaḥ śakra sūkṣmasyāpi mahātmanaḥ ..
prādurbhāvasahasrāṇi samatītānyanekaśaḥ .. 16 ..
1.174.d:
तस्याविनाशिनः शक्र सूक्ष्मस्यापि महात्मनः ॥
प्रादुर्भावसहस्राणि समतीतान्यनेकशः ॥ 16 ॥
1.174.m:
Of that indestructible, subtle, and great-souled one, O Śakra,
thousands of manifestations have passed away repeatedly.

1.174.s:
bhūyaścaiva bhaviṣyati nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
vaivasvate'smindeveśa yathā manvantare śubhe .. 17 ..
1.174.d:
भूयश्चैव भविष्यति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
वैवस्वतेऽस्मिन्देवेश यथा मन्वन्तरे शुभे ॥ 17 ॥
1.174.m:
And there will be more; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.
Just as in this auspicious Vaivasvata manvantara, O lord of gods,

1.174.s:
prādurbhāvāni dṛṣṭāni mayā tasya mahātmanaḥ ..
varāhaṃ vāmanaṃ caiva tathā śakra trivikramam .. 18 ..
1.174.d:
प्रादुर्भावानि दृष्टानि मया तस्य महात्मनः ॥
वराहं वामनं चैव तथा शक्र त्रिविक्रमम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.174.m:
manifestations of that great-souled one were seen by me:
the Boar, the Dwarf, and likewise Trivikrama, O Śakra,

1.174.s:
nārasiṃhaṃ tathā mātsyaṃ kūrmaṃ haṃsaṃ tathaiva ca ..
nṛvarāhaṃ tathā rāmaṃ rāmaṃ ca surasattama .. 19 ..
1.174.d:
नारसिंहं तथा मात्स्यं कूर्मं हंसं तथैव च ॥
नृवराहं तथा रामं रामं च सुरसत्तम ॥ 19 ॥
1.174.m:
the Man-Lion, the Fish, the Tortoise, and likewise the Swan,
the Man-Boar, and Rāma, and Rāma, O best of the gods,

1.174.s:
māndhātāraṃ pṛthuṃ caiva kārtavīryārjunaṃ tathā ..
dhātāraṃ ca tathā mitraṃ cāṃśumaryamaṇaṃ tathā .. 1.190.20 ..
1.174.d:
मान्धातारं पृथुं चैव कार्तवीर्यार्जुनं तथा ॥
धातारं च तथा मित्रं चांशुमर्यमणं तथा ॥ 1.190.20 ॥
1.174.m:
Māndhātṛ, Pṛthu, and Kārtavīryārjuna,
Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aṃśu, and Aryaman,

1.174.s:
pūṣaṇaṃ ca bhavantaṃ ca varuṇaṃ bhagameva ca ..
tvaṣṭāraṃ ca vivasvantaṃ savitāraṃ tathaiva ca .. 21 ..
1.174.d:
पूषणं च भवन्तं च वरुणं भगमेव च ॥
त्वष्टारं च विवस्वन्तं सवितारं तथैव च ॥ 21 ॥
1.174.m:
Pūṣan, yourself, Varuṇa, and Bhaga,
Tvaṣṭṛ, Vivasvat, and Savitṛ,

1.174.s:
viṣṇuṃ candramasaṃ rudraṃ brahmāṇaṃ yamameva ca ..
hutāśanaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ śeṣaṃ nāgeśvaraṃ tathā .. 22 ..
1.174.d:
विष्णुं चन्द्रमसं रुद्रं ब्रह्माणं यममेव च ॥
हुताशनं वैश्रवणं शेषं नागेश्वरं तथा ॥ 22 ॥
1.174.m:
Viṣṇu, the Moon, Rudra, Brahmā, and Yama,
the Fire, Vaiśravaṇa, and Śeṣa the lord of serpents,

1.174.s:
grahamukhyaṃ budhaṃ caiva apaḥ khaṃ pṛthivīṃ tathā ..
vāyustejaśca deveśa tathaivānyāni vāsava .. 23 ..
1.174.d:
ग्रहमुख्यं बुधं चैव अपः खं पृथिवीं तथा ॥
वायुस्तेजश्च देवेश तथैवान्यानि वासव ॥ 23 ॥
1.174.m:
Budha the chief of planets, water, space, and earth,
wind and fire, O lord of gods, and likewise others, O Vāsava.

1.174.s:
prādurbhāvasahasrāṇi tasya dṛṣṭāni yāni te ..
manvantareṣvatīteṣu tasyātītānyanekaśaḥ .. 24 ..
1.174.d:
प्रादुर्भावसहस्राणि तस्य दृष्टानि यानि ते ॥
मन्वन्तरेष्वतीतेषु तस्यातीतान्यनेकशः ॥ 24 ॥
1.174.m:
Those thousands of manifestations of his that were seen by you,
many have passed away in past manvantaras;

1.174.s:
bhaviṣyanti bhaviṣyeṣu śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
manvantaramathāsādya caikamekaṃ tathā tava..25..
1.174.d:
भविष्यन्ति भविष्येषु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
मन्वन्तरमथासाद्य चैकमेकं तथा तव॥25॥
1.174.m:
they will occur by the hundreds and by the thousands in future ones.
And coming to each and every manvantara for you,

1.174.s:
prādurbhāvamidaṃ proktaṃ dviguṇaṃ dviguṇaṃ yataḥ ..
prādurbhāvānyaśeṣeṇa vāsudevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
kaḥ samartho bhavedvaktumiha varṣaśatairapi .. 26 ..
1.174.d:
प्रादुर्भावमिदं प्रोक्तं द्विगुणं द्विगुणं यतः ॥
प्रादुर्भावान्यशेषेण वासुदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
कः समर्थो भवेद्वक्तुमिह वर्षशतैरपि ॥ 26 ॥
1.174.m:
this manifestation is said to double and double again. Wherefore,
who would be able to declare in full the manifestations of Vāsudeva the wielder of the discus,
even in hundreds of years here?

1.174.s:
ekaḥ sa devo bhuvanasya goptā paraḥ purāṇaḥ puruṣo mahātmā ..
tasyāṃśamātraṃ bhuvanaṃ samagraṃ bhāgāstrayastasya na varṇanīyāḥ .. 27 .. ..
1.174.d:
एकः स देवो भुवनस्य गोप्ता परः पुराणः पुरुषो महात्मा ॥
तस्यांशमात्रं भुवनं समग्रं भागास्त्रयस्तस्य न वर्णनीयाः ॥ 27 ॥ ॥
1.174.m: He alone is the god, the protector of the universe, the supreme, ancient Cosmic Person, the Great Soul. / The entire universe is only a fraction of him; three parts of him are beyond description.
